Your search for this particular shout takes you to [[Skyrim:High Hrothgar|High Hrothgar]] and eventually to the leader of the [[Skyrim:Greybeards|Greybeards]], the dragon [[Skyrim:Paarthurnax (dragon)|Paarthurnax]]. He reveals that the [[Lore:Throat of the World|Throat of the World]] was indeed the battleground where the ancient Nords fought Alduin and ended the [[Lore:Dragon War|Dragon War]]. He also reveals that the [[Skyrim:Dragonrend|Dragonrend]] shout was not enough to truly defeat Alduin, in reality merely crippling him. In a final attempt to banish Alduin, the Nords were forced to use an [[Lore:Elder Scroll|Elder Scroll]] to send their foe forward in time, postponing the threat, but not ending it. The event created a rift in time itself atop the mountain, known as the Time-Wound. Paarthurnax believes that, in order to learn the Dragonrend shout, you will have to locate the Elder Scroll, then use it to open the Time-Wound and learn the shout from the ancient Nords that created it. To begin your lengthy quest for the legendary Scroll, you will need to talk to either [[Skyrim:Arngeir|Arngeir]] or [[Skyrim:Esbern|Esbern]]. {{Quest Fork |imageL=SR-npc-Arngeir 02.jpg |imageR=SR-quest-Elder Knowledge 04.jpg |captionL=''"If the world is meant to end, so be it."'' |captionR=''"The whole world was in darkness."'' |titleL=Arngeir's Warning |titleR=Esbern's Dream |textL= If you choose to question Arngeir about obtaining an Elder Scroll, you will find him inside High Hrothgar, where he will be reading, meditating, or sleeping. Arngeir is more skeptical than Esbern about the necessity of learning the Dragonrend shout and, when asked how one would find an Elder Scroll, he will vehemently protest: ''"Such blasphemies are the calling of mages, not followers of the Way. Take your question to the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (faction)|College of Winterhold]]. They may be able to help you."'' When asked if there is another way to defeat Alduin, he will explain his uncertainty: ''"Perhaps not. But this Shout was used once before, was it not? And here we are again. Have you considered that Alduin was not meant to be defeated? Those who overthrew him in ancient times only postponed the day of reckoning, they did not stop it. If the world is meant to end, so be it. Let it end and be reborn."'' |textR= If you choose to visit Esbern, you will find him outside [[Skyrim:Sky Haven Temple|Sky Haven Temple]], where he and [[Skyrim:Delphine|Delphine]] can be seen staring into the horizon as Esbern recalls a strange dream he once had about Alduin. After the story, Esbern will greet you as if he only just realized your presence: ''"Ah, you're back. I hope you've made some progress on tracking down this Shout we need to defeat Alduin?"'' You can then explain that you need an Elder Scroll in order to learn Dragonrend. He will be intrigued: ''"Ah, indeed? There's a pretty puzzle. Not the kind of thing you'll find in your local bookshop. Let me think... Perhaps the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (place)|College of Winterhold]]. What learning there is in Skyrim is gathered there. One of the mages there may be able to put you on the trail of this Elder Scroll."''}} ===An Incomprehensible Book=== [[File:SR-quest-Elder_Knowledge_05.jpg|thumb|right|Urag gro-Shub and his two books on the Elder Scrolls]] Make your way to the College of Winterhold. If you have not joined the College, you will be forced to start the initiation quest, [[Skyrim:First Lessons|First Lessons]], to get past gatekeeper [[Skyrim:Faralda|Faralda]]. If you are already a member, enter the College as normal and follow your map marker to the [[Skyrim:The Arcanaeum|Arcanaeum]]. Here you will find the librarian [[Skyrim:Urag gro-Shub|Urag gro-Shub]]. After belittling you for your ignorance, he will fill you in on the potential dangers of the Scrolls: ''"An Elder Scroll is an instrument of immense knowledge and power. To read an Elder Scroll, a person must have the most rigorously trained mind, or else risk madness. Even so, the Divines usually take the reader's sight as a price."'' He will then elaborate on the incredible nature of the Elder Scrolls: ''"The simplest way to put it is "knowledge," but there's nothing simple about an Elder Scroll. It's a reflection of all possible futures and all possible pasts. Each reader sees different reflections through different lenses, and may come away with a very different reading. But at the same time, all of it is true. Even the falsehoods. Especially the falsehoods."'' You can also ask him who wrote the Elder Scrolls and he will respond: ''"It would take a month to explain to you how that very question doesn't even make sense. The Scrolls exist here, with us, but also beyond and beneath. Before and after. They are bits of Divine made substance so we could know them. Some people who study them devoutly go mad."'' Naturally, Urag does not have a Scroll lying around, and he wouldn't simply give it to you if he had. After a short discussion, Urag leaves his spot behind the counter and fetches two rare books for you, ''[[Skyrim:Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls|Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls]]'' and ''[[Skyrim:Effects of the Elder Scrolls|Effects of the Elder Scrolls]]''. The first book is written by [[Skyrim:Septimus Signus|Septimus Signus]] and starts the concurrent quest [[Skyrim:Discerning the Transmundane|Discerning the Transmundane]] when opened. When you tell Urag that Signus's book is incomprehensible, he will explain that Septimus Signus is a specialist in Elder Scrolls lore, but he has not been back to the College for a long time. He mentions that Signus became obsessed with the [[Lore:Dwemer|Dwemer]] and took off north to study an old artifact. ===Beyond the Physical World=== [[File:SR-npc-Septimus Signus 02.jpg|thumb|right|Septimus Signus and the Dwemer lockbox]] From this point, the quest Discerning the Transmundane will be part of your quest to claim the Elder Scroll. Follow your map marker to a remote ice cavern named [[Skyrim:Septimus Signus's Outpost|Septimus Signus's Outpost]] and enter. Inside you will find Septimus Signus pacing before a huge device with a strange-looking lock, muttering to himself about the Dwemer. When questioned on the Elder Scrolls, his answer will be just as incomprehensible as his book: ''"Elder Scrolls. Indeed. The Empire. They absconded with them. Or so they think. The ones they saw. The ones they thought they saw. I know of one. Forgotten. Sequestered. But I cannot go to it, not poor Septimus, for I... I have arisen beyond its grasp."'' When you inquire as to the location of the Scroll, he will respond: ''"Here. Well, here as in this plane. Mundus. Tamriel. Nearby, relatively speaking. On the cosmological scale, it's all nearby."'' He will then agree to help you, but only if you help him, naturally. He'll point towards the Dwemer lockbox in the icy cavern and say: ''"You see this masterwork of the Dwemer. Deep inside their greatest knowings. Septimus is clever among men, but he is but an idiot child compared to the dullest of the Dwemer. Lucky then they left behind their own way of reading the Elder Scrolls. In the depths of [[Skyrim:Blackreach|Blackreach]] one yet lies."'' He will explain what Blackreach is and what you must go through: ''"Under deep. Below the dark. The hidden keep. [[Skyrim:Tower_of_Mzark|Tower Mzark]]. [[Skyrim:Alftand|Alftand]]. The point of puncture, of first entry, of the tapping. Delve to its limits, and Blackreach lies just beyond. But not all can enter there. Only Septimus knows the hidden key to loose the lock to jump beneath the deathly rock."'' While it is clear that Septimus doesn't care about the Elder Scroll itself, it is quite clear that he needs the information it possesses. You will have no choice but to help him. He will hand you two items, the [[Skyrim:Blank Lexicon|Blank Lexicon]] and the [[Skyrim:Attunement Sphere|Attunement Sphere]]. A knowledgeable person indeed, he will then provide his complex explanation on what to do with the items, including a tip that will prove valuable [[#The Elder Scroll|later]]. He will also provide his knowledge on what defines an Elder Scroll: ''"You look to your left, you see one way. You look to your right, you see another. But neither is any harder than the opposite. But the Elder Scrolls... they look left and right in the stream of time. The future and past are as one. Sometimes they even look up. What do they see then? What if they dive in? Then the madness begins."'' {{NewLine}} {{SkyrimBox|main-color=#FBEFD5|text-color=black|text= [[File:SR-icon-misc-AttunementSphere.png|left|50px]] '''NOTE''': While the map marker will point you towards Alftand, you can gain access to Blackreach from two other [[Skyrim:Dwarven_Ruins|ruins]], specifically [[Skyrim:Mzinchaleft|Mzinchaleft]] and [[Skyrim:Raldbthar|Raldbthar]]. However, if you have yet to clear either of those, the route through Alftand is recommended as your map marker will point you in the right direction. }} ===Alftand=== [[File:SR-place-Alftand_09.jpg|thumb|right|[[Skyrim:Alftand|Alftand]]]] The Dwemer ruin of [[Skyrim:Alftand|Alftand]] is located southwest of [[Skyrim:Winterhold|Winterhold]]. The exterior area contains a deserted camp, but upon investigating the ruined shack near the campsite, you will find an ''[[Skyrim:Expedition Manifest|Expedition Manifest]]'' written by expedition leader [[Skyrim:Sulla_Trebatius|Sulla Trebatius]], hinting that you may not be alone when traversing Alftand. From the shack, head down the slope and enter the first zone, [[Skyrim:Alftand Glacial Ruins|Alftand Glacial Ruins]]. ====The Lost Expedition==== The icy tunnel ahead contains no enemies but plenty of destroyed cooking spits, and before long you will see blood spatters all over the floor. A little further down the tunnel, you will hear the voice of one of the [[Skyrim:Khajiit|Khajiit]] members of the expedition in a [[Skyrim:Skooma|Skooma]]-induced rant, demanding that his companion tell him where the rest of the Skooma is hidden. Head east through the tunnel and follow the path as it twists and turns. You will soon arrive in a room with a table and [[Skyrim:Calcelmo|Calcelmo]]'s book ''[[Skyrim:Dwarves,_v2|Dwarves, v2]]'' along with some ''[[Skyrim:Research Notes|Research Notes]]'' from Sulla Trebatius. The door to the north is barred, so take the western path and fight the dwarven automatons that guard it. As the tunnel becomes icy again, you will encounter [[Skyrim:J'darr|J'darr]], mad from Skooma withdrawal, who will attack you on sight. In the corner, you will find the corpse of his brother [[Skyrim:J'zhar|J'zhar]], lying in a pool of his own blood. Leave the bodies behind and head north until you reach a chamber with two [[Skyrim:Dwarven Sphere|dwarven spheres]]. Proceed forward. To the left, there are a set of rising and falling platforms. If you manage to get onto the tallest of the three, there will be two unlocked chests, with several potions and a jewel on a nearby surface. Then proceed through the only available path, where you will find a [[Skyrim:Forge|forge]] and more [[Skyrim:Dwarven Spider|dwarven spiders]]. In this room, you can find ''[[Skyrim:Umana's Journal|Umana's Journal]]'', which describes how the dangers of Alftand have claimed even more victims. Before you open the western door, there will be a novice-locked gate containing two locked chests (adept and apprentice) and various small dwemer items. After opening the western door, beware of the [[Skyrim:Pressure Plate|dwarven pressure plate]] in front of the chest at the top of the stairs. To the right will be another [[Skyrim:Dwarven Spider|dwarven spider]], easy to either kill or sneak past, and an adept-locked chest. From there, head south, where another spider will be waiting. Directly past it, on your left, will be a room containing a potion of minor stamina and a potion of either vigorous or extreme healing. Even further ahead on the right is an apprentice-locked door. Inside is a dwarven sphere, an unlocked chest, two beds, and various other dwarven items. Past this the hallway splits into two: on the left, a long ledge featuring [[Skyrim:Dwarven Spider|dwarven spider workers]] and pipes that could easily push you off; to the right, a solitary spider focused on attacking the wall, and a [[Skyrim:Blacksmith's Potion|Blacksmith's Potion]]. Climb across to the end of the ledge and proceed to the [[Skyrim:Alftand Animonculory|Alftand Animonculory]]. ====The Eyeless Creatures==== The Animonculory door opens up into another hallway. Turn left past the first gear in the wall to find an unlocked chest, a [[Skyrim:Falmer Helmet|Falmer helmet]] and [[Skyrim:Falmer Shield|shield]], a hint as to your future enemies, and assorted dwemer items. Open the door at the far end and enter the enormous chamber beyond. To your right will be a distracted Dwarven Spider Worker; if you enter the small pathway next to the stairs, you will find yet another deceased expedition member, [[Skyrim:Endrast|Endrast]], who is still holding his [[Skyrim:Endrast's Journal|journal]]. On top of the journal are a lockpick and stick of charcoal, and opposite the body is an adept-locked chest. Retrace your steps, climb the stairs and find the slope to the east, where a Dwarven Sphere is patrolling. There are three pressure plates here that trigger a deadly set of [[Skyrim:Spinning Blades|spinning blades]]. Dodge these and proceed to the level. [[File:SR-interior-Alftand_06.jpg|thumb|right|The central chamber of the [[Skyrim:Alftand Animonculory|Animonculory]]]] This room is the first very large, multi-leveled chamber in Alftand. You are on the top level, so start making your way down the slopes and fight the enemies as you go. The area near the beginning, as you step down the first ramp, contains a Dwarven Spider, a potion of extreme magicka, and a novice-locked chest. When you have traversed one floor, an apprentice-locked door to the east leads to some worthwhile treasure. Inside is another [[Skyrim:Dwarven Spider|Dwarven Spider Worker]], two other gates (One unlocked and open, with an unlocked chest imside; the other with an expert lock. Inside are two chests, one unlocked, one master-locked, two potions, a [[Skyrim:Dwarven Helmet|Dwarven Helmet]], a skeleton, and a [[Skyrim:The Locked Room|book]].)You'll need to make a short jump down to proceed, where you will land near the body of [[Skyrim:Yag_gra-Gortwog|Yag gra-Gortwog]]. To the southeast is another slope leading down, where you will find the first [[Skyrim:Falmer|Falmer]] enemy. Stay on the path and kill any Falmer that get in your way. You will reach a platform with a door and a broken pipe spitting out fire. Open the door to leave the huge chamber for now and proceed forward towards an [[Skyrim:Alchemy Lab|alchemy lab]] and several Falmer emerging from their tents. Dodge the flames coming from the pipes and head south until you reach a junction. The stairs to the east lead to a small room with some ingredients, while the path south will lead you to the next room. In this room, the elevator on the other side of the barred doorway leads back to the previous zone, Alftand Glacial Ruins, so at this point it is possible to return to the outside world and stock up on supplies. Otherwise, skip the elevator ride and locate Sulla Trebatius's Pack. You will also find a table holding the dead body of [[Skyrim:Valie|Valie]] and another with an array of rare ingredients, including a [[Skyrim:Small Pearl|small pearl]], one of only two samples in Skyrim. Find the path to the northeast and open the door. You will find yourself back in the huge central chamber, where you can continue your descent. There are three Falmer and a [[Skyrim:Frostbite Spider|frostbite spider]] at the bottom of the chamber; dispose of them and locate the door to the north and enter. The next area contains a [[Skyrim:Tripwire|tripwire]], which triggers a [[Skyrim:Claw|claw trap]]. Avoid the tripwire and the trap and continue into [[Skyrim:Alftand Cathedral|Alftand Cathedral]]. ====The Dwemer Mechanism==== [[File:SR-interior-Alftand_13.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Skyrim:Alftand Cathedral|Cathedral]]]] Alftand Cathedral is the last zone of Alftand, and the smallest as well. Upon entering, take a right turn and dodge the three [[Skyrim:Pressure Plate|pressure plates]], all of which will trigger a [[Skyrim:Slicer|slicer]] from the ceiling. Fight a single Falmer enemy and open the door to another huge chamber, where you will find more Falmer. Dispose of them, take a moment to explore the room for lots of chests and loot, then head up the stairs next to the entrance and pull the lever. This lowers the spikes blocking the gate to the west, but approach the area carefully as you will awaken a [[Skyrim:Dwarven Centurion|dwarven centurion]]. After the battle, loot the centurion for the [[Skyrim:Key to Alftand Lift|Key to Alftand Lift]] and head up the stairs. Open the gate where you will witness the last two survivors of the failed expedition, [[Skyrim:Sulla_Trebatius|Sulla Trebatius]] and [[Skyrim:Umana|Umana]], having a conversation revealing Sulla's true intentions: '''Umana''': ''"Sulla look, the passage is open, wait... there's someone down there!"''
'''Sulla''': ''"No! Blackreach was to be my discovery!"''
'''Umana''': ''"Sulla, let's just get out of here. Hasn't there been enough death?"''
'''Sulla''': ''"Oh, of course you want me to leave. Just waiting for me to turn my back. So you can have all the glory for yourself!"'' Sulla and Umana will then proceed to fight each other; keep your distance until one is victorious (usually Umana). The other will then turn against you. Dispose of them and investigate Umana's body for the unique shield [[Skyrim:Targe of the Blooded|Targe of the Blooded]]. Turn your attention towards the Dwarven Mechanism in the center of the room. Activate it, and the Attunement Sphere will do the rest, revealing a staircase leading downward. You can return to the outside world from here by using your newly acquired [[Skyrim:Key to Alftand Lift|key]] on the gate to the southwest. This will also provide a useful shortcut for later visits (make sure to open the gate at the top of the elevator). From here, head down the stairs and prepare yourself for [[Skyrim:Blackreach|Blackreach]]. ===Blackreach=== [[File:SR-place-Blackreach.jpg|thumb|right|Blackreach]] [[File:SR-quest-Elder_Knowledge_07.jpg|thumb|right|The Tower of Mzark]] Finally, you will be in Blackreach, a vast, beautiful, eerie, and dangerous underground cavern that will take time to traverse completely. Dwarven automatons and Falmer continue to be common enemies, and you may encounter [[Skyrim:Chaurus|chaurus]] and [[Skyrim:Giant|giants]] as well. Blackreach can be overwhelming and quite difficult to navigate, especially since your in-game map will only ever allow you to see a portion of the cavern. Additionally, it is loaded with distractions, so stay on the path for now and keep your eye on the prize: the Elder Scroll. The fastest route from Alftand to the Tower of Mzark is the road to the left, immediately out of the Alftand Cathedral. Continue along the road in a southeastern direction and fight a dwarven sphere and a Falmer. When you come to the first junction, make a right and head southwest along that road and fight more chaurus and another Falmer. As you travel underneath a bridge, a Falmer will shoot arrows at you from above, but just move forward and stay on the path. Fight two chaurus and continue on until the path turns in a western direction, across a bridge. When you cross the bridge, the Tower of Mzark will be visible to the southwest, and the trail will lead you right to the entrance. ===The Elder Scroll=== [[File:SR-quest-Elder_Knowledge.jpg|thumb|right|The Elder Scroll recovered]] Once you have entered the Tower of Mzark, investigate the first room for some minor loot. The [[Skyrim:Smithing|Smithing]] [[Skyrim:Skill Books|skill book]] ''[[Skyrim:The Armorer's Challenge|The Armorer's Challenge]]'' is located in the west facing corner of the room (to the right of the doorway on the far wall). Proceed through the door and behold a Dwemer contraption that would make even Septimus Signus proud: a giant sphere with various lenses fills the entire first floor of the room. The second floor sits on the upper part of the sphere and, hanging from the ceiling, a series of lenses conceal a container. If you investigate the surrounding area, you will find the skeletal remains of [[Skyrim:Drokt|Drokt]]. His [[Skyrim:Journal of Drokt|journal]] will inform you how he became obsessed with the Oculory, and he seemingly died without managing to align it correctly. The journal also contains a tip on how to solve the puzzle: ''"The light through the knowledge through the machine rests on the cube."'' This echoes the words of Septimus Signus: ''"The Dwemer found a loophole, as they always do. To focus the knowledge away and inside without harm. Place the lexicon into their contraption and focus the knowings into it."'' With these two tips in mind, head up the last slope, where you will find four buttons and a Lexicon Receptacle. Place the Blank Lexicon in the receptacle and watch the ceiling of the room open, shining light onto the container beneath. This also activates the two buttons on the right. To focus the lenses on the floor, place yourself so you can see the Lexicon and the central floor. Activate the button on the second pedestal from the right four times in a row and the Lexicon will open. This also activates one of the buttons to the left. Press the second button from the left twice and the lenses in the ceiling will change position, allowing the light shining through the container to hit the corresponding lenses on the floor, thus filling the Lexicon with knowledge. The last button to the left will now be active, so push it once and the upper lenses will move aside, making room for the container to be lowered down from the ceiling. Once it has reached the floor, it will open and reveal the legendary Elder Scroll (Dragon), the very source of the elder knowledge, yours for the taking. Remember to pick up the inscribed [[Skyrim:Runed Lexicon|Runed Lexicon]] from the receptacle, then claim the Elder Scroll. This ends the quest and starts the next one, [[Skyrim:Alduin's Bane|Alduin's Bane]]. ===Achievements=== One [[Skyrim:Achievements|achievement]] is unlocked when you complete this quest: * {{achievement|Elder Knowledge (achievement)|descr=no}} ==Notes== *Attempting to read the Elder Scroll will inflict temporary blindness upon you. *Having the [[Skyrim:Clairvoyance_(spell)|Clairvoyance]] spell can be very helpful for navigating Blackreach. *If you have already spoken to Urag gro-Shub, you will have an option to tell Paarthurnax that the "Lorekeeper" of the College of Winterhold can point you in the direction of the Scroll. *If you have already obtained the Elder Scroll during Discerning the Transmundane, or if you have already completed the ''Dawnguard'' questline, as soon as The Throat of the World is completed, this quest will be automatically completed as well and Alduin's Bane will begin. Either way, this will skip some of Paarthurnax's optional dialogue. *If you have the ''Dawnguard'' add-on installed, the Elder Scroll will now appear as "Elder Scroll (Dragon)" in your inventory. ==Bugs== {{Bug|This quest occasionally conflicts with the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (faction)|College of Winterhold]] quest line. Urag gro-Shub will sometimes lack the dialogue options required to continue Elder Knowledge. At other times he may not even talk to you, or not place all the books on the desk.|confirmed=1}} **This can be resolved by either going directly to Septimus Signus and speaking with him, or by finishing the College of Winterhold quests. **{{pc22}} Alternatively, PC users can use the console to progress by advancing to stage 80 (setstage MQ205 80). {{Bug|If you leave the Tower of Mzark without collecting the Elder Scroll and complete [[Skyrim:Discerning the Transmundane|Discerning the Transmundane]], collecting the scroll later will have no effect and this quest will be blocked.|confirmed=1|modnotes=Once Discerning the Transmundane is complete, the reference to "ElderScroll" in DA04ElderScrollActivatorScript is no longer valid, breaking the script.}} **If this happens, the Scroll will not appear in your inventory after collection. **{{pc22}} This can be resolved by collecting the Scroll and then spawning it in your inventory with player.additem 2d513 1. You should be able to read the Scroll after using this console code. {{Bug|The optional quest objective to talk to Esbern may not be listed in your journal.|USKP|1.3.1}} {{Bug|You may not be able to start this quest if you have removed the Elder Scroll from your inventory before meeting Paarthurnax.}} **{{pc22}} This can be resolved by using setstage MQ206 10 to start Alduin's Bane. {{Bug|If you don't take the Elder Scroll during [[Skyrim:Discerning the Transmundane|Discerning the Transmundane]] and eventually go on to end that quest without doing so, it becomes impossible to take the scroll later due to the activator being set for an alias in said quest.|USSEP|4.1.4|The activator is instead set to use the alias in this quest to get the scroll since Elder Knowledge is a background quest that is never terminated during the life of the game.}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |10||I met the master of the Greybeards, the dragon Paarthurnax. ==Radiant Options==
This is a radiant quest which you can receive from either [[Skyrim:Skald|Skald]] or [[Skyrim:Brina Merilis|Brina Merilis]], whichever is the [[Skyrim:Jarl|Jarl]] of the Pale. The Jarl lives in [[Skyrim:The White Hall|The White Hall]] in [[Skyrim:Dawnstar|Dawnstar]].

==Quick Walkthrough==
# Befriend the [[Skyrim:Jarl|Jarl]] of [[Skyrim:The_Pale|the Pale]].
# Assist three people of the Pale.
# Return to the jarl for your reward.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become [[Skyrim:Thane|Thane]] of [[Skyrim:The_Pale|the Pale]]. In order to receive this quest you must first aid the current [[Skyrim:Jarl|Jarl]]. If [[Skyrim:Skald|Skald]] is Jarl of the Pale, then normally, you must first complete [[Skyrim:Waking Nightmare|Waking Nightmare]] and then [[Skyrim:Kill the Giant (Jarl)|Kill the Giant]] in order to befriend him. If Skald was ousted from [[Skyrim:Dawnstar|Dawnstar]] during [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]], and then reinstated after [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Dunstad (Stormcloaks)|The Battle for Fort Dunstad]], that will also befriend him. If [[Skyrim:Brina_Merilis|Brina]] is Jarl of the Pale (whether she was installed via [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Dunstad (Imperial)|The Battle for Fort Dunstad]] or [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]]), then she is automatically friendly to you.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and he or she will ask you to [[Skyrim:Making Friends and Influencing People|assist the people of the hold]]. In order to assist the people of the hold, you must befriend three people who are citizens of the Pale. Usually you do this by completing [[Skyrim:Favors|favor quests]] on their behalf. All of the favor quests in the Pale are for people in Dawnstar, except for Aeri, who lives at [[Skyrim:Anga's Mill|Anga's Mill]]. Note that you can also befriend merchants if you have the [[Skyrim:Investor|Investor]] perk by investing in their stores.

=== The Pale Favor Quests ===

Highlighted quests can be easily completed without any skill use. If any citizen offers multiple favor quests, only the first completed one will count towards Thaneship.

==Radiant Options==
This is a radiant quest which you can receive from either [[Skyrim:Idgrod Ravencrone|Idgrod Ravencrone]] or [[Skyrim:Sorli the Builder|Sorli the Builder]], whichever is the Jarl of Hjaalmarch. The jarl lives in [[Skyrim:Highmoon Hall|Highmoon Hall]] in [[Skyrim:Morthal|Morthal]]. You must assist three people.

==Quick Walkthrough==
# Befriend the Jarl of Hjaalmarch.
# Assist three people of Hjaalmarch.
# Return to the jarl for your reward.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
This is an umbrella quest for several other quests which must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Hjaalmarch. In order to receive this quest, you must first aid the current jarl. You must usually complete [[Skyrim:Laid to Rest|Laid to Rest]] first if the jarl is Idgrod; however, you can begin the quest if she was ousted from Morthal during [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]] and reinstated following [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Snowhawk (Imperial)|The Battle for Fort Snowhawk]]. You can also begin the quest if the jarl is Sorli, whether she was installed via [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]] or [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Snowhawk (Stormcloaks)|The Battle for Fort Snowhawk]].

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and she will ask you to [[Skyrim:Making Friends and Influencing People|assist the people of the hold]]. You must assist three people in the hold, usually by completing [[Skyrim:Favors|favor quests]] for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests . If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the [[Skyrim:Investor|Investor]] perk by investing in their stores.

==Radiant Options==
This is a radiant quest which you can receive from either [[Skyrim:Brunwulf Free-Winter|Brunwulf Free-Winter]] or [[Skyrim:Ulfric Stormcloak|Ulfric Stormcloak]], whichever is the jarl of Eastmarch. The jarl lives in the [[Skyrim:Palace of the Kings|Palace of the Kings]] in [[Skyrim:Windhelm|Windhelm]].

==Quick Walkthrough==
# Befriend the Jarl of Eastmarch by progressing through the [[Skyrim:Civil War|civil war]] questline and complete quest [[Skyrim:Blood on the Ice|Blood on the Ice]].
# Assist five people of Eastmarch.
# Purchase [[Skyrim:Hjerim|Hjerim]].
# Return to the jarl for your reward.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
This is an umbrella quest, involving several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of Eastmarch. You will have to capture [[Skyrim:Rescue from Fort Neugrad|Falkreath]] for the Stormcloaks and complete quest [[Skyrim:Blood on the Ice|Blood on the Ice]] (if you joined the Stormcloaks) or complete the [[Skyrim:Battle for Windhelm|Battle for Windhelm]] (if you sided with the Imperials) before this quest becomes available. Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the jarl again and he will ask you to [[Skyrim:Making Friends and Influencing People|assist the people of the hold]]. You must assist five people in the hold, usually by completing [[Skyrim:Favors|favor quests]] for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. Also, you can befriend merchants if you have the [[Skyrim:Investor|Investor]] perk by investing in their stores.

You must also purchase [[Skyrim:Hjerim|Hjerim]], which costs 8,000 to 12,000 gold. Simply purchasing it is enough; there is no requirement to decorate, although it becomes more useful if decorated. Note that it cannot be decorated unless you have completed [[Skyrim:Blood on the Ice|Blood on the Ice]], and if you have not started that quest yet you should start it before entering Hjerim.

==Radiant Options==
This is a radiant quest which you can receive from [[Skyrim:Igmund|Igmund]] or [[Skyrim:Thongvor Silver-Blood|Thongvor Silver-Blood]], whichever is Jarl of the Reach. The jarl lives in [[Skyrim:Understone Keep|Understone Keep]] in [[Skyrim:Markarth|Markarth]]. The jarl can be found in multiple places - arguing with [[Skyrim:Calcelmo|Calcelmo]], roaming the halls, sleeping in his bedroom or sitting on the throne.

==Quick Walkthrough==
# Befriend the Jarl of the Reach.
# Assist five people of the Reach.
# Purchase [[Skyrim:Vlindrel Hall|Vlindrel Hall]].
# Return to the jarl for your reward.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
This is an umbrella quest for several other quests that must be completed if you wish to become Thane of the Reach. The Jarl requires you buy the house in town as well as performing five favors for the townsfolk. Once this is achieved you can become Thane.

In order to receive this quest you must first aid the current Jarl. If the Jarl is Igmund, then you must usually [[Skyrim:Kill the Forsworn Leader (Jarl)|kill a Forsworn leader]] and [[Skyrim:Dungeon Delving (Jarl - Hagravens)|Find Hrolfdir's Shield]]; however, if he was ousted from [[Skyrim:Markarth|Markarth]] during [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]] and reinstated following [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Sungard (Imperial)|The Battle for Fort Sungard]], that is sufficient to begin this quest. If the Jarl is Thongvor, whether he was installed via [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]] or [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Sungard (Stormcloaks)|The Battle for Fort Sungard]], then the completion of that quest is sufficient to fulfill the prerequisite.

Once you have completed the prerequisite, speak with the Jarl again and he will ask you to [[Skyrim:Making Friends and Influencing People|assist the people of the hold]]. You must assist five people in the hold, usually by completing [[Skyrim:Favors|favor quests]] for them. Note that many of the quest givers are non-essential NPCs, so their deaths would result in a loss of potential quests to complete. If they die after you assist them, they still count towards your Thane status. You can also befriend merchants if you have the [[Skyrim:Investor|Investor]] perk by investing in their stores.

Note that there are several favor quests involving members of Orc strongholds in the Reach; assisting Orcs living in strongholds does not count towards your Thane quest, but Orcs in Markarth do count.

You may consider completing [[Skyrim:The Heart of Dibella|The Heart of Dibella]] as successfully completing it befriends all four of the priestesses of Dibella, which is almost enough to qualify for thaneship alone. It also requires you to visit [[Skyrim:Karthwasten|Karthwasten]]; resolving the [[Skyrim:Sanuarach Mine (quest)|Sanuarach mine dispute]] there (for either side) will be enough to complete this requirement.

You must also purchase [[Skyrim:Vlindrel Hall|Vlindrel Hall]], which costs 8,000 gold. Simply purchasing it is enough, there is no requirement to decorate, although it becomes more useful if decorated.

===Reward===
After helping five inhabitants and purchasing [[Skyrim:Vlindrel Hall|Vlindrel Hall]], the journal tells you to return to the Jarl. The reward, the [[Skyrim:Blade of the Reach|Blade of the Reach]], is a random, leveled, enchanted axe. There is a 50% chance that it will be a war axe (one-handed), and a 50% chance it will be a battleaxe (two-handed). You will also receive a housecarl named [[Skyrim:Argis the Bulwark|Argis the Bulwark]], who will be waiting for you at Vlindrel Hall.

=1 ([[Skyrim:Viola Giordano|Viola Giordano]]) }} ==Quick Walkthrough== #Speak to [[Skyrim:Revyn Sadri|Revyn Sadri]] to begin the quest and obtain [[Skyrim:Viola's Gold Ring|Viola's Gold Ring]]. #Choose whether to: #* Break into [[Skyrim:Viola Giordano's House|Viola Giordano's House]] and return the ring, ''or'' #* Tell [[Skyrim:Viola Giordano|Viola Giordano]] about the ring. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===The Accidental Fence=== [[Skyrim:Revyn Sadri|Revyn Sadri]] runs a pawnshop, [[Skyrim:Sadri's Used Wares|Sadri's Used Wares]], in [[Skyrim:Windhelm|Windhelm]]'s Gray Quarter. Revyn tends to tell visitors to his store, somewhat overemphatically, that, "''All my goods are legitimate, which is more than I can say for some''". If you question him on it, he will change his story and confess that he bought a [[Skyrim:Viola's Gold Ring|ring]] before realizing that it matched the description of an item recently stolen from [[Skyrim:Viola Giordano|Viola Giordano]]. Even if you offer to return the ring for Revyn, he is still worried. He insists that Viola can't be told, because she would surely report the crime to the [[Skyrim:Jarl|Jarl]]. Instead, he wants you to sneak into [[Skyrim:Viola Giordano's House|Viola Giordano's House]] and leave the ring. Your quest log at this point suggests that you only have one option for how to proceed, namely to [[#Option 1: Return the Ring|return the ring]]. However, Revyn's dialogue hints at a second option: you can [[#Option 2: Tell Viola|tell Viola]] about the stolen ring. ===Option 1: Return the Ring=== To return the ring, the first step is gaining entrance to Viola's house. Her house is a large manor located in the Valunstrad district, on the west side of town. The front door is locked with a difficult leveled lock (Expert or Master level). Alternatively, you can opt to pickpocket the [[Skyrim:Viola Giordano's House Key|key]] from Viola. Once you enter the house, the dresser where you are expected to place the ring is located immediately to the right of the front door. Open the dresser, and select that you want to "Store" the ring in the dresser. This will trigger a quest update. Return to Revyn to obtain your reward, a medium leveled amount of gold. In addition, Revyn's disposition towards you will increase. The most immediate implication is that you will be able to freely take all low-cost items in the store and sleep in his bed for free. You will also be able to buy training in Speech to level 50. He is the only Speech trainer that you can trade with (which you can do to get the gold back) without joining the [[Skyrim:Volkihar Vampire Clan|Volkihar vampires]]{{DG}}. ===Option 2: Tell Viola=== The other option requires you to find Viola. She is frequently found walking the streets of Windhelm, or else at [[Skyrim:Candlehearth Hall|Candlehearth Hall]] in the evenings. If you talk to her, you will have the option to tell Viola about the ring. She takes the ring but seems more interested in finding ways to punish Revyn than actually being happy to have the ring back. In particular, she promises to report this to the Jarl and get Revyn's taxes doubled or even tripled. She will also reward you with a medium leveled amount of gold. Her disposition towards you will increase, one implication being that you can freely take all low-cost items in her house. This is also the only way to be able to marry her. On the other hand, Revyn's disposition will decrease. This will result in negative comments every time you enter his store, but he will still trade with you (and his other dialogue will be as friendly as otherwise). ===Reward=== {{SRLeveledReward|Medium|float=left}} {{NewLeft}} ==Notes== *Because this is a favor quest which positively affects either Revyn or Viola's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the [[Skyrim:Thane of Eastmarch|Thane of Eastmarch]] quest. *After returning the ring in the drawer and getting the quest update, you can remove the ring and tell Revyn that you returned it. The quest will complete and you will still have Viola's ring, which is no longer flagged as a quest item. ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |10||{{Quest Objective|10|Plant Viola's Gold Ring in Viola Giordano's House}} |15||{{Quest Objective|15|Tell Revyn Viola's Gold Ring has been planted}} |20|fin| |missing=0, 17, 200 }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}}

==Quick Walkthrough==

==Detailed Walkthrough==
Speak to [[Skyrim:Sybille_Stentor|Sybille Stentor]] in the [[Skyrim:Blue Palace|Blue Palace]] throne room and ask what her problem is. She will tell you about a local nest of [[Skyrim:Vampire|vampires]] which you should wipe out.
[[File:SR-quest-Kill_the_Vampire_02.jpg|thumb|right|The first area of Pinemoon Cave]]
Make your way to [[Skyrim:Pinemoon Cave|Pinemoon Cave]], west of Solitude. It is a very small cave with only four chambers, and an assortment of vampires and wolves. You only need to kill the Master Vampire to complete the quest. He can be found in the third chamber, a large room with pews facing an altar. The Master Vampire can be found on the altar area. However, he has two companions who will also attack if you are detected. They will reanimate a corpse of a [[Skyrim:Nord (dead)|Nord]] which lies on a table in the southern part of the chamber.
[[File:SR-quest-Kill_the_Vampire_03.jpg|thumb|left|Vampires attacking]]
If you do clear out the cave, there is a locked chest next to the altar. Also do not forget the fourth chamber, the sleeping quarters, which contains the [[Skyrim:Illusion|Illusion]] [[Skyrim:Skill Books|skill book]] ''[[Skyrim:Incident_at_Necrom|Incident at Necrom]]'' and another chest.

===Reward===
Exit the way you came in and return to Sybille Stentor for your reward, which is [[Skyrim:Jewelry|jewelry]] and a single free skill boost in Illusion.

# Speak to [[Skyrim:Igmund|Igmund]].

==Detailed Walkthrough==
When you ask Igmund if he has more work for you, he will mention how his father was killed by [[SR:Forsworn|Forsworn]] when he tried to negotiate with them. He will then ask you to retrieve his father's shield, which is being guarded by a [[Skyrim:Hagraven|hagraven]].

Note that [[Skyrim:Bleakwind Bluff|Bleakwind Bluff]] is by far the easiest location from which to retrieve the shield, as it is a small tower with no interior zones and is only inhabited by a few Forsworn and a hagraven. So if you don't feel like doing an extensive dungeon delve, it is expedient to reload until you get that radiant location. Unlike the previous favor, you don't need to kill anyone, so a stealthy character can easily grab the shield and get out without having to fight.

===Reward===
As a reward, you will get a leveled piece of armor, which is either a light/heavy cuirass, helmet, or shield of the best quality for your level. In addition, you'll be able to purchase [[Skyrim:Vlindrel Hall|Vlindrel Hall]] from [[Skyrim:Raerek|Raerek]]. After completing the quest, the shield can be found in the Jarl's private quarters.

Having that might get the ear of the other Holds and give me some authority."'' Once you've agreed to find it, head to the location marked on your map, and head to the boss chest, where you will find the helm. The location will be randomly selected from the following: {{LinkList|Driftshade Refuge|Fort Fellhammer|Hela's Folly|Hob's Fall Cave|Ironbind Barrow|Pride of Tel Vos|Saarthal|Snow Veil Sanctum|Yngol Barrow|Yngvild}}. It will no longer be a quest item, but appears to retain its Stolen status even if sold to a Thieves Guild fence and repurchased (at least, this was the case with Mallus Maccius in Skyrim Special Edition). *Unlike many "named" objects, there is nothing much special about the Helm of Winterhold. ==Detailed Walkthrough==
It is a standard fetch-and-return quest. The item will be found in the boss chest in the target dungeon, and is treated as a [[Skyrim:Quest Items|quest item]].

=== Amren's Family Sword ===
When you encounter Amren, he may be arguing with his wife [[Skyrim:Saffir|Saffir]]. If asked about the argument, Amren will tell you about his father's sword:
:''My Saffir doesn't like that I've been spending so much time looking for my father's old sword. He fed his entire family with the gold he made using that weapon. I'm not about to let it gather dust in some thief's trophy room.''
Volunteering to retrieve the sword for him triggers the start of the quest.
{{Quest Item|Amren's Family Sword}}
When you return the sword, Amren gives you a one point bonus in both [[Skyrim:Block|Block]] and [[Skyrim:One-handed|One-handed]], commenting, "''Here, my father had a favorite sword and shield technique. Let me teach it to you, in honor of his memory.''"

=== Shahvee's Amulet of Zenithar ===
If you talk to Shahvee you may have the option to ask her, "Your people have bad luck?" In response she will tell you:
:''We have not {{sic|faired|fared}} well outside our native [[Lore:Black Marsh|Black Marsh]], but we're determined to make the best of things. I began praying to [[Lore:Zenithar|Zenithar]], the god of wealth, to bring us some fortune, but thieves made off with my sacred amulet almost as soon as I bought it.''
Volunteering to retrieve the amulet triggers the start of the quest.
{{Quest Item|Shahvee's Amulet}}
When you return the amulet, Shahvee gives you a one point bonus in both [[Skyrim:Light Armor|Light Armor]] and [[Skyrim:Lockpicking|Lockpicking]], commenting, "''Before I came into Zenithar's calling, I confess I was a thief. But I learned a few things in my time that might help you survive. Let me show you.''"

==Notes==
* Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the [[Skyrim:Thane|thane]] quest for the quest giver's hold.
* It is impossible to do both quests at the same time, e.g., if you do the quest for Amren, you are unable to do it for Shahvee until you have completed the quest for Amren.
* Shahvee's Amulet can spawn in Uttering Hills Camp, a location that also has a chance for Annekke Crag-Jumper or Brunwulf Free-Winter's personal quests. If they do, none of these quests can be taken at the same time. Waiting 30 days outside their map cells will allow one of the other quests to be taken.

If you have this uncompleted radiant miscellaneous quest in your quest log, then you will not be able to see the dialogue option to receive Amren's quest when talking to him.|confirmed=1}}

==Notes==
* Once you've turned in these quests, the items you were meant to retrieve can then be either pickpocketed from the quest-giver, looted off their corpse, or purchased from them if they are a merchant. The most valuable item to take is the Ring of Pure Mixtures, which is one of only two guaranteed [[Skyrim:Fortify Alchemy|Fortify Alchemy]] enchantments in the game that can be disenchanted (and the only one that does not require you to join a faction or complete an optional leg of a particular quest). It can be purchased from Frida once you deliver it, but only with the Merchant perk.  
*If you make Roggi Knot-Beard a follower, you may be able to take the shield from his inventory.
* Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. You must clear the radiant quest from your miscellaneous quests in order to be eligible to receive another of the same type.
* Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the [[Skyrim:Thane|thane]] quest for the quest giver's hold.
* Frida and Oengul will only have the relevant dialogue options during their business hours.

==Quick Walkthrough==
# Speak to [[Skyrim:Elisif the Fair|Elisif the Fair]].
# Place [[Skyrim:Torygg's_War_Horn|Torygg's War Horn]] at the shrine of Talos {{Map Link|x=52654|y=8111|zoom=16}}.
# Return to Elisif.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
===A Personal Request===
After you complete [[Skyrim:The Man Who Cried Wolf|The Man Who Cried Wolf]], [[Skyrim:Elisif the Fair|Elisif's]] goodwill towards you has increased. So much so that she extends a tentative trust in you by making a personal request regarding her late husband, [[Skyrim:High King Torygg|High King Torygg]]. She will tell you, ''"When we buried my husband I made offerings to all the gods... except [[Lore:Talos|Talos]]."'' This is because Talos worship is outlawed in the Empire. She would like you to take [[Skyrim:Torygg's_War_Horn|Torygg's War Horn]] and place it at a specific [[Skyrim:Shrines#Shrine_of_Talos|Shrine of Talos]]. Although she doesn't worship Talos herself, her husband would have wanted a proper [[Lore:Nord|Nordic]] burial done in this fashion.   
===The Shrine of Talos===
Travel to the Shrine of Talos in the wilderness of [[Skyrim:Whiterun Hold|Whiterun Hold]], due north of [[Skyrim:The Ritual Stone|The Ritual Stone]]. Follow the path near [[Skyrim:Shimmermist Cave|Shimmermist Cave]], along the northern bank of the river, and you can find the shrine behind some trees. As you approach the shrine, [[Skyrim:Agent Lorcalin|Agent Lorcalin]] and a [[Skyrim:Thalmor|Thalmor]] soldier will appear and attack you, as Lorcalin is under [[Skyrim:Lorcalin's Orders|orders]] from the [[Skyrim:Elenwen|Thalmor emissary]] to kill any Talos worshippers he can find. Once the horn is placed in front of the statue of Talos and the quest updates, you are free to take it away at any time without affecting the quest's progress, and it will no longer be marked as a quest item.

===The Jarl's Good Grace===
Return to Elisif at the [[Skyrim:Blue Palace|Blue Palace]] in [[Skyrim:Solitude|Solitude]] where she will reaffirm her belief in you and allow you to purchase [[Skyrim:Proudspire Manor|Proudspire Manor]] as well as take the next step to becoming a [[Skyrim:Thane|thane]].

==Notes==
* Prior to completing the prerequisite quest, the horn can be pickpocketed from Elisif. It will be marked as a quest item and cannot be removed from your inventory without completing the quest.
* Fighting the Thalmor is not necessary to finish the quest; they can be [[Skyrim:Calm|calmed]] or evaded in order to activate the statue's base.
* The Thalmor will always spawn the first time you are at the shrine, regardless of whether you're doing the quest.

==Bugs==
{{bug|The Thalmor may not spawn at all because of a random encounter such as a dragon attack, although this doesn't affect the quest.|confirmed=1}}
{{Bug|Alternatively, the Thalmor may spawn at the shrine itself, frequently sitting on one of the benches.|confirmed=1}}

Skyrim:Vald's Debt.wikitext: {{Cleanup-srqrp |writtenBy=Beezer1029 |checkedBy= |reward=Nephele |rewardChecked=Riliane }}{{About|the quest|the note|Vald's Debt (note)}}{{Quest Header |type=Miscellaneous |Giver= |Loc= |Reward=The [[Skyrim:Mercer's House Key|key]] to [[Skyrim:Riftweald Manor|Riftweald Manor]] |Image=SR-quest-Vald's Debt.jpg |Imgdesc=Vald's Strongbox |Conc=[[Skyrim:The Pursuit|The Pursuit]] |description=Find the [[Skyrim:Quill of Gemination|Quill of Gemination]] to clear [[Skyrim:Vald|Vald]]'s debt to [[Skyrim:Maven_Black-Briar|Maven Black-Briar]]. |ID=FreeformValdDebt }} ==Quick Walkthrough== # Talk to [[Skyrim:Maven Black-Briar|Maven Black-Briar]] about erasing [[Skyrim:Vald|Vald]]'s debt. # Find the [[Skyrim:Quill of Gemination|Quill of Gemination]] in [[Skyrim:Lake_Honrich|Lake Honrich]]. # Bring the quill to Maven. # Give the note to Vald. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===To Catch a Thief=== With hard evidence in hand, you and [[Skyrim:Karliah|Karliah]] inform [[Skyrim:Brynjolf|Brynjolf]] of [[Skyrim: Mercer Frey|Mercer Frey's]] nefarious deeds. Brynjolf decides that more intelligence is needed on Mercer's plans and asks you break into [[Skyrim:Riftweald Manor|Riftweald Manor]] to see what you can find out—with impunity. ===The Watchdog=== Ask Brynjolf about Riftweald Manor and he will mention a "trained watchdog" guarding the house; a man named [[Skyrim:Vald|Vald]] that Mercer is extorting. Brynjolf suggests you speak to [[Skyrim:Vex|Vex]] for more on Vald. Vex has a few choice words about Vald, but will also tell you that he is working for Mercer Frey because of a debt he owes to [[Skyrim:Maven Black-Briar|Maven Black-Briar]]. Clearing the debt is suggested as one way to get Vald to stop guarding Mercer's house. ===The Queen Bee and the Quill=== To learn the details of the debt, track down Maven, who can typically be found at [[Skyrim:The Bee and Barb|The Bee and Barb]]. She tells you that years ago she commissioned a [[Skyrim:Quill of Gemination|unique quill]] from Winterhold. Vald was to deliver the quill to her, but he lost it at the bottom of [[Skyrim:Lake Honrich|Lake Honrich]], outside of [[Skyrim:Riften|Riften]]. [[File:SR-quest-Vald's Debt 02.png|thumb|The location of the quill shown on the local map]] From [[Skyrim:Riften Stables|Riften Stables]], head southwest until you reach the edge of the lake. Ahead, you should see a large ship docked at Riften. Swim towards the westernmost end of that ship and look west across the lake towards [[Skyrim:Goldenglow Estate|Goldenglow Estate]] to see a similar ship docked there. Halfway to the other boat, the prow of Vald's sunken rowboat can be found at the bottom of the lake. For reference, a small island to the north will mark the halfway point. You'll see half a boat prow sticking out of the ground and the quill is located in Vald's Strongbox (leveled lock) {{Map Link|Vald's Strongbox}}. Pick it, take the quill and a leveled amount of gold, then head back to find Maven. She'll hand you a [[Skyrim:Vald's Debt (note)|note]] to take to Vald. ===Clearing the way=== Head to the back gate of Riftweald Manor and wait there until Vald comes to talk to you. Inform him that you have erased his debt, and he will want to do you a good turn as well, giving you the key to the Manor and opening the back gate for you. ==Notes== * The quill does not spawn until you have spoken to Maven about it, so you cannot skip this step. * It's possible to keep the quill for yourself. To do this, talk to Maven to get the quill to spawn, go and obtain the quill, then go to Vald and intimidate/bribe him to let you pass. The miscellaneous quest will disappear from your quest log and the quill will no longer be marked as a quest item and is free to be dropped/deposited. This was done with the Unofficial Skyrim Patch installed. Results may vary. [Confirmed in USSEP 4.3.0] ==Bugs== {{Bug|Even if you kill Vald, you will still have the dialogue option to erase his debt with Maven. Attempting to erase Vald's debt after he is dead will still earn you leveled gold, but you will be unable to complete the quest by delivering the letter of pardon. The quest and item will stay active.|USKP|1.2.4}} ** If the undelivered letter bothers you, it seems you can place it on owned bookshelves. You can also leave it on his corpse. * The dialogue option to tell Vald his debt is gone appears as soon as you've picked up the quill. Turning it in to Maven is therefore optional. {{Bug|It's possible that Vald won't come talk to you at the gate when you bring him the note to clear his debt, becoming hostile toward you instead. This can occur if you've walked too close to the yard after the quest has started, but before erasing Vald's debt.|USKP|2.0.4}} **Sometimes the bug occurs even with the Unofficial Patch. **You can also try using [[Skyrim:Pacify (effect)|Pacify]] if he becomes hostile and you don't wish to kill him. **Alternatively, approach him with your weapon out and when he attacks go into the console, click him, type setav aggression 0, exit the console, then sheathe your weapon. {{Bug|It is possible to tell Vald you erased his debt even if you had not yet been to Maven Black-Briar to turn in the Quill of Gemination.|USLEEP|3.0.1|A bad stage check on one of the dialogue lines in The Pursuit was responsible for this.}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |10||{{Quest Objective|10|Talk to Maven about Vald's debt}} |20||{{Quest Objective|20|Locate the Quill of Gemination under Lake Honrich}} |30||{{Quest Objective|30|Bring the Quill of Gemination to Maven}} |missing=0, 40, 200 }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}} {{Stub|Quest}}

[[Skyrim:Arondil's Journal, Part 2|Arondil's Journal, Part 2]]

[[Skyrim:Arondil's Journal, Part 4|Arondil's Journal, Part 4]] |Image=SR-quest-Toying With The Dead.jpg |Imgdesc=Arondil on his throne |description=Retrieve a [[Skyrim:Arondil|necromancer]]'s journals for an interested buyer. |ID=FreeformRiften21 |Icon=SR-qico-Thieves Guild.png |SuggLevel=8 |Difficulty=Medium }} ==Quick Walkthrough== #Travel to [[Skyrim:Yngvild|Yngvild]]. #Collect the four journals. #Return to [[Skyrim:Vekel the Man|Vekel]]. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===The Proposition=== If you approach Vekel in [[Skyrim:The Ragged Flagon|The Ragged Flagon]] and ask him for work, he will tell you about some journals that he's been after: ''"I have a buyer with a very odd taste in literature, looking for some particular books. I'm told they're the ravings of a madman, a wizard named [[Skyrim:Arondil|Arondil]] and his peculiar cravings. It's said to be in four volumes and very hard to come by. My client is offering quite a reward for them, which I'd split with you."'' If you ask for him to elaborate further on the journals, he will go on to say, ''"Recently, a woman was found... naked and shivering along the road to [[Skyrim:Dawnstar|Dawnstar]]. The only information the guard could get from her were tales of strange experiments and Arondil scribbling in his journals."'' Asking about Arondil won't get you much, as Vekel says, ''"Only rumors. He used to have a home in Dawnstar until they burned it down. The people say he was doing unspeakable experiments on reanimation... rituals only a necromancer would perform. After he made for Yngvild, he was never heard from again."'' Once you agree to retrieve the journals, he will conclude the conversation with: ''"Then we have a deal. In his later years, {{sic|Andoril|Arondil}} moved into some ice caves known as Yngvild. He {{sic|prefered|preferred}} the solitude in which to perform his, um... experiments."'' ===Yngvild=== [[File:SR-place-Yngvild.jpg|thumb|right|The ruins of Yngvild]] Yngvild is an ice cave located on an island northeast of Dawnstar. To access it, find the entrance on the north side by following the pathway up the island. Once inside, you are able to find the first three journals. The [[Skyrim:Arondil's Journal, Part 1|first journal]] is located on a table near two [[Skyrim:Yngvild Ghost|Yngvild ghosts]] and a leveled [[Skyrim:Draugr|draugr]]. The [[Skyrim:Arondil's Journal, Part 2|second journal]] can be found on a table alongside a [[Skyrim:Woodcutter's Axe|woodcutter's axe]] and a [[Skyrim:Scroll of Raise Zombie|scroll]]. The [[Skyrim:Arondil's Journal, Part 3|third journal]] can be found on a table just before the door leading to [[Skyrim:Yngvild Throne Room|Yngvild Throne Room]]. ===Yngvild Throne Room=== Once you enter the main chamber in the throne room, you will see Arondil sitting on his throne with an Yngvild ghost alongside him. The [[Skyrim:Arondil's Journal, Part 4|fourth]] and final part of the journal lies through the door behind him, on a table along with an [[Skyrim:Unusual Gem|unusual gem]] for the quest [[Skyrim:No Stone Unturned|No Stone Unturned]]. Once you have retrieved the journals, you can exit the cave and head back to [[Skyrim:The Ragged Flagon|The Ragged Flagon]] to receive your reward. ===Reward=== Return all four journals to Vekel and he will remark, ''"Good. I was hoping you hadn't forgotten about it. As promised, here's your payment for bringing them to me. Got it as part of a fair trade from my client."'' Your reward for returning the journals is a leveled and [[Skyrim:Enchanting Effects|enchanted]] [[Skyrim:One-Handed Weapons|one-handed weapon]]. ==Notes== * You don't have to kill [[Skyrim:Arondil|Arondil]] to complete the quest, merely get his journals. * This quest can be started even if you're not a member of the [[Skyrim:Thieves Guild (faction)|Thieves Guild]] at all. * Sneaking into the final chamber unnoticed and removing the Soul Gem from the pedestal next to Arondil causes the ghosts near him to attack and kill him. * Objectives for this quest will add themselves to the quest log even if you'd never been to see Vekel about finding the books. ** This is no longer the case with version 4.2.4 of the [[Skyrim Mod:Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch|Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch]]. ==Bugs== {{Bug|Vekel will neither reward you on completion of the quest, nor take the journals.|OSP|1.9.26.0.8|He will now reward you properly, and the journals will no longer be marked as quest items once the quest is complete, and can be dropped or sold.}} {{Bug|As stated above, Vekel does not actually remove the journals from your inventory upon quest completion, even with the Official Patch.|USKP|1.0}} {{Bug|This quest can be started without talking to Vekel; if you go to Yngvild and pick up all four journals, you will receive a quest update telling you to return them to Vekel, even if you never spoke to him before.|USKP|1.0|He has been given appropriate dialogue to acknowledge the fact that he had never given you the task to find the journals prior.}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |20||{{Quest Objective|10|Enter Yngvild Barrow}} |30||{{Quest Objective|20|Retrieve Arondil's Journals (/4)}} |40||{{Quest Objective|30|Return to Vekel}} |200|fin| |missing=10, 250 }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}}

{{Cleanup-srqrp |writtenBy=Krusty |checkedBy=Beezer1029 |reward=Krusty |rewardChecked=Chezburgar }}[[Category:Skyrim-Quests-Dungeon Quests]][[Category:Skyrim-Quests-Non-Journal Quests]]{{About|the quest|the location|Yngol Barrow}}{{Quest Header |type=Miscellaneous |Giver= |Loc=[[Skyrim:Yngol Barrow|Yngol Barrow]] |Reward=[[Skyrim:Helm of Yngol|Helm of Yngol]] |image=SR-place-Yngol_Barrow.jpg |imgdesc=Yngol Barrow |description=Find the treasure unlocked by the [[Skyrim:Coral Dragon Claw|Coral Dragon Claw]]. |ID=dunYngolBarrowQST |SuggLevel=6 }}{{#addtotrail:Dungeon Quests|separator=' / '}} ==Quick Walkthrough== '''Note''': This quest does not appear in your journal (see [[#Bugs|this section]] for details). #Obtain a [[Skyrim:Coral Dragon Claw|Coral Dragon Claw]]. #Solve the Barrow's puzzle. #Escape the Barrow. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===Birna's Odd Investment=== When you arrive in snowy [[Skyrim:Winterhold|Winterhold]] for the first time, you may witness local merchant [[Skyrim:Birna|Birna]] and her brother [[Skyrim:Ranmir|Ranmir]] shout at each other in the middle of the street: [[File:SR-quest-Yngol's Barrow.jpg|thumb|''"We need coin, Ranmir, and you're not bringing home any."'']] '''Birna''': ''"We need coin, Ranmir, and you're not bringing home any."''
'''Ranmir''': ''"And you'd have me do what, join the College and prance about casting spells all day?"''
'''Birna''': ''"Don't just walk away from me! Where do you think you're going?"''
'''Ranmir''': ''"To the Inn for a drink, of course! Where else could I even go in this gods-forsaken town?"''
'''Birna''': ''"And what, you think that'll solve all your problems?"''
'''Ranmir''': ''"Probably not, but it's worth a try!"'' Obviously, Birna needs some profits, and during conversation she will mention a bad deal she made recently: ''"Yeah, it was stupid of me. I shouldn't have believed the story and just refused the trade. But I didn't, and now I'm stuck with this worthless junk."'' She will then tell the tale: ''"Some line about this claw thing and Yngol Barrow. He said it was worth more than its weight in gold if I took it back there. Something about placing it back in Yngol's chamber, I don't know. What was I thinking? Even if it were true, I'm not setting foot in some ancient tomb, filled with who knows what."'' She will then sell you the [[Skyrim:Coral Dragon Claw|Coral Dragon Claw]] for 50 gold and leave you to find [[Skyrim:Yngol Barrow|Yngol Barrow]] on your own. Alternatively, the claw can be found inside Yngol Barrow, before purchasing it from Birna. ===Yngol Barrow=== Nobody in Winterhold will guide you to the Barrow, as it is located much closer to Windhelm, where guards will provide directions and a bit of fair warning: ''"Across the river to the northeast lies Yngol Barrow. Steer clear of that foul place, lest the walking dead claim you as their own."'' Head northeast and follow the [[Skyrim:White River|White River]] until you reach the Barrow on the eastern shore. The exterior of the Barrow is unguarded, but a strange altar with a few ingredients and the book ''[[Skyrim:Yngol and the Sea-Ghosts|Yngol and the Sea-Ghosts]]'' welcomes you. Reading through the book reveals that the Barrow is the final resting place of [[Skyrim:Ysgramor|Ysgramor]]'s son Yngol, who was killed by Sea-Ghosts during Ysgramor's return to [[Lore:Tamriel|Tamriel]]. The first tunnel is narrow and covered in ice so proceed forward until you reach a cauldron. A small beeping sound can be heard and a light-blue orb will jump up, following you around to lead the path. As you proceed forward another orb will soon join from a sarcophagus, then a third, all of them floating towards the same goal. ===A Dead Scholar=== [[File:SR-interior-Yngol Barrow.jpg|thumb|The Puzzle Room]] In the first real chamber, a [[Skyrim:Dead Scholar|Dead Scholar]] lies headdown in front of a sealed-off gate and a handle. Pushing the handle will cause a [[Skyrim:Dart Trap|dart trap]] to trigger, making it obvious what killed the scholar. Search his inventory for his [[Skyrim:Notes on Yngol Barrow|Notes on Yngol Barrow]] which includes his transcription of the many carvings around the chamber. Look around and you will see four alcoves, one with a throne and three of them with rotating pillars. There's an alcove with running water, one with sunlight, and one overgrown by plants. Check out the scholar's transcripts and rotate the pillars as follows: *'''''Whale''' in the sea, so should he be'' *'''''Eagle''' in Sun's Sky, so should he be'' *'''''Snake''' in the weed so should he be'' Pull the handle and the gate will disappear, allowing yet another light-blue orb to join the party. Note that if you didn't buy the claw from [[Skyrim:Birna|Birna]], a second claw will be sitting on the pedestal on the other side of the gate. Proceed forward through the empty tombs and icy passages and take a dive in the flooded room for a bit of minor treasure. When you reach a room overgrown with ferns, beware of the hidden [[Skyrim:Pressure Plate|pressure plate]] triggering a [[Skyrim:Spike Wall|spike wall]] from the ceiling. As you reach the expected [[Skyrim:Traps#Puzzle Door|puzzle door]], a total of eleven light-blue orbs will bounce around you, pointing towards the puzzle. Take a closer look at the claw for the correct combination, '''Snake—Wolf—Moth''', and turn the rings to match. Insert the claw in the keyhole and watch as the door opens. ===The Shade of Yngol=== [[File:SR-interior-Yngol Barrow 03.jpg|thumb|Yngol rising]] The gate opens to a fluorescent room with a huge boss-leveled chest and a throne, facing away from you. As soon as you enter, [[Skyrim:Yngol's Shade|Yngol's Shade]] breaks loose from the skeletal remains of Yngol and attacks. The shade is a boss-leveled [[Skyrim:Draugr|draugr]] and can be as powerful as a [[Skyrim:Dragon Priest|dragon priest]] at higher levels. Depending on your level, he may have [[Skyrim:Unrelenting Force|Unrelenting Force]], [[Skyrim:Disarm|Disarm]], [[Skyrim:Frost Breath|Frost Breath]], and a [[Skyrim:Frost Cloak|Frost Cloak]] spell. His weapon is leveled, possibly enchanted, and can be either one- or two-handed. After the battle, loot the remains for valuables and search the boss-leveled chest for a healthy amount of gold and a copy of the rare [[Skyrim:Two-handed|Two-handed]] skill book ''[[Skyrim:Song Of Hrormir|Song Of Hrormir]]'', then claim the [[Skyrim:Helm of Yngol|Helm of Yngol]] from the skeleton in the throne. When you take it, the gate behind you will raise and provide easy access to a staircase and a door leading to the outside world. ==Notes== * You can still purchase the Coral Dragon Claw from Birna even if you picked up the claw in the barrow first. However, once you've offered to buy the coral dragon claw from Birna (even if you didn't actually do so), the one in the barrow will disappear. * A button near Yngol's resting place, positioned to the right of the puzzle door, seems to serve as a fail-safe should you ever unintentionally become trapped within the room. How players could end up in such a situation is unclear. ==Bugs== {{Bug|The objectives for the quest are listed in the game files, but they're never set to display. This prevents any objectives from ever showing up in your journal. Additionally, it will not count in your statistics.|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|If the dragon claw door does not work, check [[Skyrim:Puzzle Totems#Bugs|here]] for possible fixes.|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|If [[Skyrim:Dungeon Delving (Jarl - Caves)|Dungeon Delving]] has sent you to Yngol Barrow, the Helm of Yngol and the skeleton it rests upon are completely missing.|USKP|2.0.4|Dungeon Delving will reserve the location and block this quest from running until it is completed.}} ** It is reported that the game spawns Yngol and his helm when you are near his throne. Thus, a possible workaround is to send a follower to retrieve the Helm of Winterhold from the final chest, then backtrack Yngol Barrow and finish Korir's favor quest by giving him the Helm of Winterhold. Then, go back to the barrow, and Yngol and his helm will be successfully spawned. ** {{Pc22}} Once the Helm of Winterhold has been returned to Jarl Korir, use the console commands pcb to clear the cell cache, and then ResetInterior YngolBarrow01 to make the dungeon respawn. Yngol's Shade and his helm should be at their correct location next time you enter, and you should be able to get out through the gate at the end. Yngol's Shade's inventory will activate automatically on re-entering the room and there will be no additional boss to fight. {{Bug|It is possible to acquire 2 copies of the Coral Dragon Claw, which was not intended. This is in part due to the Winterhold segment being part of an unfinished quest that was never completely disabled.|USLEEP|3.0.1}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |''Unknown''||{{Quest Objective|0|Explore Yngol's Barrow}} {{Quest Objective|50|Escape Yngol's Barrow}} [[Category:Skyrim-SRQRP-Unknown Objectives]] |missing=10, 15, 49, 50, 100 }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}}

==Quick Walkthrough==
'''Note''': This quest does not appear in your journal.
# Speak to the quest giver.
# Challenge them to a brawl.
# Win the brawl.
# Speak to them again.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
If you talk to one of the quest givers they will eventually challenge you to a [[Skyrim:Brawl|brawl]]. The dialogue and circumstances vary from person to person and are listed in the table above. Accepting the challenge means that you place a 100 gold bet on the outcome. You must then brawl them and win. Standard brawling rules apply and use of things such as hostile magic, shouts, and weapons will instantly change it from a brawl to a criminal assault.

Brawling should be relatively easy if you're wearing any armor and have gained at least a few levels. Only low level players on higher difficulties may have issues with winning a brawl. If you are having problems, use some potions and spells with lingering effects and don't forget about racial powers. It may be of use as well to read more in-depth information on [[Skyrim:Combat#Unarmed Combat|unarmed combat]].  You do not gain any experience from the unarmed combat during a brawl, although you may gain experience in armor skills.

You can only win a brawl with any given person once. If you lose the brawl, you will not get your wagered money back, although you will be able to get a rematch. If you win the brawl, you will get your wager back and receive an additional 100 gold.

==Notes==
* There are other quests that simply involve brawling such as [[Skyrim:Bloody Nose|Bloody Nose]] that are in fact separate from this quest, despite being nearly identical in nature.
* If you have less than 100 gold when asking for a bet, the combatant may say things like "Come back when you actually have 100 gold."
* When you win your wager back and receive an additional 100 gold, a "Gold (200) Added" message will appear on the top left of the screen.
* When you engage in a brawl, spectators may say things like these:
** ''"Twelve septims on the big one!"''
** ''"Fight! Fight!"''
** ''"Drive that snowback to the ground. Come on!"''
** ''"You just going to stand there and take it? Fight back."''
** ''"Who taught you to fight? Keep those hands up!"'' 
* When you engage in a brawl, viewing NPCs become immersed and tend to run around the fight. This can be quite annoying, as they can potentially run between you and your combatant which can lead you to accidentally punching one of the excited onlookers, which counts as an assault. Also, if you run away from the fight and exit through any doors, the first four NPCs who witness your fight will keep following you and will still think you are in a brawl until you fast travel.
* Certain considerations apply to the brawl itself:
** Although your opponent may say "No magic," you can in fact use magic on yourself, such as [[Skyrim:Armor (spells)|armor]], [[Skyrim:Restore Health|healing]], or [[Skyrim:Ward (spells)|ward]] spells. However, using spells on your opponent, even beneficial healing spells, will count as assault.
** Wearing the [[Skyrim:Ebony Mail|Ebony Mail]] or using a cloaking spell will also count as assault. However, wearing [[Skyrim:Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution|Ahzidal's Armor of Retribution]]{{DB}} does not.
** You can use a shield bash to "punch" your opponent.
* Winning the brawl will raise the [[Skyrim:Disposition|disposition]] of the challenger. This will allow you to take low-value items they own, and they may become available as [[Skyrim:Followers|followers]] or potential [[Skyrim:Marriage|marriage]] partners. See the individual NPC pages for details.
* Because this is a favor quest which affects the quest giver's disposition, it will count towards the "Help the People" part of the [[Skyrim:Thane|thane]] quest for the quest giver's hold (with the exception of quest givers who live in Orc strongholds).
* Only one radiant quest of a similar type can be assigned at any given time. However, the dialogue to start the brawl is part of the quest, and the quest starts silently when you approach a location containing a quest giver. If two quest givers are near each other (e.g., Cosnach and Chief Burguk), the quest may start for one and block the dialogue to brawl with the other. Besides winning the brawl, the quest will also silently stop after some time away from the location.

==Bugs==
{{Bug|Sometimes your opponent may draw their weapon and attack you like in a normal fight. In this case, your only options are to yield or kill them (except Rolff, who is essential), and it is unlikely you will be able to properly complete the quest even if you try again.}}
{{Bug|Having the [[Skyrim:Fists of Steel|Fists of Steel]] perk may cause your opponent to remain in bleedout mode after you win the fight. Unequipping your Heavy Armor gauntlets will resolve this.}}
{{Bug|Engaging in a brawl for this quest can cause the [[Skyrim:Gray Cowl of Nocturnal|Gray Cowl of Nocturnal]] to permanently lose its ability to detect life and trigger guard hostility.}}
{{Bug|Engaging in brawls for this quest while wearing the [[Skyrim:Ebony Mail|Ebony Mail]] can inflict the armor's poison damage effect on your opponent, leading to assault bounties.|USKP|1.2.4}}

== Quick Walkthrough ==
# Speak to [[Skyrim:Neloth|Neloth]].
# Allow him to cast an [[Skyrim:Neloth's Health Boost|experimental spell]] on you.
# Enter the water at any point in gameplay.
# Return to Neloth to report the side effects of his spell.

== Detailed Walkthrough ==
[[Skyrim:Neloth|Neloth]] will request you help him with an experiment. Agree and he will cast an [[Skyrim:Neloth's Health Boost|experimental spell]] on you, instructing you to report to him any side effects. The spell will endow you with 25 additional points of health. You can observe the status of the effect through the Active Effects section of your magic menu. The effect is permanent until you submerge yourself up to arm's length in water. Doing so will then cause a 25 point decrease to health permanently until you return to Neloth. Streams running through caves, and other shallow water regions should not affect this, nor should wading in shallow water for any period of time. It is therefore possible by carefully avoiding deep water to maintain this bonus for a significant period. By obtaining [[Skyrim:Ahzidal's Boots of Waterwalking|Ahzidal's Boots of Waterwalking]] during [[Skyrim:Unearthed|Unearthed]] this bonus can theoretically be maintained indefinitely, provided you manage to stay out of the rain (some players have reported that rain induces the negative effects).
Returning to Neloth and reporting the negative effects will result in him removing the spell, which will set you back to normal. He will then reward you 250 gold regardless of your level.

== Notes ==
* Any body of liquid, such as the acid in [[Skyrim:Apocrypha|Apocrypha]] or the lava in [[Skyrim:The Aetherium Forge|The Aetherium Forge]], counts as water for the purposes of this quest.

== Bugs ==
{{Bug|When Neloth asks if you are willing to be an experimental subject, the dialogue may end without presenting the option "What kind of experiment". This means the quest cannot be started.|UDBP|2.0.4}}
**It may also break the Research quest chain. Completing another quest for Neloth may restore the proper dialogue functions.

== Detailed Walkthrough ==
Find [[Skyrim:Elmus|Elmus]] at [[Skyrim:Bujold's Retreat|Bujold's Retreat]] and talk to him. He requests that you bring him a bottle of [[Skyrim:Ashfire Mead|Ashfire Mead]] from the [[Skyrim:Thirsk Mead Hall|Thirsk Mead Hall]], which has been taken over by [[Skyrim:Riekling|rieklings]]. After that, travel over to the mead hall. If you have never visited it before, you will meet a riekling outside, trying to lead you to his tribe's [[Skyrim:Riekling Chief|chief]]. Just head inside, take at least one bottle of Ashfire Mead, and return to Elmus. Give him the mead and receive your reward.

== Detailed Walkthrough ==
===The Eighth Silence===
[[Skyrim:Neloth|Neloth]] is excited about his new research. Offer to help and he will explain that he is working on a new silence spell. If you agree to help Neloth will reply, ''"Excellent. If this works, I'll prepare a version that you can cast yourself, if you ever wish to inflict... er, study silence."'' He will then prepare and cast the spell.

===Tentacle Things===
You will be rendered blind for a short time, and your stamina will drain. In the dark, Neloth will speak to you, while a panicked [[Skyrim:Talvas Fathryon|Talvas Fathryon]] interjects:
{| cellspacing=8 class="hiddentable vtop"
| '''Talvas:'''||''"Master Neloth! What have you done to him/her? What are those things growing out of his/her eyes?"''
|-
| '''Neloth:'''||''"Well that's unexpected. I presume you are blind, given the state of your eyes. It's nothing that can't be fixed. The spell that is. I think I can fix the spell. It should only take a couple more years. But first, I need some data. Try wiggling them. No, don't shake your fist. Wiggle the tentacle things where your eyes used to be."''
|-
| '''Talvas:'''||''"I think I'm going to be sick."''
|-
| '''Neloth:''' ||''"Hmm. From the way they are waving about, I'm assuming they aren't under your control. And I see now that your tongue is also...well, it's probably best if I don't say. Don't bother trying to scream though."''
|-
| '''Talvas:'''|| ''(Vomits)''
|-
| '''Talvas:'''||''"Is it over yet? Does he/she have eyes again?"''
|-
| '''Neloth:'''||''"It looks like it's beginning to wear off. Hmm. Your eyes appear to be completely back to normal. Interesting."''
|}

===Compensation===
Your sight will automatically be restored at this point. You can ask Neloth for compensation:

:'''I think you owe me for that spell.'''
:''"I suppose I do. It's too bad it wore off so quickly though. Unfortunately you don't appear to be suffering from any side effects. Anyway, take this for your time."''

He will give you 250 gold.

# In the console, enter `GetGlobalValue DLC2TT4bRun`. Check if the return value is 1.
# In the console, enter `set DLC2TT4bRun to 0` and `resetquest DLC2TT4bRun`.

Completing another Neloth quest should allow you to start this one.
