He rode through town not long ago with an escort of soldiers. They didn't stop, just headed south across the Dragon Bridge.'' |} Head across the Dragon Bridge and make your way south along the road until you come across a wrecked carriage. Among the wreckage are a dead [[Skyrim:Horse|horse]], a bloodstained [[Skyrim:Corpse|corpse]], a copy of the book ''[[Skyrim:Effects of the Elder Scrolls|Effects of the Elder Scrolls]]'', and a dead [[Skyrim:Vampire|vampire]]. Search the vampire to find a [[Skyrim:Vampire's Note|note]] directing you to [[Skyrim:Forebears' Holdout|Forebears' Holdout]], a ruin up the hill to the northeast. Follow the blood spatters, and when you reach the four standing stones, the entrance is to the north. ===Forebears' Holdout=== [[File:SR-quest-Prophet (Vampire) 02.jpg|thumb|right|The barrier with the Moth Priest inside]] Inside, you will see what appears to be a ruined underground fort inside a large natural cavern divided by a river. Past the fort, you may notice the large blue-green orb on the platform; this is your target. Head left down the stairs and across the bridge. There is a [[Skyrim:Dawnguard (faction)|Dawnguard]] warrior patrolling the walls of the fort, and more enemies inside, including an [[Skyrim:Armored Troll|armored troll]]. However you wish to deal with them, make your way to the interior of the fort, climb the stairs and head across the platform to the orb from before. It is actually a magical barrier, and it contains the Moth Priest, [[Skyrim:Dexion Evicus|Dexion Evicus]], trapped inside. If you are stealthy enough as you go up the stairs, you can overhear a conversation between a Dawnguard lieutenant and his [[Skyrim:Vanik|commander]]: :'''Dawnguard Lieutenant''': ''"Those vampires put up a hell of a fight."'' :'''Vanik''': ''"I just hope we weren't too late. I'm not sure what they did to this Moth Priest, but he doesn't look right."'' :'''Dawnguard Lieutenant''': ''"You think they turned him?"'' :'''Vanik''': ''"I don't know, maybe. Won't know until we get him out of there."'' :'''Dawnguard Lieutenant''': ''"How do we do that?"'' :'''Vanik''': ''"I'm working on it, now give me some silence so I can think."'' Kill them, and search the corpse of [[Skyrim:Malkus|Malkus]], located between the barrier and the west wall, for the [[Skyrim:Weystone Focus|weystone focus]]. With this in hand, go up the western stairs and find the weystone source on another platform overlooking the barrier. Activating the source with the focus in your possession will drop the barrier, and Dexion will emerge, chanting, ''"I serve my master's will."'' His demeanor will then change: ''"But my master is dead, and his enemies will pay!"'' He attacks you with all his might, so fight back until he yields. While he is kneeling, use your Vampire's Seduction power on him. Activate him after this to feed on him and make him your thrall. He will be awestruck: ''"By the divines! It's as if my eyes have been opened! I am blinded by the light of your majesty. I... I must obey you. What would you have of me, master?"'' Order him to travel to Castle Volkihar, where you must return as well. ===Prophet=== When you arrive, your new thrall will be waiting in the main hall, along with your fellow vampires. Talk to Harkon at the far end of the hall. When you tell him what you have done, he will say, ''"Yes, I see that. I trust his capture was not too difficult a task?"'' You then have three options; whichever one you choose, he will then give you your next instruction: ''"Well, your thrall awaits and we have given him the Elder Scroll. Command him to read it, and let us hear the words of prophecy together."'' Order Dexion to read the Elder Scroll, and he will be excited: ''"Ah, yes, the Elder Scroll! I admit, I'm looking forward to this."'' Then he will produce the Scroll and read from it, leaving you with more questions than answers:
{|cellpadding="10" cellspacing="10" |- |style="border: dotted 1px black; text-align:center;"| '''''"I see a vision before me, an image of a great bow. I know this weapon! It is Auriel's Bow!'''''
'''''Now a voice whispers, saying "Among the night's children, a dread lord will rise."'''''
'''''In an age of strife, when dragons return to the realm of men, darkness will mingle with light and the night and day will be as one.'''''
'''''The voice fades and the words begin to shimmer and distort. But wait, there is more here.'''''
'''''The secret of the bow's power is written elsewhere. I think there is more to the prophecy, recorded in other scrolls.'''''
'''''Yes, I see them now... One contains the ancient secrets of the dragons, and the other speaks of the potency of ancient blood.'''''
'''''My vision darkens, and I see no more.'''''
'''''To know the complete prophecy, we must have the other two scrolls."''''' |}
Thus ends Prophet, and begins the next two quests, [[Skyrim:Chasing Echoes|Chasing Echoes]] and [[Skyrim:Seeking Disclosure|Seeking Disclosure]]. ==Notes== *If you do not possess the power [[Skyrim:Vampire's Seduction|Vampire's Seduction]] when you are required to enthrall [[Skyrim:Dexion Evicus|Dexion Evicus]], you will transform to vampiric level 2 immediately and gain it. If you have been cured of vampirism, you will need to ask Serana to make you a vampire again, then wait for 24 hours to regain the power. *Be careful with your aim when using Vampire's Seduction, as it can only be used once each day. If you miss, you'll have to wait a full 24 hours to try again. Dexion will remain patiently cowering on the ground where you defeated him, however. *Clinton Lylvieve sometimes wanders outside the borders of the town, in which case, the dialogue option for the Moth Priest will not be available. Wait for him to get closer to town and it will become available again. *After you are told to go to Dragon Bridge, you can instead head straight to Forebears' Holdout, where at a point inside, the quest will update and proceed normally. ==Bugs== {{Bug|Talking to the guards in Dragon Bridge may not bring up a dialogue option to ask them about the Moth Priest, even when you have been directed towards them by other citizens.|USKP|1.2.5|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|If you exit the castle before Harkon finishes his speech, Serana might not come up and talk to you, preventing quest progression.|vn=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|It is possible for Dexion to escape the barrier prematurely and become permanently hostile to you.|UDGP|2.0.1}} {{Bug|Once you defeat the enthralled Moth Priest and use your seduction power on him, the option to feed may not appear. You may have to reload a previous save before entering the code if Dexion has already engaged in combat with the vampires. {{Bug|Using your Vampire's Seduction on Dexion may have no effect. You will visually see your Power firing but doing so does not progress the quest.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} **{{Pc22}}Use the console command setstage DLC1VQ03Vampire 70 to advance to the next stage. {{Bug|After using Vampire's Seduction to feed on the Moth Priest, he may remain hostile. [[SR:Fura Bloodmouth|Fura Bloodmouth]] will say:
''"A feral-blooded has holed up with a group of bandits/necromancers. Likely wants to create a nest of broodlings."
"We don't need competition for blood, and we don't want the mortals getting up in arms making things difficult for us."
"Go destroy the feral beast before this becomes a problem."''
When hunting the vampire, it will be at a random location, either a [[:Category:Skyrim-Places-Bandit Camps|bandit camp]] or [[:Category:Skyrim-Places-Warlock Lairs|warlock lair]]. This can include locations added by [[Skyrim:Add-ons|official add-ons]] such as [[Skyrim:Hrodulf's House|Hrodulf's House]] in [[Lore:Solstheim|Solstheim]]. ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |10||, concerned that additional vampires in the area will cause problems for the Court, has sent me to where I am to destroy the before it turns its allies into vampires. {{Quest Objective|10|Kill the at }} |100||{{Quest Objective|100|Return to }} |255|fin|, concerned that additional vampires in the area would cause problems for the Court, sent me to where I destroyed the before it turned its allies into vampires. }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}} {{Stub|Quest}}

==Quick Walkthrough==
# Speak with [[Skyrim:Florentius_Baenius|Florentius Baenius]].
# Rescue a kidnapped victim from [[Skyrim:Vampire|vampires]].
# Report back to Florentius.

==Detailed Walkthrough==

After [[Skyrim:Bolstering_the_Ranks|rescuing Florentius Baenius]], speak to him, and ask "What can I do to help?" He will either refer you [[Skyrim:Dawnguard Quests#Dawnguard Side Quests|to somebody else]], or he will explain: ''"[[Lore:Arkay|Arkay]] has some grave news, friend. Your friend, kidnapped! A vicious night stalker rules over a group of [class] - seeks to gain leverage over the righteous. Arkay's never clear on life and death. Is [s]he still alive? There's always hope..."''

The victim can be nearly anyone with a positive [[Skyrim:Disposition|disposition]] towards you, including [[Skyrim:Followers|followers]] and [[Skyrim:Marriage|spouses]]. He or she will be held captive at a random [[:Category:Skyrim-Places-Bandit Camps|bandit camp]] or [[:Category:Skyrim-Places-Warlock Lairs|warlock lair]], bound and helpless.  

Travel to the destination and cut your way through the enemies until you reach the victim. To release them from their bindings, simply interact with them. Once you have rescued them, kill the boss-level vampire in the dungeon before returning to Florentius for your reward: a leveled enchanted item.

==Notes==
{{Dragonborn Radiant Location Note}}
*If the radiant location selected is [[Skyrim:Gallows Rock|Gallows Rock]] there will only be Silver Hand members inside; they will also kill the vampire for you.
*Even if the victim dies before or after you rescue them, the objective will still count as completed.

==Quick Walkthrough==

==Detailed Walkthrough==
Gunmar will inform you that he has located another vampire, hiding among outlaws, and will task you with eliminating it before it turns its companions into vampires. He will then mark a random location on your map: either a [[:Category:Skyrim-Places-Bandit Camps|bandit camp]] or a [[:Category:Skyrim-Places-Warlock Lairs|warlock lair]] (including locations added by [[Skyrim:Add-ons|official add-ons]]).

Travel to the location and dispose of the vampire hiding there. You won't need to kill all other enemies to complete the quest, although in practice you often won't have much choice. Once the vampire is slain, return to Gunmar for your reward: a leveled enchanted item.

==Notes==
* Despite Gunmar stating that the vampire is hiding among "''necromancers''", as you will be sent to a generic warlock lair, you will end up fighting any number of [[Skyrim:Warlock|spellcasters]].

You're an asset."'']] Once you have recruited [[Skyrim:Sorine Jurard|Sorine Jurard]] and [[Skyrim:Gunmar|Gunmar]] into the [[Skyrim:Dawnguard_(faction)|Dawnguard]], and [[Skyrim:Isran|Isran]] has welcomed them to [[Skyrim:Fort Dawnguard|Fort Dawnguard]], you are told to follow Isran for a little interrogation session with the newly arrived vampire, named [[Skyrim:Serana|Serana]]. When asked what she is doing in the enemy fort, she will explain: ''"I'd rather not be here either, but I needed to talk to you. It's important, so please just listen before your friend, here, loses his patience. It's... well, it's about me. And the Elder Scroll that was buried with me. I'm guessing you figured this part out already, but my father's not exactly a good person. Even by vampire standards."'' She then proceeds to explain that her father once was a better person but stumbled upon a prophecy that foretold vampires could control the sun, thus not be afraid of daylight. She finishes with: ''"That's what he's after. He wants to control the sun, have vampires control the world."'' Serana and her mother tried to stop him from taking over the world, so Serana was sealed away with the scroll, to keep it from her father. She realizes she is in a fort filled with vampire hunters, but agrees to try and persuade Isran to let her help. Once again, you will have to do the talking, although Isran will be his usual paranoid self: ''"All right, you've heard what it has to say. Now tell me, is there any reason I shouldn't kill this bloodsucking fiend right now?"'' Regardless of your choice, Isran will agree to let Serana help out, but will turn to Serana and let her know: ''"Don't feel like a guest, because you're not. You're a resource. You're an asset. In the meantime, don't make me regret my sudden outburst of tolerance and generosity, because if you do, your friend here is going to pay for it."'' While Serana can't help but make fun of Isran's anger, she will turn to you and remind you that she carries the Elder Scroll on her back and that it is necessary to read it to understand the prophecy. The only people who can read the scrolls are the blind [[Lore:Cult_of_the_Ancestor_Moth|Moth Priests]] who live in the [[Lore:Imperial City|Imperial City]] in [[Lore:Cyrodiil|Cyrodiil]], a long way from Skyrim. Luckily, Isran noticed an Imperial scholar passing by on the road just a few days ago. He is unwilling to waste men looking for him, but suggests that you ask innkeepers or carriage drivers all over Skyrim. Serana, however, suggests the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (place)|College of Winterhold]] as a place where a scholar would go. Either way, Serana feels adventurous and will be your follower on the search for the scholar. ===Searching for the Priest=== You will face three different options, either asking the numerous [[Skyrim:Carriage|carriage drivers]] parked all over Skyrim, asking the innkeepers in the various cities, or taking a trip to the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (place)|College of Winterhold]]. It is also possible to just wander around Skyrim; if you come to the area south of Dragon Bridge where the Moth Priest was kidnapped from, then you can continue on with the quest even if you haven't done this part. If you hurry, you might catch him there.''" |} ===The Ambush at Dragon Bridge=== [[File:SR-quest-Prophet_(Dawnguard)_02.jpg|thumb|right|The ambush]] With all clues pointing to the small settlement of [[Skyrim:Dragon Bridge|Dragon Bridge]], travel there and ask the locals if they have seen a Moth Priest. Some will not even have the topic, while others will claim they know nothing about a traveling priest. [[Skyrim:Azzada Lylvieve|Azzada]] and [[Skyrim:Michel Lylvieve|Michel Lylvieve]] will both suggest talking to a guard: ''"A Moth Priest? I'm sorry, but I don't know anything about that. Try asking one of the guards."'' Following their advice and asking a local guard will have him say: ''"Ah, so that was a Moth Priest, then? He rode through town not long ago with an escort of soldiers. They didn't stop, just headed south across the Dragon Bridge."'' The only other person who ever noticed a caravan traveling through town is young [[Skyrim:Clinton Lylvieve|Clinton Lylvieve]], who will tell you: ''"I don't know what a Moth Priest is, but I did see an old man in a robe not long ago. He was riding in a wagon with some Imperial guards. They didn't stop to visit, though. They rode through town heading south, and went across the big bridge. It was only just a little bit ago. I bet you can catch them if you hurry up."'' Head southeast out of town and cross the old bridge. Stay on the path and before long you will see signs of a roadside attack, an overturned cart, a dead [[Skyrim:Horse|horse]], a bloodstained [[Skyrim:Corpse|corpse]], a copy of the book ''[[Skyrim:Effects of the Elder Scrolls|Effects of the Elder Scrolls]]'', and a dead [[Skyrim:Vampire|vampire]]. Examine the vampire and read the [[Skyrim:Vampire's Note|vampire's note]]. The note points you towards a place named [[Skyrim:Forebears' Holdout|Forebears' Holdout]], apparently where the attackers dragged the Moth Priest. Follow the bloodstains over the bridge to the east until you reach yet another attacked cart, with two corpses: a [[Skyrim:Redguard (dead)|Redguard]] and a [[Skyrim:Nord (dead)|Nord]]. Follow the blood spatters to the northeast until you reach five standing stones, and the entrance to Forebears' Holdout. === Forebears' Holdout=== [[File:SR-quest-Prophet_(Dawnguard)_03.jpg|thumb|right|''"The more you fight me, the more you will suffer, mortal."'']] [[File:SR-quest-Prophet_(Dawnguard)_04.jpg|thumb|right|''"I serve my master's will."'']] Head down the slope and around the corner. Before long you will land on a balcony in a huge chamber with a river, and what resembles an old interior fort with a patrolling vampire, and a bluish orb glowing on the other side. Sneak down the stairs to the south and watch out for two patrolling [[Skyrim:Death Hound|death hounds]] on the ground level. Cross the narrow bridge leading west and follow the wall until an opening reveals a huge bonfire. You will likely be detected by two vampires and two of their thralls, so dispose of them and make use of Serana as she is quite strong with her ranged attacks. Head up the stairs where [[Skyrim:Malkus|Malkus]], the author of the note, will be busy trying to enthrall the imprisoned priest. '''Malkus''': ''"The more you fight me, the more you will suffer, mortal."''
'''Priest''': ''"I will resist you, monster. I must!"''
'''Malkus''': ''"How much longer can you keep this up, Moth Priest? Your mind was strong, but you're exhausted from the struggle."''
'''Priest''': ''"Must... resist..."''
'''Malkus''': ''"Yes, I can feel your defenses crumbling. You want it to end. You want to give in to me. Now, acknowledge me as your master!"''
'''Priest''': ''"Yes. {{sic|master|Master|description=lowercase letter}}."'' Dispose of Malkus and claim the [[Skyrim:Weystone Focus|Weystone Focus]] from his corpse. Follow the marker up the stairs and activate the Weystone Source with the Focus you took from Malkus. The magical barrier will disappear and reveal the Moth Priest, although not in the state you expected. Instead, he will chant: ''"I serve my master's will. But my master is dead, and his enemies will pay!"'' The enthralled priest will then attack with everything he has got, so fight him until he yields. He will then stutter: ''"That... that wasn't me you were fighting. I could see through my eyes, but I could not control my actions. Thank you for breaking that foul vampire's hold over me."'' You can now ask him several questions, but first he will introduce himself: ''"I'm quite alright, thanks to you. [[Skyrim:Dexion Evicus|Dexion Evicus]] is my name. I'm a Moth Priest of the White Gold Tower. These vampires claimed they had some purpose in store for me, but they wouldn't say what. Probably hoping to ransom me, the fools. Now tell me, whom do you represent, and what do you want with me?"'' When you introduce yourself as a member of the Dawnguard, and that you need him to read an Elder Scroll, he will prove quite knowledgeable: ''"You have an Elder Scroll? Remarkable! If my knowledge of history serves me, I recall that the Dawnguard was an ancient order of vampire hunters. I will be happy to assist you with your Elder Scroll. Just tell me where I need to go."'' When you tell him to go to Fort Dawnguard, he will immediately be on his way and you are to report back to Isran. Before leaving, loot the chest nearby then exit the same way you came. ===The Elder Scroll=== When you return to [[Skyrim:Fort Dawnguard|Fort Dawnguard]], you will find Dexion Evicus in the main chamber, facing Isran. Isran will confirm that Dexion has the Elder Scroll and is ready to start reading it. When you speak to the priest he will prove to be overwhelmed with joy: ''"Ah, my rescuer! It's good to see you again. It's not exactly the hospitality I'm used to, but your man Isran has seen to my needs well enough. And might I add, this is a remarkable fortress. I have colleagues back home that would love to study this place in detail."'' When you tell him to read the Elder Scroll he will begin: [[File:SR-quest-Prophet_(Dawnguard).jpg|thumb|right|''"Among the night's children, a dread lord will rise."'']]
'''''Now, if everyone will please be quiet, I must concentrate.'''''
'''''I see a vision before me, an image of a great bow. I know this weapon! It is Auriel's Bow!'''''
'''''Now a voice whispers, saying "Among the night's children, a dread lord will rise."'''''
'''''In an age of strife, when dragons return to the realm of men, darkness will mingle with light and the night and day will be as one.'''''
'''''The voice fades and the words begin to shimmer and distort. But wait, there is more here.'''''
'''''The secret of the bow's power is written elsewhere. I think there is more to the prophecy, recorded in other scrolls.'''''
'''''Yes, I see them now... One contains the ancient secrets of the dragons, and the other speaks of the potency of ancient blood.'''''
'''''My vision darkens, and I see no more.'''''
'''''To know the complete prophecy, we must have the other two scrolls.'''''
This ends the quest and starts the next three quests, [[Skyrim:Chasing Echoes|Chasing Echoes]], [[Skyrim:Scroll Scouting|Scroll Scouting]] and [[Skyrim:Seeking Disclosure|Seeking Disclosure]]. {{NewRight}} ==Notes== * After rescuing the Moth Priest and returning to Fort Dawnguard all the ordinary Dawnguard members will start greeting you as a friend, and become available as followers. Also, at the same time, if you are not already [[Skyrim:Blood-Kin|Blood-Kin]] to the Orcs, [[Skyrim:Durak|Durak]] will grant you that status, which will immediately grant you access to all [[Skyrim:Orc Strongholds|Orc Strongholds]]. ** The Dawnguard members who patrol [[Skyrim:Dayspring Canyon|Dayspring Canyon]] ([[Skyrim:Mogrul (Dawnguard)|Mogrul]], [[Skyrim:Ollrod|Ollrod]], [[Skyrim:Tilde|Tilde]], and [[Skyrim:Vori|Vori]]) won't be affected. ** The Blood-Kin reward won't apply if you're an Orc, as they always have access to Orc Strongholds by default. The ability to recruit Durak as a follower, however, will. * If you pickpocket the Weystone Focus and activate the Weystone Source without being detected, the Moth Priest will be freed and immediately attack the surrounding vampires. After defeating them, he will still be aggressive towards you, but he should then have significantly less health and be an easier fight. * If Serana raises a Thrall that survives the battle, it may begin to sleep in one of the coffins after your conversation with Dexion is finished. * Once Dexion is set free, the [[Skyrim:Elk|elk]] outside the cave entrance will immediately respawn once you and Serana exit. * When Dexion reads Serana's [[Skyrim:Elder Scroll (Sun)|Scroll]], it can also still be seen on her back. * After Serana has told you to locate a Moth Priest, you can speak with Gunmar and he'll give you some [[Skyrim:Dawnguard Armor|Dawnguard Armor]] pieces. * Serana will not automatically become your follower if you don't speak to her about where to find a Moth Priest, or if you have another follower with you. * Once your initial conversations with Isran and Serana are finished, it is possible to talk to [[Skyrim:Sorine Jurard|Sorine Jurard]] and start the [[Skyrim:Bolstering the Ranks|Bolstering the Ranks]] quest to rescue [[Skyrim:Florentius Baenius|Florentius Baenius]] and return him to [[Skyrim:Fort Dawnguard|Fort Dawnguard]] before finishing this one, so he can also be present when Dexion reads the Scroll. ==Bugs== {{Bug|If Dexion is outside of the magic barrier when you first see him, or if you manage to speak with him and tell him to meet you at Fort Dawnguard before he becomes hostile towards you, he ends up becoming permanently hostile after that point.|UDGP|2.0.1|dlc=DG}} **Reloading and making sure he is in the magic barrier, then playing the quest sequence in the proper order (rescue, defeat, then speak to him) will resolve this. **It is also possible to use [[Skyrim:Bend Will|Bend Will]]{{DB}} on Dexion if you've got two or more words of the shout to let him stop attacking everyone. **If reloading does not get Dexion to spawn inside the magic barrier, it is also possible to complete the quest by simply ''not'' interacting with the magic barrier. You can defeat the vampires and send Dexion to Fort Dawnguard without him ever turning hostile. ==Quick Walkthrough==
'''Note''': This quest does not appear in your journal.
# Encounter the regretful [[Skyrim:Subjugated Ghost|ghosts]] outside [[Skyrim:Rannveig's Fast|Rannveig's Fast]].
# Fall into the [[Skyrim:Trap Door|trap]] of a [[Skyrim:Sild the Warlock|sadistic warlock]] '''or''' (optional) sneak behind the warlock for an ambush attack.
# Claim the treasure and learn a word for the [[Skyrim:Kyne's Peace|Kyne's Peace]] [[Skyrim:Dragon Shouts|shout]].

==Detailed Walkthrough==
===The Ghosts of Rannveig's Fast===
The [[Skyrim:Nordic Ruins|Nordic ruin]] called [[Skyrim:Rannveig's Fast|Rannveig's Fast]] is located in the wilderness south and slightly to the west of [[Skyrim:Morthal|Morthal]], not far from the shores of [[Skyrim:River Hjaal|River Hjaal]]. No road will take you there, so either follow the river or take a shortcut through [[Skyrim:Cold Rock Pass|Cold Rock Pass]] to reach the ruin. The exterior is quite large and guarded by some rather unusual [[Skyrim:Subjugated Ghost|Subjugated Ghosts]] and a single [[Skyrim:Ghost Adventurer|Ghost Adventurer]], all of whom will apologize for attacking you. You can either choose to put them out of their misery or simply enter the ruin, as they will not follow you inside.

===The Setup===
The door opens to a huge chamber with the sky visible above and the floor overgrown with ferns. Proceed north and you will meet another subjugated ghost, who is unwilling to attack you but forced to by unknown powers. The next huge chamber has another regretful ghost wandering around. There are several paths to choose: the locked southern door leads to a small chamber with a minor loot chest, while the northern door will offer an alternate route to discover the secrets of the ruin. The most tempting option will obviously be the chiming [[Skyrim:Word Wall|word wall]] to the east, with a huge glowing chest in front.
{{Quest Fork
|imageL=SR-quest-Rannveig's Fast 02.jpg
|imageR=SR-quest-Rannveig's Fast 03.jpg
|captionL=''"This is actually going to hurt a lot."''
|captionR=''"This one didn't survive the fall either."''
|titleL=Falling Down
|titleR=Ambush
|textL=
If you walk directly toward the word wall and the glowing chest, the darkened part of the walkway will turn out to be a cleverly hidden [[Skyrim:Trap Door|trap door]] and you will fall down to another level through another trap door until you finally land inside a locked cage. Here you find yourself surrounded by the bodies of dead [[Skyrim:Bandit|bandits]] floating in knee-deep water. Outside the cage, Sild the Warlock will be wandering around and will be pleasantly surprised by yet another rat in the trap: ''"Ooooh...yes...yes. You've fallen for my trap! Greed makes a great lure. Odd you didn't die from the fall though. Most do."'' Due to your unexpected, but most welcome survival, he will start messing around the chamber, looking for something with which he can dispose of you as quickly as possible, so he can subjugate you as part of his army of ghosts. When he finally locates his desired item he will say: ''"Ah...Here it is. Now, if you'd be so kind as to stand still this will be much easier for me to do. Oh, and I wasn't entirely truthful before. This is actually going to hurt a lot. You see, you have to be dead in order for the spell to take hold."'' Sild will then proceed to cast [[Skyrim:Oakflesh|Oakflesh]] on himself and then shower you with [[Skyrim:Flames|flames]] or [[Skyrim:Firebolt|firebolts]]. Without resorting to dragon shouts from inside the cage, there are three ways to get out and fight Sild face-to-face. First, you can examine the dead bandits in the water; one of them has ten [[Skyrim:Lockpick|lockpicks]]. Alternatively, search the [[Skyrim:Satchel|satchel]] found just to the left on the cage door. It contains the [[Skyrim:Rannveigs Fast Key|key]] to the door. Lastly, when your health is almost down to zero, Sild will open the cage himself to finish you off.
|textR=
If you manage to resist the temptation of the word wall and the glowing chest, the northern tunnel leads to a closed gate with a handle visible on the other side. Go south from the gate and up two sets of stairs until you reach a handle. The western path leads to the overhead bridges above the huge chamber and a room with another subjugated ghost and some minor loot, including a locked chest and a [[Skyrim:Diamond|diamond]] in the hands of a dead [[Skyrim:Bandit|bandit]]. Backtrack to the handle, pull it, and head downstairs to the iron gate, which will now be raised. Fight another ghost and take the only available path into the depths of the ruin. You will see a wooden door, but that will be your escape route so skip that for now and follow the voice coming from the western chamber, preferably using [[Skyrim:Sneak|Sneak]] to avoid detection. Before long you will see Sild the Warlock wandering restlessly around in his chamber, waiting for yet another victim to fall for his glowing chest-trap, mumbling to himself: ''"Come on! You know you want what's in that chest. Just walk toward it!"'', ''"Just walk toward the chest! Gravity will do the rest."'' and ''"I know you're up there. Go get the treasure. Doesn't it look pretty?"'' If you wait long enough, an [[Skyrim:Bandit (dead)#Orc Male|Orc bandit]] will take the bait and fall down in the chamber, dying immediately. A frustrated Sild will comment: ''"Well...that's disappointing. This one didn't survive the fall either. No matter. Another one will be along any time now."'' He will then keep wandering around the cage, hoping for more victims, but nothing else will happen. Note that Sild is hard to sneak up on, so just get as close to him as possible, then fight and kill him.}}

===The Truth About Sild===
After battling Sild, make sure to claim the [[Skyrim:Rannveigs Fast Key|key]] if you haven't picked it up already. Notice the dead body of [[Skyrim: Sild's Assistant|Sild's assistant]] near the cage, then examine the chamber for answers. The rows of cages contain more dead bandits, a dead [[Skyrim:Dog|dog]], a dead [[Skyrim:Wood Elf (dead)|Wood Elf]], and a dead [[Skyrim:Breton (dead)|Breton]]. Most importantly, examine the table next to the [[Skyrim:Alchemy Lab|Alchemy Lab]] for ''[[Skyrim:Sild's Journal|Sild's Journal]]'' to learn the truth of Sild's sadistic activities. Lastly, unlock the boss-leveled chest for your reward, and check the table for an [[Skyrim:Unusual Gem|Unusual Gem]] and the [[Skyrim:Destruction|Destruction]] skill book ''[[Skyrim:Horror of Castle Xyr|Horror of Castle Xyr]]''. When all is said and done, head east and, when you reach the wooden door, open it and head south. In the last room, a door leads outside to a small ledge east of the main entrance.

==Notes==
* Learning the word of Kyne's Peace can be done after or before confronting Sild. The trap door is before the word wall, but you can either walk on the edge of the floor or jump over the trap door making it possible to run past the door without falling down.

{{Cleanup-srqrp |writtenBy=Krusty |checkedBy= |reward=Krusty |rewardChecked= }}{{Mod Header|Dragonborn}}{{Trail2|Dragonborn|Quests|link2=Dragonborn Quests|Side Quests}}[[Category:Skyrim-Quests]]{{Quest Header |notrail=1 |type=Side Quests |Giver=[[Skyrim:Bujold the Unworthy|Bujold the Unworthy]] |Reward=Master trainer in [[Skyrim:Heavy Armor|Heavy Armor]] |Disp= |Rep= |Prev= |Conc= |Next= |Loc=[[Skyrim:Bujold's Retreat|Bujold's Retreat]], [[Skyrim:Thirsk Mead Hall|Thirsk Mead Hall]], [[Skyrim:Hrothmund's Barrow|Hrothmund's Barrow]] |Image=SR-quest-Retaking Thirsk.jpg |ImgDesc=The assault on [[Skyrim:Thirsk Mead Hall|Thirsk Mead Hall]] |description=Help [[Skyrim:Bujold the Unworthy|Bujold the Unworthy]] retake [[Skyrim:Thirsk Mead Hall|Thirsk Mead Hall]]. * Not available if you chose to assist the rieklings and become the Riekling Chief in [[Skyrim:The Chief of Thirsk Hall|The Chief of Thirsk Hall]]. [[Skyrim:Bujold the Unworthy|Bujold the Unworthy]] is killed during the assault on [[Skyrim:Bujold's Retreat|Bujold's Retreat]] in the closing stages of [[Skyrim:The Chief of Thirsk Hall|The Chief of Thirsk Hall]]. |ID=DLC2MH01 |Icon=SR-qico-Miscellaneous.png }} == Quick Walkthrough == # Speak to [[Skyrim:Bujold the Unworthy|Bujold the Unworthy]] in [[Skyrim:Bujold's Retreat|Bujold's Retreat]]. # Join the assault on Thirsk Mead Hall and defeat the rieklings. # Meet her at [[Skyrim:Hrothmund's Barrow|Hrothmund's Barrow]]. # Listen to her interaction with [[Skyrim:Hrothmund|Hrothmund's spirit]]. # Keep her secret, kill her, or betray her to Kuvar. == Detailed Walkthrough == ===Exiled Warriors=== [[Lore:Thirsk|Thirsk]], the legendary mead hall founded in the [[Lore:Third Era|Third Era]] by [[Lore:Hrothmund the Red|Hrothmund the Red]] of the [[Lore:Skaal|Skaal]], was built for [[Lore:Nord|Nord]] warriors who wanted to live, hunt, and fight in the wilderness, the old way. When you visit [[Skyrim:Thirsk Mead Hall|Thirsk Mead Hall]], it is clear that the mead hall has seen better days, as it is currently inhabited by [[Skyrim:Riekling|rieklings]], without a single proud Nord in sight. Head east from the Hall and locate [[Skyrim:Bujold's Retreat|Bujold's Retreat]], where you will find the former Nord inhabitants, clearly exiled from their own Hall and quite frustrated and embarrassed. As you enter the camp, you will witness a heated discussion between [[Skyrim:Bujold the Unworthy|Bujold]] and [[Skyrim:Kuvar|Kuvar]]: [[File:SR-quest-Retaking Thirsk 05.jpg|thumb|right|''"We'll act when I say we do and not before."'']] '''Bujold''': ''"It won't be that easy to get rid of the Rieklings, Kuvar."''
'''Kuvar''': ''"I never said it would be. But either way, we have to try. Whether we succeed or not, it'll stir up some of the old blood in this crowd."''
'''Bujold''': ''"I'm not going to lead them to their deaths if they aren't ready."''
'''Kuvar''': ''"Then train them. What are we doing here? We should either get used to staying here, or be preparing to retake the hall. You're having us do neither, and I can't stomach it."''
'''Bujold''': ''"Your stomach isn't my problem. We'll act when I say we do and not before."''
'''Kuvar''': ''"Well, you'd better say something. And soon."'' Talking to the other residents reveals that everyone is unhappy about living in the remote camp, instead of the cozy warmth they are used to in the Hall. If you seek out Kuvar, he will explain it: ''"We brought ourselves out here, along with our shame. We used to be proud warriors of Thirsk Mead Hall. There, up on the hill. But we let that sweet life get the better of us. We grew soft, and..."'' He then tells you what happened: ''"Rieklings. Those filthy vermin... they came in numbers. Waves of the things. One at a time, they're pests, but with this many... And so here we are, out of our home."'' ===The Unworthy=== Locate the leader with the unflattering byname, Bujold the Unworthy, and ask her what is going on. Like Kuvar, she will be painfully honest: ''"What's going on here is that we've been kicked out of our home."'' She then proceeds to explain that rieklings took over the Hall and will explain how the mighty warriors lost the battle against the small vermin: ''"With tenacity and numbers. Didn't help that we'd grown a little too comfortable up there. Too much mead. Too many stories. Too few battles."'' While it is clear that the Nords drank themselves out of their home, ask her if she needs any help and she will gladly accept and reason that ''"Some new blood should be enough to rouse these layabouts to actually fight again."'' At this point, consider completing [[Skyrim:Elmus Favor Quest (mead)|a favor quest]] for camp inhabitant [[Skyrim:Elmus|Elmus]] (it becomes unavailable once this quest is started) - and consider if you want to help the Nords or not, as you will miss out on the quest [[Skyrim:The Chief of Thirsk Hall|The Chief of Thirsk Hall]]. ===Retaking Thirsk=== As soon as you agree to help the Nords, the quest will initiate and Bujold will gather her warriors with the words: ''"Hey, you lazy milk-drinkers, get over here! I know you're all starting to settle in here, and keep up the fat lives you got used to up in the hall. But look here. This outsider has more fire than any of you. All I had to do was mention our little infestation, and he/she volunteered in a second! I don't want to have my spirit outstripped by some wanderer. So let's get up there and kill us some Rieklings!"'' After the speech, all the warriors will draw weapons and set off at a running pace towards Thirsk Mead Hall, determined to reclaim it and wipe out the rieklings. You will have no choice but to tag along and fight a total of nineteen angry rieklings defending their new property. A total of six rieklings will defend the exterior while the rest will be inside, doing everything they can to protect their property, including the [[Skyrim:Riekling Chief|riekling chief]] himself. The chief can only be wounded by the Nords to the point where he drops into the recovery position; it falls to you to finish him off. When all is said and done and dead rieklings lie everywhere in the Hall, locate Bujold who will be exhilarated by the battle and ask how you feel. Regardless of your answer, she will ask you to be her 'second' for a journey, as she needs to get another blessing from [[Lore:Hrothmund the Red|Hrothmund the Red]] before the Nords again take up residence in the Hall. ===Hrothmund's Barrow=== Bujold will lead you to a Nordic ruin called [[Skyrim:Hrothmund's Barrow|Hrothmund's Barrow]], southwest of [[Skyrim:Benkongerike|Benkongerike]]. Near the entrance she will turn around and ask you whether you are ready or not. You can then ask her what this place is and she will explain the full background: ''"The burial place of Hrothmund, who founded Thirsk. He brought a group of true warriors away from the soft life of the Skaal, to know the wilderness, to feel the sting of cold and of steel. I know that... sounds a little silly. It's just the way it's written in the books, and that phrase has always stuck with me."'' She will also explain what will happen in the barrow: ''"It's pretty simple. Hrothmund's axe is in there with him. Anyone who attempts to take hold of it has their spirit judged by Hrothmund himself."'' She will then reveal that she is quite confident that she will receive Hrothmund's blessing once again. After all, she received it before. ===The Spirit of Hrothmund=== Inside the barrow, head through the first empty chamber and enter a huge water-filled room. As you approach, the water will disappear, and the now-visible path will lead you right to Hrothmund's Axe, where Bujold will try and grab it, as per tradition. When she does, [[Skyrim:Hrothmund|Hrothmund's spirit]] will speak: [[File:SR-quest-Retaking Thirsk 02.jpg|thumb|right|''"Then... the leadership is not mine?"'']] '''Hrothmund''': ''"You seek my blessing for the leadership of Thirsk Hall?"''
'''Bujold''': ''"I do. It is I, Bujold. You blessed me in the past, and now I've rid the hall of Rieklings and returned it to its rightful owners."''
'''Hrothmund''': ''"And well it is that this has happened. But I have always watched, and know that it was your softness that led to your own exile."''
'''Bujold''': ''"No! I..."''
'''Hrothmund''': ''"You allowed your fellow warriors to grow weak while the dangers around you mounted."''
'''Bujold''': ''"Then... the leadership is not mine?"''
'''Hrothmund''': ''"No. Nor is there any among you fit to serve. For a band in the wilderness, it is better to have no leader than a poor one."''
'''Hrothmund''': Go forth and seek your fortunes. Inhabit the hall as you may. In time, a true leader worthy of the Thirsk name may arise."''
'''Hrothmund''': But I see that new leader's coming is yet far off in the distant horizon."'' After her conversation with Hrothmund, an embarrassed Bujold will approach you and two options will be available, although both will lead to Bujold making the decision to return to Thirsk Mead Hall and continue her leadership as if Hrothmund had given his blessing. She will explain why: ''"No matter what Hrothmund says, we need a leader. And I'm still the best person for that."'' When you point out that she goes against Hrothmund's wishes she will continue: ''"Look what's happened to us so far under his watchful eye. He gave his blessing to all the leaders who brought us to this point. Anyway, he's dead and we're alive. It's time to begin a new tradition for Thirsk. And I'm going to do that. All I need is for you to back me up. You don't even need to lie... just don't tell anyone else what you heard here."'' {{NewRight}}{{SkyrimBox|main-color=#FBEFD5|text-color=black|style=margin:8px auto;|text='''Your next decision will make a huge difference for Bujold and maybe even cost you a few useful relationships within Thirsk Mead Hall.''' With Bujold determined to keep leading the mead hall regardless of Hrothmund's wishes, you must decide whether to intervene and end her leadership. After she tells you her plan, you will have two options: '''NOTE''': The quest will end right after you make the decision, and no reward will be given, so think carefully what benefits you the most: your relationship with [[Skyrim:Kuvar|Kuvar]] or the old Nord traditions of Hrothmund. }} {{Quest Fork |imageL=SR-quest-Retaking Thirsk 04.jpg |imageR=SR-quest-Retaking Thirsk 03.jpg |titleL=Follow Bujold |titleR=Follow Hrothmund |captionL=''"Get out of here. Run to the wilds."'' |captionR=Bujold attacks |textL= If you choose to accept Bujold's scheme, she will simply end the quest and walk away with the words: ''"Good. See that you do. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a hall to lead."'' When you return to Thirsk Mead Hall, Bujold will wander around carrying a new name, specifically Bujold the Intrepid. As soon as you enter, Kuvar will approach you and say: ''"Bujold says you served well. Before we were married, I was her second on the first trip to the barrow. Hrothmund knows strength, in this world and the next."'' You can either tell him the truth, that she was rejected by Hrothmund, or lie, saying that it was an honor to accompany her. Think twice before choosing, because Kuvar is a master [[Skyrim:Trainers|trainer]] in [[Skyrim:Heavy Armor|Heavy Armor]]: '''TRUTH''': ''"I don't think you know how dangerous it is to say what you've just said. This is a serious accusation. I'm sure Bujold can straighten it out for us.."'' He will then seek out Bujold and demand to hear the truth. Bujold will be taken by surprise by your betrayal and will admit everything, much to the regret of her husband. The argument ends with a heartbroken Kuvar asking Bujold to leave Thirsk and run to the wilds. Trying to talk to Kuvar further will reveal that he now holds a grudge towards you for separating him from his wife, meaning that he will no longer offer training. '''LIE''': ''"Yes, I remember how I felt being there with her the first time, before we were wed. I hope to see you more around the hall, friend."'' He will then continue his daily routine and will offer training. |textR= If you choose to follow ancient Nord tradition and say: ''"I can't let you lead Thirsk."'', Bujold will be quite sad when she says: ''"I was afraid you might say that. Well, looks as though I'll have to prove my mettle against you now."'' She will then draw her [[Skyrim:Nordic War Axe|war axe]] and proceed to attack in order to keep her secret. Once she is dead, the quest will finish and Thirsk will be left without a leader. A return to the now cleaned-up mead hall will net you a concerned Kuvar who demands to know what happened to his wife: ''"How did things go out there? Where is Bujold?"'' You can then choose to tell the truth, that she was rejected, or lie and tell him you don't know what happened to her. Think twice before choosing, because he is a master [[Skyrim:Trainers|trainer]] in [[Skyrim:Heavy Armor|Heavy Armor]]: '''TRUTH''': ''"Are you being serious? How... how did she take it?"'' When you tell him she attacked you, he will respond: ''"Ah. I see. I hope she... fought well. Was it... did Hrothmund recognize anyone else? Was it you? Is that why..."'' When you tell him that Hrothmund said the next leader is a long way off, he will accept this, although he will refuse to speak to you again: ''"Well, then. I'll do my best to keep the hall together until that day comes. Now, look... I understand you were just defending yourself. And because you helped us retake the hall, I'll look past it this once. But I wouldn't show my face in here again, if I were you. Do we understand each other?"'' Trying to talk to Kuvar further will reveal that he now holds a grudge towards you for separating him from his wife, meaning that he will no longer offer training. '''LIE''': ''"Well, let's hope she makes it back soon. This lot doesn't have much patience with me."'' He will then continue his daily routine and will offer training.}} ==Notes== * Should you choose to tell Bujold that you will keep her secret, then tell Kuvar the truth, Bujold will be disabled and disappear from the game as soon as she leaves Thirsk Mead Hall. * If you delay too long in responding to Bujold after her conversation with the spirit of Hrothmund the quest will autocomplete (advance to stage 200) as if you had agreed with her actions. * Once the warriors have cleaned up the mead hall, three new favor quests will be available. His current steward is named [[Skyrim:Varona Nelas|Varona Nelas]] and is constantly challenged by the demanding wizard, who has a weak spot for tea brewed from [[Skyrim:Canis Root|canis root]]. Once you have spoken with Varona and left Tel Mithryn at least once, she will be nowhere to be found. Pay a visit to Neloth in his [[Skyrim:Tel Mithryn (tower)|tower]] and he will wander around saying: ''"Where is that ash sucking steward of mine? Varona!"'' As it turns out, the wizard is quite hungry and will task you with finding Varona: ''"Well find her. Tell her I want apple cabbage stew, with some canis root tea."'' He will not take 'no' for an answer, regardless of which option you choose: [[File:SR-quest-Reluctant-Steward 02.jpg|thumb|right|''"Where is that ash sucking steward of mine?"'']] '''Why don't you just make your own tea?'''
''"What? Make my own tea? I am a master wizard of the House Telvanni. Other people make tea for me."'' '''Hey, I'm not your servant.'''
''"Obviously not, or you would have a cup of tea in your hands. I supposed you want to be asked nicely. Very well. Please, oh hero of Skyrim. Please find Varona. I shall be ever so grateful."'' '''Of course, Master Neloth. As you command.'''
''"Finally. Someone who recognizes my importance around here."'' Neloth will then return to his daily routine and you will have no choice but to search for the missing steward. No map marker will be provided, so look around for the other inhabitants of the settlement. ===Ash Spawn Attack=== Outside, Neloth's apprentice [[Skyrim:Talvas Fathryon|Talvas Fathryon]] will refuse to talk about Varona until you complete his quest [[Skyrim:From the Ashes|From the Ashes]]. Even so, he will point you towards local apothecary [[Skyrim:Elynea Mothren|Elynea Mothren]] for information. Alternatively, you can talk to [[Skyrim:Ulves Romoran|Ulves Romoran]] inside [[Skyrim:Tel Mithryn Kitchen|Tel Mithryn Kitchen]]. Both he and Elynea will tell you that Varona just departed for [[Skyrim:Raven Rock|Raven Rock]] in order to gather supplies. Bringing this information to Neloth will net you nothing, as he only cares if his tea is hot or not. After speaking to Elynea or Ulves, a map marker will now point you towards Varona who will most likely (see [[#Bugs|bugs]]) be in the area west of the [[Skyrim:Sun Stone|Sun Stone]], not far from a dead [[Skyrim:Reaver|reaver]]. Unfortunately, she never made it to Raven Rock as she was killed by three [[Skyrim:Ash Spawn|ash spawn]], all of them still gathered around her dead body. Kill the ash spawn and investigate her body for a quest update. ===A Popular Wizard=== Back in his tower, Neloth will have a hard time showing any emotion when you tell him the sad news: ''"Dead? Well that's annoying. How did she die?"'' When you tell him about the ash spawn attack, he will reflect a bit but will quickly get over it: ''"There are more and more of those things showing up around here lately. I suppose you'll have to find me a new steward. Try Raven Rock. They are in awe of me there. I'm sure almost anyone would be willing to serve me."'' Three options will be available and the two top options will always lead to the third: [[File:SR-quest-Reluctant-Steward 03.jpg|thumb|right|''"Try [[Skyrim:Raven Rock|Raven Rock]]. They are in awe of me there."'']] '''You can't just order me around.'''
''"Well, somebody needs to get me a new steward. It might as well be you. But if you don't want to help a master wizard of House Telvanni, possibly earning his favor, you're a fool."'' '''What's in it for me? '''
''"So gaining the favor of a Telvanni wizard isn't enough? I suppose I'll have to pay you. Heroes. They get greedier every century."'' '''What kind of a person should I look for?'''
''"Hmm. Excellent question. Once word gets out, there will be a lot of people to choose from. Someone with a brilliant mind and robust physique that is blindly obedient would be ideal. Oh, and they need to know how to brew tea. Ulves always waters it down."'' Once again, you will have to obey orders, so travel to Raven Rock, where a huge amount of the [[Skyrim:Raven Rock#Raven Rock People|citizens]] will have an extra dialogue option, namely to consider a position as Neloth's new steward. ===Unexpected Reactions=== When you begin asking the inhabitants of Raven Rock if they want a new job as Neloth's personal steward, it soon becomes quite clear that the wizard may have overestimated both his reputation and popularity, as shown in the table below: {|class="wikitable sortable" !Name !!House !! Besides, Neloth is a madman!"'' |} [[File:SR-quest-Reluctant Steward 04.jpg|thumb|right|''"There's got to be more to life than sweeping and cleaning all day."'']] While Neloth seems to be the laughingstock in town, three citizens will prove helpful and point you towards [[Skyrim:Drovas Relvi|Drovas Relvi]] who works as a cook at the [[Skyrim:The Retching Netch|Retching Netch]]. These citizens are [[Skyrim:Dreyla Alor|Dreyla Alor]], [[Skyrim:Geldis Sadri|Geldis Sadri]], and [[Skyrim:Glover Mallory|Glover Mallory]] (see [[#Notes|notes]]). ===The Unhappy Cook=== Drovas is quite unhappy with working at the Retching Netch, as Geldis Sedri doesn't allow him to drink on the job. When presented with the idea of acting as Neloth's new steward he will therefore accept right away: ''"Uh... you mean leave Raven Rock? For good? To go work for a crazed Telvanni wizard? Sure. Just let me get my things. On second thought, nevermind. I can get new stuff."'' Drovas will then set off at a running pace and head towards Tel Mithryn where he will begin his life anew, now a steward for Neloth. If you speak to Drovas before he leaves the inn, he will simply say ''"I'm off to take up my new position with Master Neloth."'' When you tell Neloth, he will hatefully comment: ''"That Drovas man? I suppose he'll do. He makes dreadful canis root tea though. But, I should be grateful. Here, take this for your efforts. Oh, and you may use my staff enchanter if you want."'' He will then hand you the reward, a leveled amount of gold and a [[Skyrim:Staff Enchanter Key|key]] that provides free access to his unique [[Skyrim:Staff Enchanter|Staff Enchanter]] in the locked southern chamber. The chamber also holds his [[Lore:Black Book|Black Book]], ''[[Skyrim:Black Book: The Hidden Twilight (book)|Hidden Twilight]]''. Lastly, you can now hear the eccentric wizard calling for his steward: ''"Where is that lazy steward of mine? Varona! No, wait. She's dead. Drovas!"'' You can also ask Neloth how Drovas is doing, and he will respond: ''"The man makes a dreadful cup of canis root tea. However, he seems run the place well enough. Oh. Were you fishing for a compliment? A sign of gratitude? Don't waste your time. Those things are for the weak and foolish."'' You can also ask Drovas how things are going, and his response will be: ''"Neloth is a real task master. And the tea. The thrice damned tea! I don't think I'll ever learn to make it properly."'' ==Notes== * Drovas' eagerness to accept the position also seems driven by a desire to escape a debt owed to [[Skyrim:Mogrul (Dragonborn)|Mogrul]], a debt that you are now [[Skyrim:A New Debt|expected to pay]]. Be prepared for a confrontation the next time you return to Raven Rock. * If you start the quest by examining the dead body of Varona, Neloth will instead say: ''"What! Who's going to make my tea? Why do these things always happen to me? Well, don't just stand there. Go find me another steward. I'm sure there's plenty of people in Raven Rock to choose from."'' He will then send you to Raven Rock (start the walkthrough from [[#Unexpected_Reactions|this section]]). * Glover Mallory will only help you find a new steward if you have completed [[Skyrim:Meet the Family|Meet the Family]]. * After the quest, you'll no longer be able to ask Drovas if he wants to test out [[Skyrim:Sadri's Sujamma|Sadri's Sujamma]] if [[Skyrim:It's All In The Taste|It's All In The Taste]] is active. * This quest is normally a prerequisite for [[Skyrim:Put A Fork In It|Put A Fork In It]]{{CC|Staff of Sheogorath}} and [[Skyrim:The Arms of Chaos|The Arms of Chaos]]{{CC|Arms of Chaos}} due to the requirement to use the Staff Enchanter during those quests. However, you can avoid this quest if you have access to a Staff Enchanter elsewhere, such as the one added by the [[Skyrim:Myrwatch|Myrwatch]] Creation. ==Bugs== {{Bug|If this quest is finished and the [[Skyrim:Sun Stone|Sun Stone]] has been cleansed, Drovas's sleep package will always be active, and therefore he will be found sleeping indefinitely in [[Skyrim:Tel Mithryn Steward's House|Tel Mithryn Steward's House]].|UDBP|1.0.5}} {{Bug|Varona will sometimes not end up dead in her intended place, but instead somewhere around Tel Mithryn. == Quick Walkthrough ==
# Speak to [[Skyrim:Captain Veleth|Captain Veleth]].
# Find the hidden stash of [[Skyrim:Emberbrand Wine|Emberbrand Wine]] in [[Skyrim:Raven Rock|Raven Rock]].
# Return to Captain Veleth.

== Detailed Walkthrough ==
Speak to [[Skyrim:Captain Veleth|Captain Veleth]] in [[Skyrim:Raven Rock|Raven Rock]]. He tells you that he's concerned about some [[Skyrim:Emberbrand Wine|Emberbrand Wine]] being stashed by his men. He'd like you to locate the stash and report back to him. He suggests you search near any abandoned buildings in the area:
:'''Is it difficult commanding the Redoran Guard?'''
:''"It can be. Even the most experienced warriors can fall prey to petty distractions. They usually didn't amount to much, but they make my job that much harder."''
:'''Petty distractions?''' 
:''"Some of my own men have become quite accustomed to a spirit they called '[[Skyrim:Emberbrand Wine|Emberbrand Wine]].' Despise the stuff myself. It's powerful and tremendously addicting... I've seen men fail to finish even a single flask. If I knew where they were stashing the bottles, I'd put an end to it myself."'' 
:'''I could track the stash down for you.'''
:''"You would? That would be helpful. I just don't have time to do it myself right now."'' 
:'''Any idea where I can begin?'''
:''"They're too smart to have left it in the Bulwark. I'd search one of the abandoned houses on the outskirts of town."'' 

Locate the [[Skyrim:Abandoned Building|abandoned building]] in town, which is just past the [[Skyrim:Glover Mallory's House|blacksmith]]. Stay outside, and head along the road southwest of the abandoned building to find eight jars of the wine in a barrel between the foundations of two destroyed houses nearby. Return to Captain Veleth for your reward:
:'''I found the Emberbrand Wine stash.'''
:''"Good, this will help me keep things running without having to worry about a bunch of soldiers falling asleep on duty. Here, take this for your trouble."''

== Notes ==

* It is not necessary to take the wine to complete the quest - merely finding the barrel and seeing its contents is enough.  If you do take it, you can keep it for your own use.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
Upon arriving at [[Skyrim:Four Skull Lookout|Four Skull Lookout]] for the first time, you will encounter hostile bandits wearing the Relics of the Crusader and the Reforged Relics of the Crusader. The former are the holy relics of [[Lore:Pelinal Whitestrake|Pelinal Whitestrake]], while the latter are a new set of light armor pieces styled after the originals.

Four Skull Lookout is a [[Skyrim:Bandit|bandit]] den. In addition to the regular bandit enemies, [[Skyrim:Eigorn|Eigorn]], [[Skyrim:Oren|Oren]], [[Skyrim:Remy|Remy]] and [[Skyrim:Viparth|Viparth]] can be found here. They are your targets, as Eigorn and Oren possess the Relics and will use them in battle. Kill the thieves and loot all twelve of the new items from their bodies to complete the quest. You can optionally also loot [[Skyrim:Viparth's Journal|Viparth's Journal]] for some explanation as to how bandits are wearing these divine relics.

===Reward===
The items you receive from this quest are as follows:
* [[Skyrim:Mace of the Crusader|Mace of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Shield of the Crusader|Shield of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Boots of the Crusader|Boots of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Cuirass of the Crusader|Cuirass of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Gauntlets of the Crusader|Gauntlets of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Helm of the Crusader|Helm of the Crusader]]
* [[Skyrim:Sword of the Crusader|Sword of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Fastened Shield of the Crusader|Fastened Shield of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Reforged Boots of the Crusader|Reforged Boots of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Reforged Cuirass of the Crusader|Reforged Cuirass of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Reforged Gauntlets of the Crusader|Reforged Gauntlets of the Crusader]], [[Skyrim:Reforged Helm of the Crusader|Reforged Helm of the Crusader]]

If you commit any crime whatsoever, at any point in the game, you will receive a message advising that your crimes have made you unfit to wield the Crusader's Relics. Attempting to wear any of the relics after this point will result in a significant debuff to your stamina and health regeneration and your carry weight. The quest [[SR:The Pilgrim's Path|The Pilgrim's Path]] will be automatically started, directing you to nine remote [[SR:Shrines|shrines]] to repent for your sins and regain the ability to wear this equipment.

==Notes==
* At release, this quest appeared in your journal and was started automatically upon installing the [[Skyrim:Divine Crusader|Divine Crusader]] [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation]], or as soon as you left [[Skyrim:Helgen Keep|Helgen Keep]] as a new character. This was changed in the [[Skyrim:Anniversary Edition|Anniversary Edition]].
* Unlike in ''[[Oblivion:Oblivion|Oblivion]]'', the Crusader's Relics could originally be used by evil characters, including the bandit thieves. This was changed with the Anniversary Edition update, which added the quest The Pilgrim's Path.
** With the Anniversary Edition update, an explanation was added as to how bandits were able to wield the Crusader's Relics: the two bandits, Eigorn and Oren, were new recruits and hadn't committed any crimes yet.
*Prior to the Anniversary Edition update, there were no named bandits at this location. Eigorn and Oren were instead two generic [[SR:Bandit Thief|Bandit Thief]] enemies.

==Quick Walkthrough==
#Travel to [[Skyrim:Solstheim|Solstheim]] and enter [[Skyrim:The Retching Netch|The Retching Netch]].
#Read the [[Skyrim:Mysterious Note (Staff of Sheogorath)|mysterious note]] and take the [[Skyrim:Fork of Horripilation|Fork of Horripilation]].
#Kill the two specified [[Skyrim:Bull Netch|bull netches]] using the fork and loot the artifacts from their bodies.
#Craft the [[Skyrim:Staff of Sheogorath (item)|Staff of Sheogorath]] using a [[Skyrim:Staff Enchanter|Staff Enchanter]].

==Detailed Walkthrough==
===Something Waiting for You===
[[File:SR-quest-Put A Fork In It.jpg|thumb|right|The mysterious message from Sheogorath]]
A [[Skyrim:Mysterious Note (Staff of Sheogorath)|mysterious note]] can be found pinned to a keg on the ground floor of [[Skyrim:The Retching Netch|The Retching Netch]] cornerclub in [[Skyrim:Raven Rock|Raven Rock]], along with the [[Skyrim:Fork of Horripilation|Fork of Horripilation]]. The items will be hard to miss, as they are surrounded by a green glow before you approach.

The note outlines a proposed combat challenge from [[Skyrim:Sheogorath|Sheogorath]], the Daedric Prince of Madness. You are instructed to use the fork to kill two specific [[Skyrim:Bull Netch|bull netches]] on Solstheim, and recover two "familiar" artifacts from their bodies. Specifically, you will need to recover the [[Skyrim:Branch of the Tree of Shades|Branch of the Tree of Shades]] and [[Skyrim:Ciirta's Eye|Ciirta's Eye]], two items which originally appeared in the [[Shivering:Symbols of Office|Symbols of Office]] quest in ''[[Shivering:Shivering Isles|Shivering Isles]]''.

===Netch Hunt===
You must take the fork in order to accept Sheogorath's combat trial. Note that while the fork is literally a kitchen utensil and has very low damage, it is neither [[sr:Fork (item)|generic cutlery]], which is not a weapon, nor the harder to find [[sr:Fork (weapon)|fork ''weapon'']], which is weapon type "other" - it actually has the [[sr:dagger|dagger]] weapon type, allowing your skills and perks to interact with it normally (e.g. it will make no noise when sneak attacking), although both fork weapons do the same base damage of 1.  It also weighs ''12 times'' as much as a normal fork, equivalent to the weight of a [[sr:Daedric Dagger|Daedric Dagger]].  It has a special enchantment that allows you to deal damage to the Bull Netches while holding the fork, which are otherwise immune to damage.

The first bull netch is located close by on the [[SR:Isle of Basalt|Isle of Basalt]], a small volcanic island directly west of the [[Skyrim:Earth Stone|Earth Stone]]. Kill the beast as instructed and claim Ciirta's Eye from its corpse. The second netch can be found due west of [[Skyrim:Skaal Village|Skaal Village]], next to an icy waterfall. It will drop the Branch of the Tree of Shades when killed. Once you have obtained both artifacts, you will need to use them to craft your true reward: the [[Skyrim:Staff of Sheogorath (item)|Staff of Sheogorath]].

===Staff Crafting===
In addition to the two items obtained from the netches, crafting the Staff of Sheogorath will require two [[Skyrim:Heart Stone|Heart Stones]] and access to a [[Skyrim:Staff Enchanter|Staff Enchanter]]. Heart Stones are readily available on Solstheim, and can be [[SR:Mining|mined]] from [[Skyrim:Heart Stone Deposit|deposits]] all over the island. In order to use the Staff Enchanter in [[Skyrim:Tel Mithryn (tower)|Tel Mithryn]], the player must complete the quest [[Skyrim:Reluctant Steward|Reluctant Steward]] for [[Skyrim:Neloth|Neloth]]. However, any staff enchanter will do, such as the one added by the [[SR:Myrwatch|Myrwatch]] or [[SR:Bloodchill Manor|Bloodchill Manor]] Creations.

Once you have obtained the necessary crafting ingredients and access to the Staff Enchanter, you can craft the Staff of Sheogorath to complete the quest. The staff has a powerful area of effect [[Skyrim:Paralysis|paralysis]] enchantment.

==Notes==
*With the [[Skyrim:Saints & Seducers|Saints & Seducers]] Creation installed, the Isle of Basalt where you find one of the netches is also home to several [[SR:Bliss Bug|Bliss Bug]]s as well as a [[SR:Monarch Butterfly|Monarch Butterfly]] and [[SR:Green Butterfly|Green Butterfly]]. These appear regardless of whether or not you have the Staff of Sheogorath Creation installed.
*At release, you would receive this quest upon installing the [[Skyrim:Staff of Sheogorath|Staff of Sheogorath]] [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation]] and be instructed to travel to [[Dragonborn:Solstheim|Solstheim]]. Upon arriving on the island, you would then be directed to the cornerclub. This was changed by the [[SR:Anniversary Edition|Anniversary Edition]] update.
*The recommended Staff Enchanter to use for this is the one at Myrwatch due to this also requiring two Heart Stones (that are readily available near the enchanter there.) The other staff enchanters are the one at Tel Mithryn (which first requires completion of the side quest "Reluctant Steward") and the one at Bloodchill Manor.

{{CC Header|Saints & Seducers}}{{Cleanup-srqrp |writtenBy=Zebendal |checkedBy= |reward=Multiple |rewardChecked= }}{{Trail2|Saints & Seducers|Quests|nocat=1}} {{Quest Header |notrail=1 |Loc=[[SR:Solitude|Solitude]], [[SR:Solitude Sewers|Solitude Sewers]] |Reward=[[Skyrim:Sword of Jyggalag|Sword of Jyggalag]], Four Summoning Spells, [[Skyrim:Ring of Disrobing|Ring of Disrobing]], [[Skyrim:Amber and Madness Smithing|Breadcrumb quest]] to unlock [[Skyrim:Amber|Amber]] and [[Skyrim:Madness|Madness]] smithing |Image=SR-quest-Restoring Order.jpg |Imgdesc=Thoron's vile ritual |Prev=[[SR:Balance of Power|Balance of Power]] |description=Put an end to the melding of planes under [[Skyrim:Solitude|Solitude]]. |ID=ccBGSSSE025_QuestB |mod=[[Skyrim:Saints & Seducers|Saints & Seducers]] }} ==Quick Walkthrough== #Discover the location of [[SR:Thoron|the conjurer's]] lair. #Investigate the Solitude sewers. #Explore the root cave. #Defeat [[Skyrim:Thoron|Thoron]]. #Retrieve the Sword of Jyggalag. ==Detailed Walkthrough== While completing the quest Balance of Power, you will learn that the Saints and Seducers are being funded by a conjurer named Thoron. While one journal will mention he is insane and living in the sewers, the other will mention he's located in Solitude. Both journals indicate that Thoron is looking for trinkets and junk, although his motives are a mystery to both bandit leaders. After entering Solitude, the map marker will direct you to a manhole cover leading down into the sewers. Straight ahead is a grate, and left is a barred door, so turn right and head down. Across the water you'll see that the tunnel is overgrown with strange-looking plant life. Enter this "root cave" and you'll notice pods that you can harvest for new types of flora. To the right is a dead end with a hollowed stump filled with random loot. Turning left will lead you into a tunnel system populated by Elytra and Spriggans. Further into the tunnel you'll reach an intersection. The right path leads to a small cave chamber populated by Spriggans, along with a dead end containing a dead hunter and goat. Continuing along the root path, you'll see a chamber ahead where some of the Solitude stonework is visible. Kill the Elytra Nymphs in the chamber, and to the left you'll see a chamber with water. From the water, you can either turn right to head up a ramp into further root tunnels, or you can go through a broken sewer wall to re-enter the sewers. If you follow the sewer path, you'll come to a room with a Spriggan and some elytra, as well as a locked chest (in an alcove behind the debris). Following the root tunnel will take you up and around, coming to an intersection where a fight apparently took place. Scattered around the intersection, you'll find both Golden and Dark armor/weapons... but no bodies. There is a short path to the right, but it's just a dead end with some enemies and a hollow stump. Continuing straight from the battle site, you'll come upon the object of your quest - Thoron, the mysterious benefactor of the Saints & Seducers gangs. The obviously insane conjurer appears to be performing a ritual, opening a doorway of some sort. Once you're close enough, the objective will update - you must defeat Thoron and stop his ritual. Thoron can be a handful - he will summon both Golden Saints & Dark Seducers, in addition to the usual atronachs. Once you've finished him off, make sure to loot his body for a unique Madness Helm as well as several spell tomes teaching you how to summon Saints or Seducers. From the 4-way intersection where you encountered Thoron, only the southern path leads anywhere (back to the beginning sewers). The northern alcove is Thoron's workstation, where you can find an arcane enchanter and numerous other items of interest. Make sure to loot it all, as both the note and the [[Skyrim:Sheogorath-Shaped Amber|Sheogorath-Shaped Amber]] are needed for other quests. The notes begin the [[Skyrim:Amber and Madness Smithing|Amber and Madness Smithing]] quest, while the Sheogorath-Shaped Amber is needed for [[Skyrim:Staada's Quest|Staada's Quest]]. In the western alcove, grab the Sword of Jyggalag from the roots in order to complete the quest. ==Notes== *After completing the questline, a courier may track you down and give you [[Skyrim:Note on New Wares|a note]]. It's from Ri'saad, letting you know that he now sells Golden/Dark items as well as the new materials added by [[Skyrim:Saints & Seducers|the creation]]. *If you have this DLC as part of the Anniversary Edition, the load order, which is the first two digits of all IDs, may not be obvious. You can find it by using console command player.showinventory and finding the ID of an item from this DLC, such as amber. ==Bugs== {{Bug|You may be unable to enter the sewers.}} **Use the console command coc ccBGSSSE025RootDungeon. {{Bug|When you reach the quest marker in front of the sword, [[Skyrim:Thoron|Thoron]] may fail to appear.}} **{{pc22}} Use the console command prid xx000c3d to select Thoron, and enable to force him to appear. {{Bug|During the battle, [[Skyrim:Thoron|Thoron]] may drift up through the ceiling.}} **{{pc22}} If he fails to reappear shortly, use the console command prid xx000c3d to select Thoron, and moveto player to bring him back. ==Map== {{huh}} {{NewLine}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |0||I've learned that a powerful conjurer, Thoron, has been funding the Saints and Seducers bandits while conducting dangerous experiments somewhere in Solitude. I should try to learn where Thoron might be found.
I've learned that a powerful conjurer, Thoron, has been funding the Saints and Seducers bandits while conducting dangerous experiments somewhere in a sewer. I should try to learn where Thoron might be found. {{Quest Objective|10|Discover the location of the conjurer's lair}} |10||After studying the journals of the both the Saints and Seducers bandit leaders, I've learned that Thoron is conducting dangerous experiments in the Solitude sewers using a strange sword. I should locate Thoron's lair within the sewers and discover the nature of the conjurer's experiments. {{Quest Objective|20|Investigate the Solitude sewers}} |20||I've discovered a network of root-like caves that appear to be spreading throughout the Solitude sewers. They may be connected to the experiments that the conjurer Thoron is supposedly conducting here. I should continue to explore the caves to locate Thoron and put a stop to the spread of these unnatural structures. {{Quest Objective|30|Explore the root cave}} |30||I've found Thoron, who is conducting some kind of ritual using a strange sword. When I entered the chamber, he summoned Daedra and attacked. I will have to defeat Thoron to put an end to this. {{Quest Objective|40|Defeat Thoron}} |40||I've defeated Thoron, and halted the ritual. {{Quest Objective|50|Retrieve the Sword of Jyggalag}} |200||I have retrieved the Sword of Jyggalag and put an end to Thoron's ritual. |missing={{huh}} }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}} {{Stub|Quest}} [[Category:Skyrim-Quests]] [[Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Quests]] [[Category:Skyrim-Saints & Seducers]]

Access to ''[[Skyrim:Dead Man's Dread (place)|Dead Man's Dread]]'' |Prev= |Next= |Image=SR-interior-Dead Man's Dread.jpg |Imgdesc=Pirate loot awaits |description=Search for an ancient pirate ship. |ID=ccBGSSSE031_QUEST |Mod=[[Skyrim:Dead Man's Dread|Dead Man's Dread]] }}[[Category:Skyrim-Quests]][[Category:Skyrim-Dead Man's Dread]][[Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Quests]] ==Quick Walkthrough== #Read ''[[SR:The Restless (book)|The Restless]]'' at [[SR:The Winking Skeever|The Winking Skeever]]. #Gain access to the cell in [[SR:Castle Dour Dungeon|Castle Dour Dungeon]] by whatever means necessary and read ''[[SR:Kevon's Note|Kevon's Note]]''. Take the map. #Travel to [[SR:Orphan's Tear|Orphan's Tear]] and find the boat to [[SR:Blackbone Isle|Blackbone Isle]]. #Enter [[SR:Blackbone Isle Grotto|Blackbone Isle Grotto]] and take [[SR:Cyrus' Boots|Cyrus' Boots]], [[SR:Cyrus' Clothes|Cyrus' Clothes]], and [[SR:Cyrus' Sabre|Cyrus' Sabre]]. #Fight your way back out to the boat. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===A Pirate's Life=== To begin this quest, you will need to go to [[SR:The Winking Skeever|The Winking Skeever]] in [[SR:Solitude|Solitude]]. On one of the tables inside, you will find a book titled ''[[SR:The Restless (book)|The Restless]]'' which describes the later life of [[Lore:Cyrus|Cyrus]], the protagonist of ''[[Redguard:Redguard|The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard]]''. It mentions [[SR:Blackbone Isle|Blackbone Isle]], a long-lost island in the [[SR:Sea of Ghosts|Sea of Ghosts]] said to house an ancient treasure. The last person to visit the island reportedly died in the nearby [[SR:Castle Dour|Castle Dour]] dungeons. Head to the dungeons in order to figure out how to gain access to the cell containing the pirate's corpse. You can speak to a [[SR:Solitude|Solitude Guard]] seated outside the cell and pass an easy [[Skyrim:Speech|Persuasion]] skill check to convince him to open the cell for you. A starting level character of any race can pass this speech check by activating the [[Skyrim:Shrines#Shrine_of_Dibella|Shrine of Dibella]] in the [[Skyrim:Temple_of_the_Divines|Temple of the Divines]] just outside. Alternatively, you can commit a crime yourself and get thrown in jail, although there are obviously some [[Skyrim:Crime#Going_to_Jail|disadvantages]] to using this method. Once inside, you will find the skeletal corpse of [[SR:Kevon|Kevon]] next to a [[SR:Kevon's Note|note]] you need to read. It will reveal that a [[SR:Map to Blackbone Isle|map to Blackbone Isle]] can be found beneath a loose brick within the cell wall. Grab it and head for the coast. ===Old Pirate Den=== Your next destination after escaping Castle Dour is a coastal shipwreck known as [[SR:Orphan's Tear|Orphan's Tear]]. Although this location is usually inhabited by [[SR:Bandit|bandit]]s, on this occasion you will encounter a gang of [[SR:Blackwater Brigand|Blackwater Brigand]]s led by [[SR:Celeste|Celeste]]. This encounter will actually add an unnamed miscellaneous objective to your journal directing you to kill Celeste and claim her unique sword, the [[SR:Blackwater Blade|Blackwater Blade]]. This is secondary to the current quest, but you will likely end up killing Celeste in any case as the brigands are hostile and are guarding the only boat to Blackbone Isle. Once the threat has been neutralized, activate the small boat to sail to Blackbone Isle. The entirety of the small island consists of a shoreline crawling with [[SR:Undead|undead]]; indeed, you will likely be attacked the minute you arrive. You may explore the island's exterior if you wish, but the quest will direct you to the entrance of [[SR:Blackbone Isle Grotto|Blackbone Isle Grotto]] located right next to the boat. The grotto is similarly filled with undead, and houses a well preserved ship named ''[[Skyrim:Dead Man's Dread (place)|Dead Man's Dread]]''. Fight your way through the ship's undead inhabitants until you reach the captain's quarters on the lower level. Here you will find the ''[[SR:Captain's Journal|Captain's Journal]]'' explaining the fate of the ship, as well as [[SR:Cyrus' Sabre|Cyrus' Sabre]] hanging above the desk. Take the sabre, and loot the chest next to the captain's bed to obtain [[SR:Cyrus' Clothes|Cyrus' Clothes]] and [[SR:Cyrus' Boots|Cyrus' Boots]]. All three of these relics of Cyrus need to be taken to progress the quest. Attempting to leave the ship with your new items, you will quickly discover that angry [[SR:Ghost Sailor|Ghost Sailor]]s have arisen to defend their final resting place. Fight your way back to the entrance and face the [[SR:Ghost Captain|Ghost Captain]] out on the deck of the ship. With all the spirits defeated, you can safely make your way back to the boat and leave Blackbone Isle. ===A New Player Home=== Although the quest formally concludes after making your escape, you will soon receive a [[Skyrim:Pirate's Note|mysterious note]] from a "restless soul" via [[SR:Courier|courier]], advising you to convert ''Dead Man's Dread'' into a [[Skyrim:Houses|player home]]. Return to the ship via the boat at Orphan's Tear to complete this objective and claim the island as your own. The ship contains several crafting stations and storage containers, as well as multiple copies of the unique [[SR:Clothing|clothing]] items added by the Creation. You will also find a map inside the ship that can be used for instant [[Skyrim:Transport#Dead Man's Dread|transport]] to [[SR:Solitude|Solitude]], [[SR:Dawnstar|Dawnstar]] and [[SR:Windhelm|Windhelm]]. You can also unlock the two other markers on the map to allow travel to [[SR:Castle Volkihar|Castle Volkihar]] (technically [[SR:Icewater Jetty|Icewater Jetty]]) and [[SR:Raven Rock|Raven Rock]] by first discovering these locations. ==Notes== *Originally, this quest was automatically added to your journal upon installing the [[Skyrim:Dead Man's Dread|Dead Man's Dread]] [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation]]. This was updated with the release of the [[SR:Anniversary Edition|Anniversary Edition]], and you are now required to locate the book yourself to begin the quest. *You will only encounter undead in the exterior areas of Blackbone Isle if you have either the [[SR:Bone Wolf|Bone Wolf]] or [[SR:Plague of the Dead|Plague of the Dead]] [[SR:Creation Club|Creations]] installed. If you have neither Creation installed, the island will instead be inhabited by six harmless [[SR:Rabbit|rabbit]]s. *The Ghost Captain and the other spirits will not follow you below deck. This can be exploited by running back inside the ship to heal. *The skeleton of Kevon is in the same cell as the Crumbling Mortar and can still be used to escape if it has never been used beforehand *Blackbone Isle has a map marker to fast travel to the location but once there you can only leave either via the rowboat or, after claiming the ship with the Pirate's Note, a map on a table aboard the ship will give an additional option to fast travel to four different ports back on Skyrim. ==Bugs== {{Bug|If you are arrested, the optional objective won't be marked as complete until you move further away from the door than where you start.}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |name=The Restless |id=ccBGSSSE031_QUEST |10||I've heard stories of lost shipwrecks strewn across the Sea of Ghosts.
