0→1 ([[Skyrim:Adelaisa Vendicci|Adelaisa Vendicci]]) |description=Help the [[Lore:East Empire Company|East Empire Company]] take care of some [[Skyrim:Blood_Horker|pirates]]. |ID=MS10MiscObjPointer, MS10 |Icon= |SuggLevel=6 }} ==Quick Walkthrough== #Talk to the guard outside the [[Skyrim:East Empire Company Warehouse|East Empire Company Warehouse]]. #Talk to [[Skyrim:Orthus Endario|Orthus Endario]]. #Steal the [[Skyrim:Suvaris Atheron's Logbook|logbook]] from [[Skyrim:Suvaris Atheron|Suvaris Atheron]]. #Talk to [[Skyrim:Stig Salt-Plank|Stig Salt-Plank]] in [[Skyrim:Dawnstar|Dawnstar]]. #Depart for [[Skyrim:Japhet's Folly|Japhet's Folly]] with [[Skyrim:Adelaisa_Vendicci|Adelaisa Vendicci]]. #Kill [[Skyrim:Haldyn|Haldyn]] and report back to Adelaisa. #Speak to Orthus. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===The East Empire Company=== [[File:SR-quest-Rise_In_The_East_02.jpg|thumb|right|''"Please excuse the mess."'']] The [[Lore:East Empire Company|East Empire Company]] is a huge organization that originated in [[Lore:Vvardenfell|Vvardenfell]] and later set up operations in [[Lore:Skyrim|Skyrim]]: a [[Skyrim:East Empire Company Warehouse|warehouse]] in [[Skyrim:Solitude|Solitude]] and an [[Skyrim:East Empire Company (place)|official office]] in [[Skyrim:Windhelm|Windhelm]]. The warehouse near Solitude is off limits, but talking to the guard outside will provide some information on the problems the Company is experiencing. The guard will then point you towards the Windhelm office, specifically an [[Skyrim:Imperial|Imperial]] named [[Skyrim:Orthus Endario|Orthus Endario]] who works there. Travel to the Windhelm dockside office; it will be unlocked between 4am and 8pm, so enter the office and take a look around. The place is falling apart, the shelves are empty, and cobwebs cover most of the ceilings. Orthus will be inside, either trying to clean the place up or eating, and will immediately apologize for the horrible state of the place. When asked, he will explain that pirate attacks have managed to stop all shipments to the Company, from [[Lore:Hammerfell|Hammerfell]] to Vvardenfell, and that the [[Skyrim:House of Clan Shatter-Shield|Shatter-Shield clan]] are the only ones who receive shipments. Apparently, the Shatter-Shields run a private shipping operation, and would be more than pleased with a monopoly at the docks. Orthus has no proof against the clan, but will point you towards a [[Skyrim:Dark Elf|Dark Elf]] named [[Skyrim:Suvaris Atheron|Suvaris Atheron]] who works in the [[Skyrim:Clan Shatter-Shield Office|Shatter-Shield Office]] next door. He then hints at Suvaris' [[Skyrim:Suvaris Atheron's Logbook|logbook]], which could contain evidence that the clan is acquainted with the pirates. The quest will now start and you will have to break into the office and steal the logbook. ===The Logbook=== Breaking into the Shatter-Shield Office is not overly difficult. At 8pm, Suvaris Atheron leaves the office to go drink and sleep at [[Skyrim:New Gnisis Cornerclub|New Gnisis Cornerclub]] until 8am. You can then pick the lock and enter unnoticed. If you're not comfortable with picking Expert locks, you can pickpocket the key from Suvaris. Another strategy is to simply enter the office during the day, while Suvaris is there and the door is unlocked. She is not exactly unwelcoming to visitors, nor does she make much of an effort at guarding her logbook, so wait until she sits down at the table near the front door, then claim the logbook from the table in the northwestern alcove. Leave the office and return to Orthus. When you hand over the logbook, Orthus will read through it and discover that Suvaris often traveled to [[Skyrim:Dawnstar|Dawnstar]] to meet up with a bunch of pirates, led by captain [[Skyrim:Stig Salt-Plank|Stig Salt-Plank]]. He will also explain more on the pirates and reveal them as the [[Lore:Blood Horkers#Blood Horkers|Blood Horkers]], a clever bunch not to be trifled with. He suspects the pirates can be found at the local inn, so travel to Dawnstar and enter the [[Skyrim:Windpeak Inn|Windpeak Inn]]. ===The Blood Horkers=== [[File:SR-quest-Rise_in_the_East_03.jpg|thumb|''"You beasts are the worst."'']] Inside the Inn, you will find Stig Salt-Plank boozing it up with his Blood Horker companions [[Skyrim:Alding|Alding]], [[Skyrim:Gjuk|Gjuk]], and [[Skyrim:Irlof|Irlof]]. They are obviously unwelcome and seemingly unpleasant towards the tavern's [[Skyrim:Bard|bard]], [[Skyrim:Karita (bard)|Karita]]: '''Karita''': ''"You beasts are the worst."''
'''Stig''': ''"Come now, dearie, surely we aren't all that bad."''
'''Karita''': ''"Just... leave me alone! I've brought your mead, now drink it and shut your filthy mouths."''
'''Alding''': ''"Oh, we've got other things in mind for our mouths, sweetie."'' Locate Stig Salt-Plank and ask him if he knows about the Blood Horkers. He will laugh in your face and admit he'd been captaining them for nine years, then proceed to ask why you are so interested. Pretend to be interested in the ship plundering business and Stig will tell you about someone named [[Skyrim:Haldyn|Haldyn]], referring to him as their 'secret ingredient', as he is a powerful battlemage and functions as the leader of the Blood Horkers. Keep pretending to be interested in joining the Horkers and Stig will get suspicious; you can choose to bribe him or challenge him to a brawl. Both options will lead to him telling you about the hiding place of Haldyn, a place called [[Skyrim:Japhet's Folly|Japhet's Folly]]. Alternatively, you can pickpocket Stig's [[Skyrim:Blood Horker Orders|note]] that mentions both Haldyn and Japhet's Folly, or kill him and take it off his corpse. Attacking or killing Stig will not result in a bounty, or even retaliation by his crew; the player may kill all the pirates with no penalty. ===Adelaisa=== [[File:SR-quest-Rise_in_the_East_04.jpg|thumb|right|''"Sorry isn't good enough, Orthus."'']] When you return to the Windhelm docks, a new ship has arrived and will be docked right outside the East Empire Company office. Inside, you will find that Orthus has received a visit from a company superior, namely [[Skyrim:Adelaisa_Vendicci|Adelaisa Vendicci]], who will be understandably upset with the state of the place and the lack of effort on Orthus' part: '''Orthus''': ''"Adelaisa, I'm sorry."''
'''Adelaisa''': ''"Sorry isn't good enough, Orthus. There's a lot of gold at stake here, and sniveling isn't going to get it back."''
'''Orthus''': ''"I've got a top man/woman on the job right now. He/She should be returning any moment."''
'''Adelaisa''': ''"This must be him/her, then."'' If you talk to Orthus, he will briefly introduce Adelaisa and point you towards her; when you approach, she will be grateful to finally see someone who can get things done and order you to join her on her mission to stop the Blood Horkers once and for all. When you reveal the name [[Skyrim:Haldyn|Haldyn]] to her, she realizes the danger of the mission and will immediately exit the office. Head outside to the docked ship and talk to the [[Skyrim:East Empire Mercenary|East Empire mercenary]] and agree to tag along on the journey to Japhet's Folly, an isolated island on the very northern border of Skyrim. During the trip, a strange fog forces the ship to drop anchor outside the island, and Adelaisa suspects Haldyn to be responsible for the sudden change in weather. With all her mercenaries too scared of Haldyn to react, Adelaisa will ask you to take out the battlemage, thus making the fog disappear. This should clear the way for the ship and an attack can be launched. You will have no choice but to accept, so jump off the railing and use the many blocks of ice as a path to Japhet's Folly. Follow the map marker to the hidden sea cave and enter. There is no use trying to shortcut by storming the main gate of the pirates' camp alone, as the door to the stone fortress requires a key found inside the fortress. (Note: Picking the Master-level lock on the compound with the Wax Key perk will give you a copy of the key required to enter the fortress, bypassing the cave entirely.) ===Kill Haldyn=== [[File:SR-quest-Rise_in_the_East_05.jpg|thumb|right|[[Skyrim:Haldyn|Haldyn]] attacks]] The Sea Cave is a small cave located underneath the folly, inhabited by two to three [[Skyrim:Mudcrab|mudcrabs]] and a single [[Skyrim:Blood Horker|Blood Horker]]. Dispose of them all and claim a few healing potions from the shelves, as well as some minor loot from the chests. Proceed up the western slope to a door, leading to Japhet Folly's Tower. As you enter you will hear the sound of more pirates from the level above, so climb the stairs carefully and beware of the [[Skyrim:Traps#Pressure Plate|pressure plate]] and the corresponding [[Skyrim:Traps#Spike_Wall|spike wall]] along the way. Dispose of the enemies, and open the door to a hallway with a chest and locked door that is your escape route later on. Leave it for now and move on to the next room where you can choose to head either upstairs or downstairs. Proceed downstairs first, where two Blood Horkers await. The remains of [[Skyrim:Japhet|Japhet]] can be found behind a locked door next to a locked boss-leveled chest and an explanatory [[Skyrim:Japhet's Journal|journal]]. Backtrack and make your way up the tower. Pick up a couple potions, several alchemy ingredients including two [[Skyrim:Briar Heart (item)#Briar Heart|briar hearts]] and a rare sample of [[Skyrim:Small Antlers|small antlers]] from a table on the way. As you proceed up the last flight of stairs to the top, you will probably hear a sliding noise; this is several bars sliding out of the floor to block off the archway at the bottom of the stairs that you just walked through. When you reach the top, Haldyn will be there and immediately attack you, showering you with [[Skyrim:Shock Damage#Spells|shock spells]]. Dispose of him and loot his body for the Japhet's Folly [[Skyrim:Japhet's Folly Key|key]], then claim the treasure from his chest. When you kill Haldyn, the bars on the archway will retract, allowing you to go back the way you came. Backtrack all the way down the stairs to the locked door and unlock it using the key. (The hallway you came in from will be caved in, so you can't go back that way. Also, there's no door back to the Sea Cave, so this is your only choice.) ===Escape from Japhet's Folly=== [[File:SR-quest-Rise_in_the_East_07.jpg|thumb|right|Rise in the East]] Once outside, you will find yourself in the middle of a regular battlefield as Haldyn's death obviously removed the bad weather surrounding the island. As a result, the East Empire Company mercenaries tear the area to pieces with bombs. The many explosions will not hurt you, but you will have to dispose of all the Blood Horkers that attack you as you make your way towards Adaleisa, who will be waiting on the docks at the bottom of the mountain. When all is said and done, talk to her and she will congratulate you on a job well done and tell you to say the word when you want to return to the mainland. Back in the East Empire Company, Orthus Endario will be overwhelmed with joy and hand you a leveled amount of gold for your trouble. He even suspects the bossy Adelaisa will go easier on him from now on and tells you to return to the office if you ever need help; this means that you can ask Adelaisa to be your [[Skyrim:Followers|follower]] should you ever need her assistance. Additionally, upon revisiting the office after the quest's completion, it will be restored to its former glory and you can take almost all the items there for free. ==Notes== * When you get close to Japhet's Folly, you may want to explore the small island before following the quest mark by entering the Sea Cave. This way, you can kill all of the Blood Horkers outside of the towers. Later, when you have to "escape", most likely only a single bandit outlaw (not labeled as Blood Horker) will be spawned by the game to stop you. * An East Empire Company logo can be seen on the wall after the Office is fixed up roughly 1 day after you finish the quest, but the logo in there is reversed from the real one. * After the quest, [[Skyrim:Guards|guards]] will start to say: ''"I hear the East Empire Company has reopened, thanks in no small part to you. Well done. All of Skyrim benefits from their trade."'' and ''"Thanks again for helping re-open the East Empire Company. Gonna have them import me some of that aged Breton cheese."'' *After the quest, the guard outside the [[Skyrim:East Empire Company Warehouse|East Empire Company Warehouse]] near Solitude will take note of the pirate problem being resolved, and says that the East Empire Company is now busier than ever thanks to your hard work. He will, however, still tell you that the warehouse is off-limits and entering without permission will still count as trespassing. Coincidentally, he is the same guard who directed you to Orthus if you asked him what problems the East Empire Company was dealing with in the first place. *If you have non-essential followers who like to be running ahead in combat, consider leaving them behind before leaving on the boat. While the fireballs at the end may not have much effect on you, your friends will likely be flung away with the explosions if they run ahead and get hit. That said, as long as they only follow behind the Dragonborn, the explosions will not hit them. Also, if the game is played on hardest difficulty (Legendary), virtually all followers should have no problem surviving a few such explosions, regardless of what they do. *After the quest, a [[Skyrim:World Interactions|random encounter]] might occur in which you will be attacked by a group of two Blood Horkers, presumably to avenge their defeat. *Stig Salt-Plank and his crew will remain in the Windpeak Inn after the quest but will not be hostile towards you. *If you have yet to complete [[Skyrim:Diplomatic Immunity|Diplomatic Immunity]] and complete this quest, Orthus can now be found among the prominent guests at the [[Skyrim:Thalmor Embassy|Thalmor Embassy]]. ==Bugs== {{Bug|Under no circumstances should you fast travel back to Japhet's Folly after completing the quest. Japhet's Folly is its own [[SR:Worldspaces|worldspace]] that prevents fast travel from within, leaving you stranded.|OSP|1.9|Fast travel to Japhet's Folly is disabled.}} ** {{Pc22}} If you happened to fast travel to Japhet's Folly and cannot escape by the normal means, you can use the [[Skyrim:Console#moveto|player.moveto]] console command to place yourself on the normal Skyrim realm. Example: player.moveto 00019DDF plops you right outside Riften, consequence free. ** If you happen to be at the stage of [[Skyrim:With Friends Like These...|With Friends Like These...]] where you have received the Mysterious Note, sleeping in Japhet's Folly will trigger the next stage of that quest as normal. That is, Astrid can still whisk you away to the Abandoned Shack even from Japhet's Folly, thus allowing you to escape.. {{Bug|If you reenter the towers from the Sea Cave entrance after the fireball attacks have caved in part of the walls, you will be stuck there, as there's no door back to the Sea Cave, and the only other exit is blocked by rubble.|confirmed=1}} **{{Pc22}} You can get out either by using the player.moveto command above, or by using tcl to turn off clipping so you can walk through the rubble to get to the door. {{Bug|During the escape stage after you kill Haldyn, some of the pirates may fall into the water near Adelaisa and get stuck under the bridge, making the quest uncompletable as you cannot talk to her.|confirmed=1}} **It is possible, though difficult, to kill them underwater with [[sr:Ice Storm|Ice Storm]] or arrows. Using [[sr:Detect Life (spell)|Detect Life]] or [[sr:Aura Whisper|Aura Whisper]] can help you target them. **{{Pc22}} If a pirate continues to hide underwater, it is also possible to swim up to the pirate, open up the [[sr:Console|Console]] with the tilde key (~), click on the pirate, and then type in the console command kill. Note that you'll have to close the console and reopen it for the pirate to actually die. {{Bug|If you swim to a little boat south of the island before killing Haldyn, the fireball attacks start prematurely. If you leave that boat, the fireball attacks stop again.|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|Adelaisa can get stuck in 'wounded' position. Reentering and exiting Japhet's Folly may fix this.|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|During your attack on the keep, before you kill Haldyn, Orthus may appear in front of the door that becomes your exit. He is unkillable, however, he gets stuck there and does not appear back on the mainland, making the quest unfinishable.|vn=1}} {{Bug|After obtaining the logbook, the EEC office may be stuck in a closed and locked state (even in midday), and Orthus may not be inside. Picking the lock, entering, exiting, and re-entering may make him appear. If not, he can be moved to the player with console commands.}} {{Bug|After meeting Stig and returning to the EEC office, you may find Adelaisa there, in a "this NPC is busy" state, without Orthus. He can be moved into the room with console commands and the scene will resume as normal.}} {{Bug|After you finish the quest, Stig and his men may permanently remain inside Windpeak Inn, and only say general quotes if you talk to them.}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |name=MS10MiscObjPointer |id=MS10MiscObjPointer |10||{{Quest Objective|10|Talk to Orthus Endario at the East Empire Company in Windhelm}} |!|Rise in the East|MS10 |10||The East Empire Company is being harassed by a group of pirates and would like me to help shut them down. Go to [[Skyrim:Castle Dour|Castle Dour]] to report your success to [[Skyrim:General Tullius|General Tullius]]. He will award you your first promotion, the rank of [[Skyrim:Imperial_Legion#Ranks|Quaestor]], along with a [[Skyrim:Leveled Lists#Enchanted Weapons|leveled enchanted weapon]] and order you to meet [[Skyrim:Legate Rikke|Legate Rikke]] at one of many [[Skyrim:Military Camps#Imperial Camps|Imperial Military Camp]] for your next assignment; depending on your progress through the [[Skyrim:Main Quest|Main Quest]] the Camp you will be sent to will change as follows. ===Quest Options=== This quest governs the overall progress of the [[Skyrim:Civil_War|Civil War]] for the [[Skyrim:Imperial_Legion|Imperial Legion]]. It serves as an "umbrella quest", taking you through a series of individual quests that you receive as it progresses. The overall goal of the quest is to conquer, for the Empire, each [[Skyrim:Holds|hold]] of Skyrim that is currently under Stormcloak control. You will accomplish this one hold at a time, by taking control of the [[Skyrim:Military Forts|military fort]] in each, ending with one final siege on the enemy's capital, [[Skyrim:Windhelm|Windhelm]], in the order of the following table. The holds to be conquered can be altered by negotiation during the optional quest [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]] and therefore only a subset of the following quests needs to be completed. *Without doing Season Unending, only the Stormcloak-controlled holds in the following table need to be conquered. *By doing Season Unending: **The initially allied-controlled holds only need to be reconquered if given to the enemy during negotiation. **The initially enemy-controlled holds will not need to be conquered if taken from the enemy during negotiation. **The initially enemy-controlled holds will need to be conquered if not taken during negotiation. **If you progress it to the point of a truce, any active quest in the series will auto-complete and cannot be restarted. After completing [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Amol|The Battle for Fort Amol]], return to Rikke who will tell you ''"We're taking the city. Meet the soldiers gathering for the attack. Move it!"''. This will automatically start [[Skyrim:Battle for Windhelm|Battle for Windhelm]]. As part of that quest, [[Skyrim:General Tullius|General Tullius]] will have a short dialogue with [[Skyrim:Ulfric Stormcloak|Ulfric Stormcloak]], who will request the Dragonborn to be the one who kills him, as it will "make for a better song." General Tullius won't care whether you kill Ulfric or not, just as long as he's dead. If you choose to kill Ulfric, General Tullius will tell you to use his sword (which is a leveled enchanteed sword) to do the deed (this is not required though) and Battle for Windhelm will be complete once you deliver the final blow. If you choose to allow Tullius to do it, Battle for Windhelm will complete after that, when General will reward you with his leveled enchanted sword. Either way, [[Skyrim:Reunification of Skyrim|Reunification of Skyrim]] will now be complete and you can join Rikke and Tullius outside to hear him delivering the final speech of the Civil War, promising increased pay and freedom for them to return to their families while giving compensation to families who have lost loved ones. Then, you're allowed to talk to Legate Rikke and General Tullius on what will happen next. Congratulations, [[Lore:Skyrim|Skyrim]] is now part of the [[Lore:Empire|Empire]] once again and peace is restored. ==Notes== *This quest is mainly used to move you between the other Imperial quests. *This quest and [[Skyrim:Liberation of Skyrim|Liberation of Skyrim]] are different radiant versions of the same quest. *Season Unending can be started anytime from prior to starting the Civil War Quest-line to when there are at least 2 holds left for you to conquer for your allied side. *If, after [[Skyrim:Dragonslayer|Dragonslayer]], depending on when the truce halted this quest, there is no quest mark, to resume it, you may need to speak to your faction leader. *It is not possible to receive and complete all the potential quests in the series, as negotiation during Season Unending is limited. *Trading the wrong holds during Season Unending can prevent obtaining some unique radiant quests from the series, [[Skyrim:Imperial Legion#Ranks|ranks]] and [[Skyrim:Achievements#War Hero|War Hero achievement]]. *Ranks are not automatic, they are rewarded if the conditions are met: successful attack (not fleeing) during the related quest and not obtaining the hold by negotiation during Season Unending. *Ranks are progressive but not required: if you miss one, you can obtain the following one by completing the relative quest. So it is actually necessary to complete only [[Skyrim:Rescue from Fort Kastav|Rescue from Fort Kastav]] to obtain the final rank of Legate. *Each rank comes with its leveled item reward. *To check your rank you can spam-speak to any allied soldier until he greets you by your current rank. *When a hold switches ownership, deposed [[Skyrim:Jarl|Jarls]] and court/family are exiled, usually to their allegiance side's capital, and replaced by opposing ones, while related [[Skyrim:Forts#Civil War Forts|Civil War Forts]] are re-garrisoned by the new owner's soldiers. *At any point during this quest, enemy-controlled Civil War Forts are always garrisoned by enemy soldiers and will be garrisoned by allied ones when conquered. However initially allied-controlled ones remain inhabited by generic enemies, needing individual clearing. *Any allied military camp located within an enemy hold disappears upon conquest of that specific hold. *Legate Rikke will replace the Officer at any military camp for the duration of the hold assignment. If she is not there but the quest marker is upon an empty spot wait a few hours for her to arrive. *After every quest of this series (except for [[Skyrim:Battle for Windhelm|Battle for Windhelm]]), unmarked by in-game references, you can approach Legate Rikke for a [[Skyrim:Leveled Lists#Gold Rewards|medium leveled gold reward]]; this is not always recommended though, as this is a cause for the missing ''"Reporting for duty."'' dialogue option (see [[#Bugs|Bugs]]). ==Bugs== {{cleanup|Lots of unlike fixes; need in-game and CK testing, removal of fake ones}} {{Bug|Legate Rikke may not offer the ''"Reporting for duty."'' dialogue option.|confirmed=1}} **This is not a proper bug, more like a soft-lock, sometimes deterministically caused by player's actions, and may or may not be solvable. Try the following fixes, listed from the most to least reliable. If you still can't fix it, you may need to identify when you triggered the bug and reload a save file previous to that point, then progress the quests in the series in a different order. The safest way to prevent the hardest version of this bug to happen at all is to do all the quests in the series straight away, skip [[Skyrim:Season Unending|Season Unending]], do it before the Civil War Quest-line or between completed quests from this series, avoiding as much as possible Legate Rikke, as loading her cell can improperly set up the next quest, even if you don't speak to her. **If you progressed Season Unending to the point of a truce, Legate Rikke will offer dialogue only after you complete [[Skyrim:Dragonslayer|Dragonslayer]]. **Go to any indoor location and wait/rest for 30+ days. This allows all location cells to respawn. **If the fort that was supposed to be the target of the next mission is occupied by generic enemies, kill them. Then travel away and spend some time (e.g. wait for 24h). **Ask General Tullius ''"How goes the war?"'' until the phrase is no longer white (the indicator that he has something new to say). **Repeatedly talk to Rikke then run into her to interrupt her dialogue. **Go to jail and serve time. **Activate the [[Skyrim:Lycanthropy#Beast Form|Beast Form]] and wait until it wears out. **{{pc22}} The console command movetoqt CWObj can be used to teleport you to the current objective of this quest, aka Legate Rikke. **If you manage to move Legate Rikke to another location (for example by making her follow you, casting a [[Skyrim:Frenzy (effect)#Spells|frenzy spell]] and [[Skyrim:Pacify (effect)|pacifying]] afterwards), then letting her walk back to the current Imperial Camp can fix it. You can also attack her until she becomes hostile. ***{{pc22}} The console commands prid 198BB to target her then moveto player can be used to teleport her to your current location. **Triggering her hostility (for example by random enemies) and going outside the camp also resets Rikke. **{{pc22}} Head to General Tullius. Talk to him, then exit out and open up the console command getstage cwobj to verify the variable is set to 1.00. If it is so, enter resetquest cwobj. Use getstage cwobj to confirm the quest stage is 0.00. Enter setstage cwobj 1. **{{pc22}} The console command coc followed by location code of the imperial camp (for example coc MilitaryCampReachImperial) can be used to teleport to the chosen Military Camp. **{{pc22}} It is possible the last fort you captured has not properly registered as Imperial. You can manually set ownership of the fort through console command. First enter an interior location, then use help 'Fort Dunstad' (replace with the fort you just tried to capture) to obtain its LCTN: variable (something like 00019182). Then, use GetKeywordDataForLocation %LCTN% CWOwner to check the owner of this location; if it shows 0 (nobody) or 2 (Stormcloaks), then use SetKeywordDataForLocation %LCTN% CWOwner 1. After that, the 'Reporting for duty' prompt should appear. **{{pc22}} At the regain Eastmarch stage, if the ''"Reporting for duty."'' dialogue is not offered by Rikke to start [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Amol]], travel to Fort Amol and kill every necromancer. After that, sleep in one of the beds and Stormcloaks should occupy the Fort. Use movetoqt CWObj to directly teleport to Rikke. If the option doesn't show, talk to Tullius in Castle Dour by entering the following command in the console coc SolitudeCastleDour, and then go to Rikke with the previous command. **{{pc22}} If nothing else works, you may need complete the entire Reunification of Skyrim quest via the console command setstage cwobj 255. You cannot use the console to start the next quest within the series, as the bug applies to the over-arching quest. **This may be cleared by saving and resetting the entire system. {{Bug|After [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Dunstad (Imperial)|The Battle for Fort Dunstad]], if General Tullius will promote you to Praefect rank you are actually promoted to Tribune with related leveled shield. It is not possible to get the actual Praefect rank. Since you already are, this will also "skip" the actual promotion to Tribune after [[Skyrim:The Battle for Fort Greenwall (Imperial)|The Battle for Fort Greenwall]].|modnotes=mistake in the script TIF__000CE0E8: there is "3", should be "2".|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|The war strategy maps located at military bases and command headquarters do not update as intended.|USKP|1.2.1|fixdetail=Each map needs to be visited twice for the correction to take effect in saved games.}} {{Bug|After retaking Winterhold and upon talking to General Tullius, you will receive a piece of leveled armor. However, General Tullius may give you no further instructions and your journal has the text "Report to General Tullius". This prevents the quest line from continuing.|confirmed=1}} **There is a way to force Tullius ''"What's next"'' option after he gave you the armor by setting ownership of Winterhold and Fort Kastav to the Empire manually through console command. First, use help 'Fort Kastav' to obtain LCTN: variable (something like 00019182) and help 'Winterhold' (there may be two of them). Then, use GetKeywordDataForLocation %LCTN% CWOwner for Fort Kastav and Winterhold LCTNs to check the owner of this locations; if any of them shows 2 (Stormcloaks), then use SetKeywordDataForLocation %LCTN% CWOwner 1. After that 'What's next' option should appear. **There may still be dialogue issues when you reach Winterhold. To prevent this, work through "Reunification of Skyrim" until you finish regaining Fort Greenwall. Before you report to General Tullius, finish the main questline. During "Season Unending", you will be given the option to put Winterhold on the negotiating table. It will most likely be the only option given, since you have control of the other holds thus far. If you choose that option, then all of the Imperial quests regarding Winterhold will be skipped and will automatically fall under Imperial control, without requiring you to attempt bugged conversations. **If there is still no dialogue option from Tullius to continue on in the quest after Winterhold, simply travel to the Eastmarch Imperial Camp and talk to Legate Rikke, that will proceed with the questline and she will give a reward as if you just completed a quest for her, even if it's the first time talking to her. ==Quest Stages== Only stages and objectives relevant to the Reunification of Skyrim (rather than Liberation of Skyrim) are included in the table. {{Journal Entries |name= |1||I will help General Tullius quell the Stormcloak rebellion and reunite Skyrim by restoring Imperial control. |||{{Quest Comment|Displayed as needed}} {{Quest Objective|1001|Report to General Tullius}} |||{{Quest Comment|Displayed as each hold becomes the new target}} {{Quest Objective|201|Regain the Reach}} {{Quest Objective|301|Regain Hjaalmarch}} {{Quest Objective|401|Regain Whiterun Hold}} {{Quest Objective|501|Regain Falkreath Hold}} {{Quest Objective|601|Regain the Pale}} {{Quest Objective|701|Regain Winterhold Hold}} {{Quest Objective|801|Regain Eastmarch}} {{Quest Objective|901|Regain the Rift}} |255|fin|We have successfully quelled the rebellion by killing Ulfric Stormcloak and have reunited Skyrim under Imperial control. }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}}

Skyrim:Return to Grace.wikitext: {{Cleanup-srqrp |writtenBy=Krusty |checkedBy=Beezer1029 |reward=Krusty |rewardChecked=Beezer1029 }}{{Quest Header |type=Miscellaneous |Giver=[[Skyrim:Svari|Svari]] |Loc=[[Skyrim:Solitude|Solitude]] |Reward=[[#Reward|Leveled Gold]] |Disp= =1 ([[Skyrim:Greta|Greta]], if Unofficial Skyrim Patch since v2.1.0 are installed) |Image=SR-quest-Return to Grace.jpg |Imgdesc=[[Skyrim:Roggvir|Roggvir]]'s execution |description=Convince a mourning [[Skyrim:Greta|mother]] to go to the [[Skyrim:Temple of the Divines|local temple]]. |ID=SolitudeFreeform03 }} ==Quick Walkthrough== #Speak to [[Skyrim:Svari|Svari]]. #Speak to [[Skyrim:Greta|Greta]]. #Retrieve [[Skyrim:Roggvir|Roggvir]]'s [[Skyrim:Amulet of Talos|amulet of Talos]]. #Return the amulet to Greta. ==Detailed Walkthrough== ===A Concerned Child=== When first entering [[Skyrim:Solitude|Solitude]], you will witness the execution of [[Skyrim:Roggvir|Roggvir]], the guard that allowed [[Skyrim:Ulfric Stormcloak|Ulfric Stormcloak]] to escape Solitude after murdering [[Skyrim:High King Torygg|High King Torygg]]. During this, a child named [[Skyrim:Svari|Svari]] is being sent home by her [[Skyrim:Addvar|father]] to spare her from seeing her uncle's execution. Svari can always be found in the streets of Solitude between 10am and 8pm when she plays with the other children. Approach her and she will appear quite sad about recent events, specifically with her uncle. When you tell her you are sorry about what happened with Roggvir, she will respond: ''"Thanks. Papa talks about it some. Mum doesn't say much since Uncle Roggvir died. She doesn't even go to Temple anymore. I wish she would. At least that way she'd have people to talk to."'' When you offer to talk to her mother, Svari will encourage you to do it right away and the quest will initiate. ===The Grieving Sister=== Svari's mother [[Skyrim:Greta|Greta]] can usually be found in the [[Skyrim: Addvar's House|family house]] across the street from the [[Skyrim:Bards College|Bards College]] or browsing the market between 3pm and 6pm. Approaching her will reveal that she is both bitter and sad about the execution of her brother. When confronted with Svari's concerns, she will respond: ''"She did, did she? She's going to get a sit down later."'' When you tell her that Svari just wants to see her mother return to the [[Skyrim:Temple of the Divines|temple]], she will explain her [[Skyrim:Nord|Nord]] beliefs: ''"Well. I wish it were that simple. Maybe it is. Look, I want to go back but I won't feel right in there without a tie to [[Lore:Talos|Talos]]. My brother Roggvir wore a symbol of Talos. He kept it hidden on his person. If I had that... I can't go near his body. Would you get it back for me?"'' Agree to help her and the quest will update and a map marker will point you towards the body of Roggvir. ===Return to Grace=== If you started the quest within three days after entering Solitude, Roggvir's headless body will still lie behind the chopping block where he met his demise. If not, his body will be inside the [[Skyrim:Solitude Catacombs|Solitude Catacombs]] behind the [[Skyrim:Hall of the Dead (Solitude)|Hall of the Dead]]. Enter the catacombs and fight the [[Skyrim:Skeleton|skeleton]] then locate Roggvir's coffin near the entrance. Pry it open and claim the [[Skyrim:Amulet of Talos|Amulet of Talos]] then exit the catacombs. Locate Greta who will cheer up a bit when you hand her the amulet: ''"Thanks so much. I'll return to temple. Here's something for your time and effort."'' She will then hand you a [[#Reward|reward]] and the quest will end. From this point forward, Greta will enter the Temple of the Divines every morning at 6am for nine hours of praying, holding her forbidden Amulet of Talos. === Reward === {{SRLeveledReward|small}} == Notes == *If you carry another Amulet of Talos in your inventory, the game identifies them all as quest items. You will have to choose the dialogue option before you can drop, sell, or build with any Amulet of Talos. == Bugs == {{Bug|If you wait to loot the Amulet of Talos from Roggvir's corpse until you receive the quest, when you offer to give an amulet to Greta, it does not complete the quest, gain a reward, nor does it remove an Amulet of Talos. The dialogue option disappears nevertheless and the amulet(s) are dropable/sellable.|USKP|1.0}} {{Bug|If you loot the amulet from Roggvir's corpse before talking to Greta, the same problems occur as above. The dialogue option disappears, but not the quest journal entry. It also makes the amulet(s) dropable/sellable.|USKP|1.2.2}} **{{Pc22}} A solution is to proceed to talk to Svari, then talk to Greta. Mention going to temple, and after she asks you to retrieve the amulet, exit the conversation. Do ''not'' choose the "Actually I've got it here" option. Now in the console, type setStage SolitudeFreeform03 20, this will set the quest to the moment you are supposed to retrieve the amulet. Since you already have it, go into the console once more and type setStage SolitudeFreeform03 30 which will set the moment you should have picked the amulet up. Return to Greta and give the amulet. It will complete the quest and will be removed from the log, though the amulet still stays in your inventory and you won't get the reward she mentions. **{{Pc22}} Another solution is, before talking to Greta (or in some cases Svari), to use the console command player.drop 000CC846 x (with x being the number of Amulets of Talos you have in your inventory +1) in order to drop all Amulets of Talos. No matter how many you have, one of it (the one relevant for the quest) will always drop separately. After talking to Greta and promising her to retrieve the amulet, just pick up all the amulets you've dropped and talk to her to finish the quest (you might get a leveled reward and complete the quest using this method). **{{Pc22}} If you end up with two Amulet of Talos in your inventory, you could try the console command, player.removeitem 000CC846 1 to eliminate the duplication. **You can get rid of the quest journal entry and make the amulet dropable/sellable without any console commands by killing Greta before telling her that you have the amulet. ***If you tell her you that you have the amulet before you kill her, the amulet is fixed but the quest entry remains in your journal indefinitely. {{Bug|When you offer Greta the amulet, sometimes she doesn't take the amulet or give you the reward, but the quest is completed.|USKP|1.0}} {{Bug|Greta's disposition towards you does not increase after completing the quest as it should.|USKP|2.1.0}} ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |10||{{Quest Objective|10|Speak to Greta about going to the Temple of Divines.}} |20||{{Quest Objective|20|Retrieve Amulet of Talos off of Roggvir.}} |30||{{Quest Objective|30|Return Amulet of Talos to Greta.}} |missing=0, 40, 200 }} {{Skyrim Quest Stages Notes}}

==Walkthrough==
If you murder an NPC who has a relative, the relative may subsequently send three [[Skyrim:Hired Thug|hired thug]]s to hunt you down and teach you a lesson (i.e. kill you in vengeance). The thugs will be carrying a [[Skyrim:Contract (Murder)|contract]] which reveals the name of the relative who hired the thugs.

== Notes ==
* You may also be attacked if you steal from someone (see [[Skyrim:Steal, Thugs hunt player|Steal, Thugs hunt player]]).

[[File:SR-qico-Miscellaneous.png|Side Quests Knotwork|left]] '''Side quests''' are standard-length quests that are not part of a questline and are not [[Skyrim:Daedric Quests|Daedric quests]]. Completing side quests generally increases the "Side Quests Completed" statistic in your journal and counts toward the [[#Achievements|Sideways]] [[Skyrim:Achievements|achievement]].

Side quests can be identified by the side quest knotwork (pictured above left) displayed next to the quest title in your journal and on each quest's page on this wiki.

Serana is the long lost daughter of [[Skyrim:Lord Harkon|Lord Harkon]] and [[Skyrim:Valerica|Valerica]], and is in possession of an [[Skyrim:Elder Scroll (Sun)|Elder Scroll]]. Upon introduction, she will know if you are a [[Skyrim:Vampirism|vampire]] or not, and she will ask you to take her to [[Skyrim:Volkihar Keep|her home]]. Throughout the [[Skyrim:Dawnguard Quests|Dawnguard questline]], Serana accompanies you as an obligatory follower regardless of whether you side with the [[Skyrim:Dawnguard (faction)|Dawnguard]] or [[Skyrim:Volkihar Vampire Clan|Volkihar Clan]]. Taught in the dark arts by her mother, she is a talented necromancer and will often reanimate corpses to assist the two of you in battle. As a magic user and vampire, she uses a variety of spells in battle and wields an [[Skyrim:Elven Dagger|elven dagger]] for close combat. In regards to her personality, she possesses a natural defensiveness that doesn't come off as cold. Skillfully, she navigates away from difficult subjects and redirects conversations toward topics you're more inclined to discuss. These defenses stem from her quick temper and intense passion, which she guards against so others won't bear the brunt of them. While she genuinely cares for those who befriend her, she only invests so much as they demonstrate their worthiness. Additionally, she carries a hint of self-deprecating humor and self-awareness. Although intelligent, she maintains a degree of naïvety. Having been sealed in Dimhollow Crypt for centuries, she harbors a curiosity about the world's current state. {{NewLeft}} == Related Quests == * {{Quest Link|Awakening}} * {{Quest Link|Bloodline}} * {{Quest Link|Prophet (Dawnguard)|Prophet (Dawnguard)}} * {{Quest Link|Prophet (Vampire)|Prophet (Vampire)}} * {{Quest Link|Chasing Echoes}} * {{Quest Link|Beyond Death}} * {{Quest Link|Unseen Visions}} * {{Quest Link|Touching the Sky}} * {{Quest Link|Kindred Judgment}} ==Background== Serana had a very close relationship with her mother growing up. In her youth, she was distant from her father, though never against him in any capacity. By vampire standards, her relationship with her mother was as loving and nurturing as it could be, given their circumstances. Even as a child, hers was a fairly lonely life. Her mother taught her necromancy and other forms of magic, allowing her to become a powerful mage in her own right. Before becoming a vampire, her father ruled as a mighty king and his domain was said to be vast and powerful. As the years passed and death approached, Harkon began to fear his own mortality. To combat the inevitable, he made a pact with [[Lore:Molag Bal|Molag Bal]] and sacrificed a thousand innocents in his name. In return, the Daedric Prince granted him immortality by turning him and his family into pure-blooded vampires, giving birth to the [[Lore:Volkihar|Volkihar]] bloodline. It was at this point her parents' marriage began to break down, as they both became drunk with their newfound powers. A thousand years ago, her father became obsessed with a prophecy called the [[Lore:Tyranny of the Sun|Tyranny of the Sun]], which would require [[Skyrim:Auriel's Bow|Auriel's Bow]] and the blood of a pure-blooded vampire to block out the sun forever, allowing vampires to reign supreme. Being a [[Lore:Daughters of Coldharbour|Daughter of Coldharbour]], Serana had the required vampire blood to make it work. Serana's relationship with her father deteriorated as he became more and more obsessed with fulfilling the prophecy. Ultimately, it reached the point that he was even willing to sacrifice her to achieve his goal. Serana's mother believed that if eternal night fell, it would bring too much attention upon vampires and ultimately would lead to their extinction. To prevent this from happening, Serana's mother fled Castle Volkihar with two Elder Scrolls that contained parts of the prophecy. She sealed Serana away in [[Skyrim:Dimhollow Crypt|Dimhollow Crypt]] with one of the scrolls to hide her from her father. Her mother then fled into the [[Skyrim:Soul Cairn|Soul Cairn]] with the other scroll for the same reason. Enraged by this betrayal, Serana's father commanded every vampire in his court to look for them. Unfortunately, none of the vampires were able to find them, and after centuries of searching, her father eventually lost hope. He did, however, have strong memories of the incident, and would make Serana and her mother answer dearly for it if he ever saw them again. ==As a Follower== In many ways, Serana is a unique follower. === Finding Her === Her main location during gameplay depends on your allegiance. If you join the [[Skyrim:Dawnguard (faction)|Dawnguard]], you can find her at [[Skyrim:Fort Dawnguard|Fort Dawnguard]]. If you choose the [[Skyrim:Volkihar Vampire Clan|Volkihar Vampire Clan]], however, you can find her at [[Skyrim:Volkihar Keep|Volkihar Keep]]. After completing the Beyond Death quest, she can also be found in Valerica's study. After completing the Dawnguard campaign, she often roams Skyrim in search of adventure. If you find her, you can recruit her, regardless of the location. === Attire === Serana wears a [[Skyrim:Vampire Royal Armor|Vampire Royal Armor]] and a pair of [[Skyrim:Vampire Boots|Vampire Boots]]. She dons a [[Skyrim:Serana Hood|unique hood]] when outside, which visually obscures her headgear. She might wear the attire you place in her inventory, although she completely ignores those included in the [[Skyrim:Arcane Accessories|Arcane Accessories]] DLC. Her attire choice logic ignores the fact that she has no need for items that bestow cold resistance while she is a vampire. === Behavior === Serana does not behave like other followers. She does not use one of the four personas of the base game (Imperial, Nord, Orc, or Arrogant). Her feedbacks are playful. While the other followers act as if they are on an invisible leash, Serana behaves more like an independent person. She sticks close to you, but might sit, read, eat, lean on a wall, use crafting stations (anvil, smelter, workbench, arcane enchanter, etc.), cook, or even mine ore veins. All of these actions are visual only; they have no gameplay impact. You can tell Serana to wait, come along with you, or exchange inventory items, but she might decline. While the Bloodline quest is active, she refuses to exchange inventory items, as she doesn't know you well enough to trust you yet. In response to a "Wait here" command, she tells you, in no ambiguous terms, that she will continue to follow you, albeit with a distance. Serana is not interested in joining the [[Skyrim:Blades|Blades]], becoming your [[Skyrim:Personal Steward|steward]]{{HF}}, or [[Skyrim:Marriage|marriage]]. She does, however, react to an [[Skyrim:Amulet of Mara|Amulet of Mara]]. === Combat === Serana is a magic user and wields an [[Skyrim:Elven Dagger|Elven Dagger]] for close combat. She has the highest health among the game's followers. She will frequently, if not always, reanimate corpses, but they later turn into ash piles when their duration ends or if they die. Thus, she is less useful if you plan to reanimate extremely powerful magicians as dead thralls, for example [[Skyrim:Sild_the_Warlock|Sild the Warlock]], [[Skyrim:Arch-Curate Vyrthur|Arch-Curate Vyrthur]], [[Skyrim:Orchendor|Orchendor]], [[Skyrim:Malkoran|Malkoran]], [[Skyrim:Lu'ah_Al-Skaven|Lu'ah Al-Skaven]], [[Skyrim:Malyn_Varen|Malyn Varen]], or [[Skyrim:The_Caller|the Caller]]. This can also be problematic if you are a [[Skyrim:Lycanthropy|werewolf]], as you'll have less time to feed on corpses to extend your bloodlust in [[Skyrim:Beast Form|Beast Form]]. Outside of this, her necromancy is powerful enough to reanimate non-humanoid entities. The spells she uses depend on her level. She has a [[Skyrim:Vampiric Drain|Drain Life]] spell that gets stronger with higher levels (even if her vampirism is cured). Additionally, in every case she knows the following spells: {| class=wikitable ! Level !!colspan=3| |- | 12–19 || [[Skyrim:Raise Zombie|Raise Zombie]] || [[Skyrim:Ice Spike|Ice Spike]] || |- | 20–27 || [[Skyrim:Reanimate Corpse|Reanimate Corpse]] || [[Skyrim:Ice Spike|Ice Spike]] || |- | 28–37 || [[Skyrim:Reanimate Corpse|Reanimate Corpse]] || [[Skyrim:Ice Spike|Ice Spike]] || [[Skyrim:Lightning Bolt|Lightning Bolt]] |- | 38–47 || [[Skyrim:Revenant|Revenant]] || [[Skyrim:Ice Spike|Ice Spike]] || [[Skyrim:Lightning Bolt|Lightning Bolt]] |- | 48–50 || [[Skyrim:Revenant|Revenant]] || [[Skyrim:Ice Storm|Ice Storm]] || [[Skyrim:Chain Lightning|Chain Lightning]] |} Since Serana is a vampire she is immune to all diseases and poisons, and because she is also a Nord she has complete immunity to any frost-based attacks. However, she also has a 50% Weakness to Fire and No Health, Magicka, or Stamina regeneration in sunlight. The [[Skyrim:Healing Hands|Healing Hands]] spell does not heal Serana. She requires [[Skyrim:Necromantic Healing|Necromantic Healing]] instead. Nevertheless, the game has flagged Serana as [[Skyrim:Essential NPCs|Essential]]; she never dies. == As an NPC == During the quest [[Skyrim:Chasing Echoes|Chasing Echoes]], she will offer to turn you into a [[Skyrim:Vampire Lord|Vampire Lord]]. After completing the quest [[Skyrim:Kindred Judgment|Kindred Judgment]], she can be asked to turn you into a Vampire Lord at any time. If you sided with the Dawnguard, while a Vampire Lord they will refuse any interactions with you, stating that you need to get cured immediately. This starts [[Skyrim:Rising at Dawn|Rising at Dawn]]. Only elven ones will work for this, remember?"'' == Curing Serana's Vampirism == [[File:SR-npc-Serana 04.jpg|thumb|right|Serana after she is cured of vampirism]] If you side with the Dawnguard, you can convince Serana to cure her vampirism after her father's death. However, there is a way to lock yourself out of this line of inquiry: after Serana brings her [[Skyrim:Elder Scroll (Sun)|Elder Scroll]] to Fort Dawnguard, ask her, "Have you always been a vampire?" During this conversation, if you ask if she has ever thought about getting cured, she will refer to her condition as a gift, insisting that she will never seek a cure for it. You can tell her to seek a cure after her father has been defeated, but she declines and refuses to speak to you about it further. After [[Skyrim:Kindred Judgment|Kindred Judgment]], once you've have left Harkon's room, if you are not a vampire yourself, you can ask Serana if she's ever considered being cured. Unless you pick a self-centered response, she will immediately leave to see [[Skyrim:Falion|Falion]] for a cure. For the next three days, she will stay with Falion, at which point, she will become human and return to Fort Dawnguard. The conversation goes as follows: :'''Have you thought about getting cured of vampirism?''' :''"No... why?"'' Three options become available: :'''Look what it did to your family.''' ::''"Even before that, we weren't the most normal family. We did worship a Daedra, remember?"'' :: (✔ Success) :'''You could be your own person again.''' ::''"It would be nice not to always be thirsty."'' :: (✔ Success) :'''I think I'd feel more comfortable.''' ::''"So you take a major decision for me, and make it all about you? Forget it."'' :: (❌ Fail; terminates conversation) If the first part of the conversation is successful, two options will become available: :'''If you want to cure yourself, I'll support you.''' ::''"I'll speak to Falion. I've heard he knows about these things."'' :: (✔ Success) :'''I don't think I can help you with this.''' ::''"(Sarcastically) Very supportive!"'' :: (❌ Fail; terminates conversation) If you convince her to cure herself, two options become available. Neither change the outcome: :'''I want to come with you.''' ::''"I know you do, but this is something I need to do alone. I'll see you again. Soon."'' :'''Good luck.''' ::''"I'll see you soon."'' If Serana chooses to become human, she will no longer be able to provide you with bloodcursed arrows nor turn you into a vampire. Her eyes will revert to her mortal blue eyes, although due to a [[#Bugs|bug]], they will be yellow instead of white on the outside. She will no longer be undead; thus, she can be healed by your Restoration healing spells, she won't be damaged by Restoration combat spells that target undead, and she appears with Detect Life instead of Detect Dead. Her combat spell usage remains the same; she continues to use a vampiric Drain Life attack along with her other attacks. {{pc22}}You can reverse the effects of your choices in conversation by typing the following into the console: SetPapyrusQuestVar DLC1NPCMentalModel ToldPlayerSheDidntWantCure_var False. You will now be able to convince her to get cured. If she still refuses to talk about being cured, type the following into the console: SetPapyrusQuestVar DLC1NPCMentalModel CutOffCureDiscussion_var False. You can force the quest to start by typing the following into the console: setstage DLC1SeranaCureSelfQuest 10. If the Serana cure quest should become stuck you can use setstage DLC1SeranaCureSelfQuest 100 to finish the quest after stage 10 and have Serana back, without her vampirism. After she is cured, the following conversation occurs: :''"There you are. I'm ... I'm back."'' :'''You're not a Vampire anymore?''' :''"All clean. I feel like I can breathe again for the first time since I was turned. The world is alive, and so am I, for once."'' :'''I was wondering when I'd see you again. ''' :''"Here I am. Human as ever. If dismissed as a follower after Kindred Judgement (player joined vampires): :''"I'll be at Castle Volkihar if you need me."'' ==Unused Dialogue== Serana has a unique death line that goes unheard due to her being essential at all times: :''"Nooo!"'' == Notes == *Serana is voiced by noted voice actress [[wikipedia:Laura Bailey (voice actress)|Laura Bailey]]. ([[imdbname:1154161|IMDb]]) She would return to voice [[Online:Isobel Veloise|Dame Isobel Veloise]] in ''[[ON:High Isle|The Elder Scrolls Online: High Isle]]''. *Serana's hairstyle is unique to her, and is not available to the player in [[Skyrim:Character Creation|character creation]] or [[Skyrim:Galathil|appearance changes]]. *Depending on your dialogue choices, at some point during or after [[Skyrim:Chasing Echoes|Chasing Echoes]], you can ask Serana to marry you. However, she will refuse indefinitely, stating that even walking near a temple scares her. Despite this, she will follow you into any of the temples during normal travel. She will not marry you even if she has been cured of vampirism. *If Serana is a follower and you have lycanthropy, corpses she has reanimated can still be killed and fed on before they vanish completely. Bloodlust will still be extended and perk progress will still be made. *While following you, Serana interacts with most activators, which sometimes results in odd behavior. She tends to use any nearby [[Skyrim:Activities#Crafting|crafting]] apparatus, sit in most chairs on her own or even on the floor, chop firewood, mine ore veins, read books, eat food, dance, drink, and clap for bards at taverns. If she has reanimated a corpse, it will join in and perform similar tasks. *When indoors, Serana's reanimation spell is able to penetrate walls and revive dead bodies you cannot see. *Even after you finish the Dawnguard main questline, Serana remains an essential character and can never be killed. This can make her a very valuable follower, as she is already quite powerful. {{Bug|If Serana is cured of her vampirism, she will still wear her hood outside, and still complain about the weather. She will also still be able to use her [[Skyrim:Vampiric Drain|vampiric drain]] spell in combat.|USLEEP|3.0.1|The vampiric drain spell will be removed from Serana's spell list if she is cured of her vampirism.}} *When Serana is initially rescued, she will join you in addition to whatever follower you currently have. However, during the quests Chasing Echoes and Beyond Death, she will replace any follower you currently have active, and will be unable to be dismissed until those quests are over, though the option to do so is present. *If you're a normal vampire, Serana will still be willing to turn you into a Volkihar vampire. However, she will not offer to do so during the quest Chasing Echoes. *If you bring Serana to [[Skyrim:Solstheim|Solstheim]]{{DB}}, she may comment on the island's lack of vegetation. *Due to her unique voice type, Serana cannot be asked to [[Skyrim:Rebuilding_the_Blades|join the Blades]]. *If she is wearing her default armor, she will automatically wear or take off her hood depending on where she is. If she is given new armor to wear, then she will not automatically switch back and forth, but will constantly wear her hood if she had it on when she was given the new armor, unless she is given a helmet. She will wear new armor if it has a higher armor stat than Vampire Royal Armor; if she is given new boots or gauntlets to wear, but still has the Vampire Royal Armor, she will continue to wear and take off her hood. *If she is given tempered Vampire Royal Armor, her displayed inventory for trading will not show it being worn. However, her Damage Resist value in the console will increase by the tempered amount. *The dialogue to start Serana on the path to curing her vampirism is only available if she is following you. If she is no longer a follower and you speak with her, the necessary options will not appear. *During Unseen Visions, her RefID inside the Ancestor Glade temporarily changes to "xx00feca". It returns to normal when you exit the cave after receiving the vision. *The Elder Scroll on her back is actually a unique item with "xx01a958" baseID. When equipped this item occupies the "arrow" part of the body. *Serana's exact age is unknown, though judging by some of her comments, she appears to predate the middle of the [[Lore:First Era|First Era]]. She doesn't know that Cyrodiil is the headquarters of an Empire (it happened in 1E 143); she may therefore be between 4,000 and 5,000 years old. If so, this would make her one of the oldest non-divine beings in the game; rivaling [[Skyrim:Dragons|dragons]] and [[Skyrim:Miraak|Miraak]]{{DB}}. ==Bugs== {{Bug|During the quest Chasing Echoes, Serana may repeat the question, "Yes? What did you need?" any time the Dragonborn gets too close in proximity to her. When standing still she will continue asking this question indefinitely.|dlc=DG|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|When Serana is your follower, she may not return to a walking position after sneaking.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} **You can use the console to teleport past the gate if Serana was bugged when you get there. The command is to get in is (change any number by 1 to get out): cow Tamriel -44,36 **Going to the sneaking position yourself, then changing instance (fast-traveling or changing zones), then going back to the walking position may cure this, at least until the next time she gets stuck in sneaking position. If that doesn't work, you can order her to perform an action on an object, forcing her to switch her animation. If you are unable to command her, you can also stand around without taking action near an interactable object for a few moments, such as a chair, or enchanting table, her idle behavior will cause her to use nearby objects which will fix the issue. **{{pc22}} Disabling and re-enabling her with the console also fixes this. {{Bug|Serana may get stuck in combat after her target has died. Entering combat again fixes this only as long as the combat persists.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} **Use the [[Skyrim:Unrelenting_Force|Unrelenting Force]] shout or [[Skyrim:Sun Fire|Sun Fire]] spell on her, or attack her until she falls to her knees. **A powerful [[Skyrim:Pacify (effect)|Pacify spell]] such as Pacify or Harmony also fixes it, but requires the [[Skyrim:Master of the Mind|Master of the Mind]] perk unless she has been cured of her vampirism. For Imperials, [[Skyrim:Voice of the Emperor|Voice of the Emperor]] will also work, without the need for Master of the Mind. **{{pc22}}Open the console, select Serana by either clicking on her or entering the code prid xx002B74, then try these codes to fix her behavior: disable followed by enable, resetai, or moveto player. {{Bug|After being asked to "wait" or being dismissed as a follower, she may not have the option to follow again.|UDGP|2.0.2|dlc=DG}} **{{pc22}}Travel to Castle Volkihar and enter using the side Undercroft entrance. Wait a few seconds and Serana should appear behind you (and following already). If she doesn't, try using the Wait feature or exit the Undercroft and fast-travel to any location. When you arrive, Serana will be following you again. **{{Pc22}} To bring back the "Come with me" dialogue after dismissing Serana, enter the code sqv DLC1NPCMentalModel in the console. You are given a long list of information. Scroll down the list using the page up and page down keys, and make sure that the following codes: CanFollow_var = True / IsFollowing_var = True / IsWaiting_var = True / TurnOffComeWithMe_var = False / LockedIn_var = False are in order by looking at the false/true (i.e., if LockedIn_var was set to true then you need to put it to false). To do this, enter the following command: setpqv DLC1NPCMentalModel LockedIn_var False. Once you do this you should be able to recruit Serana to be your follower again. **To get Serana following again after asking her to "Wait", go somewhere far away (like inside Fort Dawnguard) and wait three to five days. **{{Pc22}} To fix this issue, enter the code sqv DLC1NPCMentalModel in the console. Scroll using the page up and page down keys to see whether IsWaiting_var = True. If so, set the value to "false" with the following console command: setpqv DLC1NPCMentalModel IsWaiting_var false. Serana should then follow at the distance set by her FollowDistance... variable values. {{Bug|Even after completing [[Skyrim:Touching the Sky|Touching the Sky]], Serana will sometimes say that she will meet you at [[Skyrim:Darkfall_Cave|Darkfall Cave]] when dismissed as a follower, though she will never go there.|UDGP|2.0.1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|Several of Serana's combat lines that were intended for dragons may appear when she fights anything due to misplaced "OR" conditions.|UDGP|2.1.3}} {{Bug|If you bring Serana to the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (place)|College of Winterhold]], she may complain about the sun, even when indoors.}} **{{Pc22}} You can use the console command setpqv DLC1NPCMentalModel LockedIn_var False to reset her status. {{Bug|Sometimes after completing the main questline for Dawnguard, while visiting a specific place (like Volkihar Courtyard), she will appear out of nowhere and act as if she were your follower even if she wasn't beforehand. If you dismiss her, however, you will never be able to recruit her again as the option "''Come with me''" will not appear.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|If you have both a [[Skyrim:Dog|dog]] follower and a humanoid follower when entering the cell to kill Harkon, she will continue to follow you in addition to your other two followers after you've completed the quest. This effectively allows you to have two humanoid followers and a dog. You can dismiss the humanoid follower and acquire another while still keeping Serana as a follower. After being cured of vampirism however you cannot have her as a "second" follower. Even if you try: dismissing your current follower, recruiting Serana, and then re-recruiting your now previous follower. |vn=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|Unlike other followers, the option ''"I need you to do something."'' does not appear while conversing with her as a follower. You will need to press and hold '''E''' ({{Pc22}}) or '''A''' ({{Xbox22}}) in order to issue commands to pick up, sleep, attack, etc.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|When you convince Serana to get cured of her vampirism and meet you back at Fort Dawnguard, after the short talk about being cured, she may only reply to dialogue options with ''"What do you need?"'' and ''"Yes?"'', making it impossible to take her as a follower again.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|Sometimes when Serana is your follower, you will acquire 'vampire skills' and yet not be a vampire (Champion of the Night, Nightstalker's Footsteps and Weakness to Fire).|vn=1|dlc=DG|confirmed=1}} **To remedy this effect, get infected with vampirism. Then, after telling Serana to wait somewhere, proceed with the quest to cure it. **This is often a result of having been hit by her Drain Life attack while engaging in close combat with an enemy, or simply from being between her and the enemy when she attacks it. Wearing a Necklace of Disease Immunity seems to prevent this bug from happening. {{Bug|If you bring Serana back to Dimhollow Cavern, she may become totally immune to any attacks.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} **Advance the primary questline of the College of Winterhold. The issue will be fixed when Quaranir freezes time. **This can also be fixed when the fight with Vyrthur commences. It seems that both he and Serana get set to ghost mode when the 'cutscene' starts, and restored to normal once it's over. **{{Pc22}} Highlight Serana in the console and type setghost 0. {{Bug|Sometimes when Serana wears her hood outdoors, the game creates a new copy of the hood for her to wear, which will eventually fill up her inventory with a number of identical hoods.|UDGP|1.2.2|dlc=DG}} **{{Pc22}} You can temporarily fix this using the console: clicking on Serana, and then typing showinventory and look for an item called [[Skyrim:Serana Hood|Serana Hood]]. The number of hoods she has will be shown on the console and using removeitem xx00E6A0 #, where xx is the code for the Dawnguard add-on (probably 02 or 03, and is shown by the returned results of showinventory) and # is the number of hoods she has, should be able to get rid of the extra hoods. Unfortunately, the game will start adding new hoods after that, necessitating using this fix again. {{Bug|While Serana is your follower if you use Vampiric Drain as a Vampire Lord the spell's damage decreases dramatically. This is the result of a condition on the Damage Health effect of the spell; if Serana is following you, the Damage Health effect will be reduced to zero points for all levels of the spell and only the Drain Health, Magicka, and Stamina will take effect.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|After the explosion of Eye of Magnus in College of Winterhold, Serana may disappear.|vn=1|dlc=DG}} **She returns to you when you enter Ancestor Glade during the Unseen Visions quest. {{Bug|Talking through Serana's dialogue tree in the Soul Cairn may cause her to stay in one place instead of following you, as if you had ordered her to wait (which you cannot do in the Soul Cairn).|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|After asking Serana to ''"Wait here."'' in an area where the dialogue option is possible and getting the response ''"Sorry, I'm not that easy to get rid of..."'', Serana may wait where asked but eventually reappear at your side (for instance, when approaching [[Skyrim:Knight-Paladin Gelebor|Knight-Paladin Gelebor]] for the first time triggers a conversation involving her), then continue to follow you, but at a great distance.|confirmed=1|dlc=DG}} {{Bug|Serana's eyes remain yellow after she's cured.|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|If you kill an undead creature with [[Skyrim:Dawnbreaker|Dawnbreaker]] while Serana is nearby, she may turn invisible.}} {{Bug|During the quest [[Skyrim:Bloodline|Bloodline]], she will refuse to take any orders from you or trade items with you. This can be used to give her equipment.}} {{Bug|In the Soul Cairn, she does not have the speech option to 'do something for you'. Just don't tell her to 'wait' or she'll get bugged.}}

Gain access to the College by either passing [[Skyrim:Faralda|Faralda]]'s test or persuading her to let you through (requires a [[Skyrim:Speech|Speech]] skill of 100), and head to the [[Skyrim:The Arcanaeum|Arcanaeum]]. Here you will find [[Skyrim:Urag gro-Shub|Urag gro-Shub]], who will fill you in on some of the Elder Scrolls lore and bring out two books for you: ''[[Skyrim:Effects of the Elder Scrolls|Effects of the Elder Scrolls]]'' and ''[[Skyrim:Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls|Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls]]''. Reading the latter starts the quest [[Skyrim:Discerning the Transmundane|Discerning the Transmundane]]; once you speak to Urag about [[Skyrim:Septimus Signus|Septimus Signus]], this quest will be completed. Alternatively, you can skip the College and head directly to [[Skyrim:Septimus Signus's Outpost|Septimus Signus's Outpost]] and talk to the man himself, which will also complete this quest. If you have already obtained and subsequently sold the Elder Scroll to [[Skyrim:Urag gro-Shub|Urag gro-Shub]] at the [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (place)|College of Winterhold]] (only possible after completing [[Skyrim:Alduin's Bane|Alduin's Bane]]), you must buy back the Elder Scroll. He'll sell it back for 4,000 gold, but he can be persuaded to sell it for half price if you are the Arch-Mage or 3,000 gold if you aren't. ==Notes== * If you're doing Discerning the Transmundane as part of this quest and have Serana with you, you may want to avoid Alftand to get to Blackreach, as she will frequently raise nearby corpses, including the ones you'll want later, during the blood harvest portion of that quest. ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |20||In order to discover the location of Auriel's Bow, I need to acquire the Elder Scroll that foretells the interactions of the dragons with the history of Nirn. ==Quick Walkthrough==
'''Note''': This quest does not appear in your journal.
# Investigate [[Skyrim:Robber's Gorge|Robber's Gorge]] for a secret trapdoor.
# Find the [[Skyrim:Bandit Leader's Journal|journal]] in [[Skyrim:Robber's Gorge#Robber's Cove|Robber's Cove]].
# Follow the clues to the bandit leader's secret treasure.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
===Ambush===
[[File:SR-place-Robber's Gorge.jpg|thumb|right|The camp near [[Skyrim:Karth River|Karth River]]]]
On the road between [[Skyrim:Rorikstead|Rorikstead]] and [[Skyrim:Dragon Bridge|Dragon Bridge]], near [[Skyrim:Karth River|Karth River]], a group of [[Skyrim:Bandit|bandits]] has taken over an old overhanging bridge and set up a clever method for ambushing travelers and caravans. As soon as you approach the bridge, the bandits will release a few [[Skyrim:Falling Boulders|boulders]] to block the path, then talk to you from their safe spot above: ''"All right, that's far enough. You know how this works- toll here is 100 gold."'' If you question the meaning of a "toll" in the middle of nowhere, you will be told: ''"Don't play dumb with me. Pay up, and you walk right through. Refuse, and you'll never see the other side."'' You can choose to pay the gold and they will let you pass unharmed, while the other options will make them turn hostile. Regardless of your choice, the bandit camp at [[Skyrim:Robber's Gorge|Robber's Gorge]] has been set up right next to the road, so head up there and the bandits will attack anyway. Kill the bandit guarding the entrance and deal with the three on the overhanging bridge, then enter Robber's Gorge through the door.

===Robber's Gorge===
[[File:SR-quest-Robber's Gorge 02.jpg|thumb|right|A cave with a clue]]
The huge camp is an extension of the ambush bridge and consists of several tents with bedrolls. A few bandits will attack you on sight as you enter. Your target is the wooden house in the southern section of the camp: the home of the Bandit Leader. He will attack the moment you enter, so defeat him and take a look around for the [[Skyrim:Archery|Archery]] skill book ''[[Skyrim:The Black Arrow, v2|The Black Arrow, v2]]'' on a table and a chest with some decent loot. The bandit leader carries a boss-leveled amount of gold along with the [[Skyrim:Key to Robber's Cove|key to Robber's Cove]]. Alternatively, a second key can be found on a dresser in one of the bedrooms. Claim the key and locate the trap door leading underground to the hidden cave, [[Skyrim:Robbers' Cove|Robbers' Cove]].

===A Paranoid Bandit Leader===
[[File:SR-quest-Robber's Gorge 03.jpg|thumb|right|The island to the south]]
The cove turns out to be a secret sanctuary for the bandit leader and is merely a small ledge and an underground lake filled with [[Skyrim:Salmon (creature)|salmon]]. Some food is present along with a docked boat, some weaponry, and an empty chest (this chest will contain the quest item if you are on one of the related quests). If you jump in the water, some more minor treasure can be found as well as several skeletons. Investigate the table and read through the ''[[Skyrim:Bandit Leader's Journal|Bandit Leader's Journal]]''. The pages reveal his worries about his relationship with his men and his fears about an upcoming mutiny. He apparently started to take some of the gold earned from the ambushes, a little bit of a time, and was waiting to gather enough gold to escape to Dragon Bridge. Lastly, after one of his companions unexpectedly visited the cove, the bandit leader decided to move his stash to a better location:

'''''"I don't think he found my stash, but it's not safe here. I took the boat out tonight and stowed it on the island to the south, by the old tree stump."'''''

Jump into the water and leave the cove through the southern exit. Keep swimming south and you will immediately see a waterfall. At the foot of the waterfall is the island described in the journal, including the old tree stump. Next to the stump is the bandit leader's stash hidden away in a chest, so use the key to unlock it and claim his ill-gotten gains for yourself.
