After this, the conversation follows with: 

:'''I have to know what Miraak knows if I want to stop him:'''
:''"Now that is a dangerous path indeed. Hermaeus Mora gives nothing away for free. You may end up like Miraak, of course. Two power-mad Dragonborn. It could be very interesting."''

[[File:SR-icon-book-Black Book.png|right|150px]]
Next, the conversation moves towards the Black Books where he admits owning one and knows the location of another: 

:'''Do you know where I can find another Black Book?:'''
:''"Oh yes. They're not hard to locate once you know how to look for them. I have one here that I have been using to locate more."''

:'''You have a Black Book?'''
:''"Yes I haven't been idle while this fascinating madness engulfed Solstheim. But my book isn't what you're looking for. I'm quite sure it is unconnected with this Miraak. But I do know where to find a Black Book that can help you."''

Next, two dialogue choices are presented:

:*'''So you know where to find this Black Book? The one connected with Miraak?:''' ''"Yes I do. I haven't been able to get it, though. But maybe together we can unlock the secrets the [[Lore:Dwemer|Dwemer]] left behind."''

::*'''The Dwemer? What do they have to do with this?:''' ''"Forbidden knowledge was somewhat a specialty of the dwarves, eh? You don't think they would just leave it alone, do you? It seems the ancient Dwemer discovered this book and took it to study. I have found their "reading room" in the ruins of Nchardak. The book is there, but it's sealed in a protective case which I wasn't able to open. But perhaps the two of us together will be able to get the book. To Nchardak, then. Follow me."''
::*'''Just tell me where the book is and I'll go get it:''' ''"I'm afraid it isn't that simple. If it was, I would have the book already."''

:*'''Why won't the book you have here help me?:''' ''"Oh, it clearly is not associated with the same power that has overtaken the island. And I'm not talking about Hermaeus Mora. These Black Books are all his, of course. No, what you're looking for is a specific book. Presumably because Miraak's power derives from it."''

This ends the conversation and Neloth heads off to the ruins of [[Skyrim:Nchardak|Nchardak]], located just north of Tel Mithryn, along the coast.

===City of a Hundred Towers===
<center>
{|cellpadding="10" cellspacing="10" width="85%"
|-
|style="border: dotted 1px black;background:#ebe0c8;"|
:<center>'''''"Nchardak, The 'City of a Hundred Towers'. In its day it was the largest of the great Dwemer Archives and perhaps the most advanced."'''''</center>
|}</center>
[[File:SR-npc-Neloth 03.jpg|thumb|right|''"The Dwemer certainly knew how to build for the ages. These towers have outlasted their creators by {{Sic|millenia|millennia}}."'']]
Once you reach the outskirts of Nchardak with Neloth, he will remark: ''"The Dwemer certainly knew how to build for the ages. These towers have outlasted their creators by {{Sic|millenia|millennia}}. The book is housed inside that dome. I'll need to unlock the door for us. Let's get on with it."''. If Frea accompanies you, she will comment: ''"The Skaal have always avoided ruins such as these. Nothing of the All-Maker is to be found within."''.

There will be a band of [[Skyrim:Reaver|reavers]] camped outside of the ruins that must be defeated first. Upon spotting them, Neloth cries: ''"I had to clean out the riff-raff last time I was here, too. Where do they come from?"''. Once they are dealt with head up to the main door. Neloth remarks: ''"Maybe now we can finally begin what we came here for."''. He then walks up to the main door and reveals that he sealed the ruins on his last visit: ''"The Dwemer of Nchardak appear to have been fond of these control pedestals. Luckily I found a cube to operate it inside on my last visit. I sealed the door when I left to keep out ignorant meddlers. Let me unlock it."''

=== Nchardak Reading Room===
Once inside, follow Neloth towards a large gold ring in the center of the room where the Black Book is held. He explains: ''"You can see the book right there. So tantalizingly close...But trust me, no magic will open that. I'd have had the book already if I could. No, we'll have to do this the hard way. If we can restore the steam supply to this room, I'm certain I can open it. As you'll see, that's easier said than done. This way to the boilers."''

Next, Neloth uses his [[Skyrim:Control Cube#Control Cube|control cube]] to open another door where an elevator leading to the Nchardak Great Chamber is located. Follow him down the elevator into the next area.

===Nchardak Great Chamber===
[[File:SR-npc-Neloth 04.jpg|thumb|right|''"There seems to be an inexhaustible supply of these Dwemer contraptions."'']]
Upon entering, Neloth reveals: ''"The last time I was here, I only explored a small part of the ruins. I was here alone then, and I find an assistant is absolutely essential for this kind of dirty, dangerous work."'' as he walks down the stairs. When you get to a fork, Neloth will go to the left, but to the right there's a hole that you can drop into to find a chest.

Upon reaching the main chamber, Neloth exclaims: ''"Nchardak, The 'City of a Hundred Towers'. In its day it was the largest of the great Dwemer Archives and perhaps the most advanced. In the old stories, when the Nords came to conquer it, it's said the Dwemer sumberged the entire city beneath the sea until the invaders gave up. I have my doubts. But the city was a marvel of Dwemer engineering. Now... reduced to this."'' If you have brought Frea with you, she'll remark: ''"Amazing to think that they built this so long ago, and it still survives."''

Follow Neloth to a control pedestal overlooking a large flooded area where he activates the pumps with his cube. As the water begins to drains, he reveals: ''"The pumps only operate when a cube is in the pedestal. And unfortunately, I have only one cube. These four boilers provide steam to the room upstairs. They're shut down, but they still respond to the control cubes. So, if we can find four more cubes, we can turn these boilers back on and restore steam power to the room upstairs. Then I should be able to open the book's protective case. Bring that cube. We'll need it."''

Pick up the control cube from the pedestal and follow Neloth over to a display panel that he begins to study. He reveals: ''"Yes... here we are. This device shows the location of four more cubes in this section of the city. It looks like most of the cubes were moved to the lower levels, perhaps to try to control the flooding before the city was abandoned. Interesting. That would suggest that the city must have originally sunk during the first cataclysm of Red Mountain. Or that the Dwemer's servitors continued to try to preserve the city after their creators' disappearance."''

Before entering the Nchardak Workshop, he remarks ''"Three of the cubes are through here. This seems like a sensible place to start. You should be able to unseal this door with the control cube I gave you."'' Once you place the cube in the control switch, the large brass seal that covers the door retracts and Neloth heads into the workshop. If you neglected to pick up the cube, he'll mention: ''"You'll need a cube to unlock this door. I hope you remembered to pick up the cube I placed in the pedestal."''

At this point it's possible to ask him to explain the details again, via two dialogue options. These are: 

:'''How do we get the book out of its case?:''' ''"It won't be easy. The whole lower part of the city is flooded, which has shut down the boilers which supply steam to the reading room. If we can restore the steam supply, I'm certain I can open the book's protective case."''

:'''Why do we need these cubes?:''' ''"I thought I made myself clear the first time. The boilers in the Great Hall provide steam to the reading room upstairs, which we need in order to open the book's protective case. We need a total of five cubes - one to operate the pumps in the Great Hall, the other four to activate the boilers."''

===Nchardak Workshop===
<center>
{|cellpadding="10" cellspacing="10" width="85%"
|-
|style="border: dotted 1px black;background:#ebe0c8;"|
:<center>'''''"Much of the Dwemer army at the Battle of Red Mountain must have come from here."'''''</center>
|}</center>
[[File:SR-npc-Neloth 11.jpg|thumb|right|''"These must be the "Great Workshops of Nchardak".]]
Upon entering, follow Neloth over to a nearby control switch that contains a cube. He remarks: ''"I hope the rest of the cubes are this easy to find. Although knowing the Dwemer, I rather doubt it."''. The cube also controls the jets of fire in the next hallway. If Frea is present, she'll tell you ''"It would be madness to go through there."''. If you continue without taking the cube, Neloth will note: ''"Wouldn't it be easier just to turn off the trap? Like so?"'' and take the cube. Then follow Neloth down to the next area. 

[[Skyrim:Dwarven Spider|Dwarven spiders]] will be found down here; once they have been dealt with head over to a bridge stretching over another flooded area. Several [[Skyrim:Dwarven Centurion|Dwarven centurions]] can be seen lining the walls of this chamber. Follow Neloth as he remarks: ''"These must be the "Great Workshops of Nchardak". Impressive even in ruins. In the city's days of glory, it was reputed to be able to assemble a complete automaton in a single day. Much of the Dwemer army at the Battle of Red Mountain must have come from here."''. Even Frea will admit: ''"It is rather impressive."''

Walk over the bridge to reach two control pedestals. Neloth remarks: ''"It looks like we'll need to lower the water level to make any more progress."'' Place a cube in either pedestal to lower the water level; however this also results in a few Dwarven automatons appearing. Once they have been defeated, proceed down to the ground level and place a cube in the control switch to expand a set of stone stairs. Next, head up and around the walkway to the small brass bridge and place the cube in a second control switch to raise the bridge. Next, walk up the stairs and head left at the intersection to reach a brass gate. Open the gate and take the control cube that can be found behind it. Picking up the cube will result in the water level rising again, and Neloth will start to make a comment about how unfortunate this is. However, taking the cube also causes some Dwarven spiders to appear nearby, so Neloth's statement will almost certainly be cut short. Defeat the spiders and make your way back to the top of the room. 

Pick up the cube you left on a pedestal, which will result in the water level rising much higher than it was originally. Then proceed to the door on the southern side of the room. Neloth will remark, ''"Let's see where this leads"'', as he follows you through the door and into a narrow corridor which descends into a shallow, collapsed obstruction. If the first cube on the bridge was not collected, Neloth will state ''"There's a passage up there. We could reach it if the water level was higher."'' Otherwise, he will say: ''"With the water level this high, we can swim across the collapsed part of the passage and reach the other side."''. Swim through and defeat any Dwarven spiders and [[Skyrim:Dwarven Ballista|Dwarven ballistae]] that appear in this section. At the end of the hall the fourth cube can be found on a pedestal. Taking this cube will result in the water level rising yet again, and a Dwarven centurion awakening from its gantry. Once it's been dealt with, walk up the small staircase near the Centurion and activate the control switch, lowering a bridge which leads back toward the Great Chamber.

===Return to the Great Chamber===
Upon arrival in the Great Chamber, Neloth will walk over to the large flooded section and explain that the last cube is through the northern door, however the water must be completely drained in order to proceed. Place two cubes on the pedestals on the upper area to drain the water. Dispatch the automatons triggered by the cube placement, and follow Neloth down the curved pathway towards the northern passage. Two Dwarven ballista are guarding the northern door; once they are dealt with ascend the short staircase activate the control switch on the left side of the doorway, then open the large brass seal and head into the Nchardak Aqueduct.

===Nchardak Aqueduct===
[[File:SR-npc-Neloth 10.jpg|thumb|right|''"I'd guess that must be the pump activator up there. But how to reach it?"'']]
Follow Neloth until he spots several raised bridges and remarks: ''"Looks like we'll need those bridges down in order to get the pumps in here working."'' As he walks deeper into the chamber, he adds: ''"The last cube is somewhere in here. I hope it won't require more swimming around in this filth."'', which is answered by Frea with ''"You should leave slogging around in the muck to us youngsters."'' if she is present. Eventually, Neloth spots a small alcove on the upper floor and says: ''"I'd guess that must be the pump activator up there. But how to reach it? We'll need to get all three of these bridges down in order to reach the pump control."''

Turn around and walk up the ramp to an upper platform with three control switches overlooking the aqueduct. The sequence to lower all three bridges is the right switch, then the left switch. Once the correct combination is entered, and all three bridges lowered, Frea will congratulate you with ''"I think you did it."'', and Neloth will snap: ''"That's it! Don't touch anything else. Quickly now."'' before running across the bridges. To the south of the control switches is an apprentice-locked chest and a dwarven warhammer to loot.

Cross the bridges and defeat the Dwarven automatons that appear. The control pedestal is located on the upper platform on the eastern side of the room. Activating it with a cube will drain the water, allowing access to the last chamber. As the water begins to lower, Neloth comes up with a plan for the final cube: ''"I have an idea. I'll wait here and retrieve this cube once you find the last one we need. Good luck!''". If Frea is around, she will comment: ''"Finally. We will not have to listen to his complaining."''

Head down to floor level and find the control pedestal on the left side of a large bronze doorway on the western side of the room, on the opposite wall from the platform you used to lower the water level. Insert the cube to open the brass seal, then through the tunnels to reach a small room lined with traps. The first trap is a pressure plate activated set of iron bars that slam shut near the entrance. Next are two spinning blades in front of the gate that holds the final cube. Use [[Skyrim:Whirlwind Sprint|Whirlwind Sprint]] to dart across them and place a cube in the control pedestal on the right hand side of the gates to turn off the blades and open the doors. Be careful here as there is yet another pressure plate which activates poisoned darts just before the pedestal. Taking the last cube will raise the water level. Swim back to the aqueduct chamber, where Neloth will be waiting.

Once he sees the final cube has been obtained, he will greet you with ''"Do you have the cube? Good, good! Then I'll take this cube and we can be on our way."'' and remove the control cube from the pump activator. He then will warn you: ''"Watch out, the water's rising even higher with both pumps shut down."'', which Frea responds to with sarcasm: ''"Thanks for the warning."''. Neloth will then say, ''"That was easier than I expected. I'm glad you were here to do all the hard work. With the cubes I retrieved, we should now have a total of five. I hope you haven't left more scattered about. With the cube I retrieved from the pumping pedestal, we should now have five cubes - exactly what we need. Now we can finally see about getting those boilers started."''. Frea will then again express her skepticism toward Neloth: ''"Now we will see if he knows what he is talking about."'' Before leaving, swim and climb to the northeast chamber of the Aqueduct, just north of where Neloth was waiting by the pump control pedestal. A Dwarven Ballista guards the chamber. There is a table in the room with the [[Skyrim:Kagrumez Resonance Gem|Kagrumez resonance gem]], a weapon, a piece of armor, and some Dwemer scrap laying on it. There is also a chest on the table with loot. There is more Dwemer scrap under the table, and on a shelf on the south side of the room. The [[Skyrim:Kagrumez Resonance Gem|resonance gem]] might fall to the ground during the battle with the Ballista. Be sure to check before abandoning the room if it isn't on the table with the chest as it is very small and easy to miss. 
Return to the southern door and pass through to meet Neloth in the Nchardak Great Chamber.

===Activate the Boilers===
Head up the ramp to the main control pedestals. Pick up one of the original cubes already in the pedestals and head down to the lower platform. Place the remaining four cubes in the boiler pedestals to start the boiler. As the boilers are activated, Neloth comments: ''"That seems to have done it. Good. It took longer than I'd hoped, but at least it's finally done. "'' but then cries out ''"Look out! Another Steam Centurion!"'' as a Dwarven centurion awakens from its station at the far side of the great chamber bridge. Once it has been dealt with, he remarks: ''"I'm going to head back upstairs and see if the reading room has steam. If so, it should be a simple matter to release the book."''

Before heading back to the Nchardak Reading Room, you may wish to head over the bridge to the centurion's holding cage, where a boss-level chest can be found.

*Note: leave the activation cubes in the control pedestals.

===The Black Book===
<center>
{|cellpadding="10" cellspacing="10" width="85%"
|-
|style="border: dotted 1px black;background:#ebe0c8;"|
:<center>'''''"At last. I hope it was worth it. Please... be my guest. You deserve the first look."'''''</center>
|}</center>
[[File:SR-npc-Neloth 08.jpg|thumbnail|right|''"Aren't you going to read it? I thought that was the whole reason you dragged me out here."'']]Upon reaching the reading room, Neloth will be waiting by the control pedestal, where he remarks: ''"Now that the boilers are working, it should be simple to release the book from {{sic|it's|its|description=erroneous apostrophe}} protective case."'' 

Press the button on the pedestal to cause four beams of light to shine up from the floor and focus on a large crystal above. This also causes the room to rumble and the Black Book to rise up from the floor. Neloth remarks: ''"At last. I hope it was worth it. Please... be my guest. You deserve the first look. Besides, it could be very dangerous. These books are known to drive many people insane."''

The Black Book is revealed to be ''[[Skyrim:Black Book: Epistolary Acumen (book)|Epistolary Acumen]]''. As you begin to read the book and enter the realm of [[Skyrim:Apocrypha (Epistolary Acumen)|Apocrypha]], Neloth jokingly parts with: ''"Oh good. Be sure to say hello to Hermaeus Mora for me if you see him."''. This begins the next quest: [[Skyrim:The Gardener of Men|The Gardener of Men]].

===Reward===
Once the quest is completed, the Black Book ''[[Skyrim:Black Book: Epistolary Acumen (book)|Epistolary Acumen]]'' will be accessible. The book grants one of three [[Skyrim:Powers#Abilities|abilities]] once Apocrypha has been traversed: [[Skyrim:Dragonborn Force|Dragonborn Force]], [[Skyrim:Dragonborn Flame|Dragonborn Flame]], or [[Skyrim:Dragonborn Frost|Dragonborn Frost]].

===Achievements===
One [[Skyrim:Achievements#Dragonborn|achievement]] is unlocked when you complete this quest:
* {{Achievement|The Path of Knowledge (achievement)|descr=no}}

== Notes ==
*Progressing far enough into the quest [[Skyrim:Unearthed|Unearthed]] and acquiring [[Skyrim:Ahzidal's Boots of Waterwalking|Ahzidal's Boots of Waterwalking]] makes going through the rising water of the dungeon less of a hassle, although it is advisable to take them off before grabbing the final cube.
*If [[Skyrim:Frea|Frea]] is a follower, she will frequently comment on Neloth's instructions and plans.
*There are some areas in Nchardak that you do not have to visit to complete this quest, such as the southeast room in the Aqueduct and the floor of the Great Chamber. However, these areas are only easy to reach during, or shortly after, this quest. See [[Skyrim:Nchardak|Nchardak]] for details.
*You can use Whirlwind Sprint or the Vampire Lord's Bats ability to short-circuit the bridges in the Aqueduct. Simply jump over the gap on the eastern side, then back again. If you only have one word of Whirlwind Sprint, stand on the rocks to gain a little extra height before the first jump. You won't be able to cross back the other way, but if you jump on top of the light, you can then jump onto the ledge and take the roof up to the pedestal from there. You can get Neloth past the bridges by simply waiting an hour. You'll still have to deal with most of the area's enemies, but bypassing the bridges gives you early access to the eastern rooms so you don't have to come back again later.

==Quick Walkthrough==
'''Note''': This quest does not appear in your journal.
#Travel to [[Skyrim:Forelhost|Forelhost]].
#Defeat the [[Skyrim:Lost Paladin|Lost Paladin]] and take [[Skyrim:Chrysamere (item)|Chrysamere]].

==Detailed Walkthrough==
[[File:SR-npc-Lost Paladin.jpg|thumb|right|Face the Paladin in battle]]
'''Note: This quest was originally added to your journal upon installing the [[Skyrim:Chrysamere|Chrysamere]] [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation]]. With the release of the [[SR:Anniversary Edition|Anniversary Edition]], this quest no longer appears in your journal. Nevertheless, the reward can still be obtained by finding the artifact yourself.'''

This is a non-journal quest that takes place at [[Skyrim:Forelhost|Forelhost]]. You will likely need to navigate the entirety of the dungeon in order to reach the quest objective. Alternatively, it is possible to jump up onto the high outcropping to the left of the battlements, and use [[Skyrim:Whirlwind Sprint|Whirlwind Sprint]] to land on the battlements.

When you reach the Forelhost Battlements, you'll find the [[Skyrim:Lost Paladin|Lost Paladin]] in front of the [[SR:Word Wall|Word Wall]] wielding [[Skyrim:Chrysamere (item)|Chrysamere]]. You will be able to take the blade once you kill the ghost. Be advised that you may also have to fight [[SR:Captain Valmir|Captain Valmir]] if you are completing the quest [[SR:Siege on the Dragon Cult|Siege on the Dragon Cult]] at the same time.

===Taking the Shortcut===
It isn't necessary to navigate all the way through Forelhost to get to the upper Battlements. In fact, this is not recommended because it can start another side quest entitled Siege on the Dragon Cult which can make the final battle more difficult as noted above. It usually starts by speaking with Captain Valmir, whose campsite can be seen in the courtyard just outside the dungeon's main entrance, but sometimes there are different triggers. If the quest is initiated it may cause the Lost Paladin to fail to appear once on the Battlements, sometimes even if the quest is completed. In order to skip the dungeon entirely, simply begin jumping up the incline next to the Forelhost Battlements before entering the courtyard and you can eventually work your way up to the top, where the ghost will be waiting near the Word Wall.

==Notes==

==Detailed Walkthrough==
===Inner Darkness===
[[File:SR-quest-Through A Glass, Darkly 02.jpg|thumb|right|The Shadow]]
Once you've installed the [[Skyrim:Shadowrend|Shadowrend]] [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation]], you will receive this quest. The journal entry will inform you that an inner voice is drawing you to a geyser pool in [[SR:Eastmarch|Eastmarch]] in order to confront the darkness within yourself. The geyser can be found near the [[SR:The Atronach Stone|Atronach Stone]], to the northeast of it. Stand with the Atronach Stone at your back and walk toward a trio of pine trees in the water. Continue past the leftmost tree. The pool contains skeletal remains which have stained the water black, and will only begin to froth when you approach.

Above this anomaly, a weapon will appear. It is [[Skyrim:Shadowrend (item)|Shadowrend]], a shadow weapon from the ruins of [[Lore:Milchar|Milchar]] in the [[Lore:Shivering Isles|Shivering Isles]]. Shadowrend is both a [[SR:Greatsword|greatsword]] and a [[SR:Battleaxe|battleaxe]], and it will proceed to cycle between each version, with the weapon warping in and out of existence until you attempt to take it. Touching the weapon will summon a [[SR:Shadow|Shadow]] enemy named "[player]'s Shadow". It is a shadowy clone of you, meaning it will wear your equipment and know all of your [[SR:Spells|spells]], powers, and [[SR:Shouts|shouts]].

Defeat the Shadow and claim Shadowrend from its remains to complete the quest. Whichever version of the weapon you didn't select will reappear above the pool, where it will hang in the air indefinitely. You can return to the pool any time in order to switch between the two versions of Shadowrend. You must have it in your inventory for the swap to function, otherwise it will say, "You lack the required item." Each version is a powerful Daedric weapon in its own right, with a 15% [[Skyrim:Weakness to Magic|weakness to magic]] enchantment.

==Notes==
* Shadowrend originally [[SI:Shadowrend|appeared]] in the ''[[SI:Shivering Isles|Shivering Isles]]'' expansion for ''[[OB:Oblivion|Oblivion]]''.
*[[ON:Online|ESO]] also features an unrelated [[Online:Shadowrend|clannfear]] and [[Online:Shadowrend (set)|item set]].
* The [[Skyrim:Shadow|Shadow]] seems to be a valid target for the [[Skyrim:Ebony Blade|Ebony Blade]].
* The Shadow may choose to instead attack nearby [[SR:Bandit|bandits]].
* The name of this quest is a Biblical phrase from 1 Corinthians 13:12 (KJV).
** It also appears quite similar to the name of another quest in ''Oblivion'', [[OB:Through A Nightmare, Darkly|Through A Nightmare, Darkly]].

The cave is filled with [[SR:Warlock|warlock]] and [[SR:Skeleton|skeleton]] enemies. The quest marker will lead you to an "Ancient Tome Chest" in a reading area found roughly halfway through the dungeon. For more precise directions, see the [[Skyrim:Hob's Fall Cave#Hob's Fall Cave|dungeon walkthrough]]. Open the chest to complete the quest.

The chest contains all 16 [[Skyrim:Arcane_Accessories_Items#Spell Tomes|new spell tomes]] added by the Creation. Reading these will teach you the following spells:

==Detailed Walkthrough==
===Smuggled Goods===
Travel to an [[Skyrim:Unmarked Places#Unmarked Bandit and Forsworn Camps|unmarked bandit camp]] located beneath a cliff, west of [[Skyrim:Dragonsreach|Dragonsreach]] {{Map Link|x=22032|y=3456|zoom=17}}. Once there, you must deal with the hostile [[SR:Bandit|bandit]]s and locate the ''[[SR:Smuggler's Trade Notes|Smuggler's Trade Notes]]'' (not to be confused with the ''[[SR:Smugglers' Note|Smugglers' Note]]'' located nearby). Reading it will reveal that the smugglers were recently approached by an [[SR:Orc|Orc]] looking to purchase the [[Skyrim:Staff of Hasedoki (item)|Staff of Hasedoki]], a legendary artifact which they had recently sold to someone else. The smugglers sold this Orc the location of the buyers, planning to intercept and ambush him. Be wary if you are looting the camp, as opening the nearby chest will cause more bandits to spawn.
[[File:SR-quest-The Staff of Hasedoki 02.jpg|thumb|right|[[SR:Boneman|Bonemen]] fill the passages of Brittleshin Pass]]
The ambush site is located along the road west of [[SR:Whiterun|Whiterun]], next to the ruined house near the [[Skyrim:Western Watchtower|Western Watchtower]] {{Map Link|x=-4648|y=-8009}}. The Orc in question, [[SR:Modig Gilgar|Modig Gilgar]], will be found standing over the bodies of multiple bandits. He will turn hostile if you get too close, so you are left with the option to either kill him or pickpocket him to obtain the ''[[SR:Smuggler's Ledger|Smuggler's Ledger]]''. Reading this will reveal the location of the buyers: [[Skyrim:Ivara of Olenveld|Ivara of Olenveld]] and [[Skyrim:Lushak gra-Ragdam|Lushak gra-Ragdam]], located in [[Skyrim:Brittleshin Pass|Brittleshin Pass]]. Be sure to check Modig's cart for loot, including a copy of ''[[SR:To Raise the Living|To Raise the Living]]'' as well as a container named Modig's Satchel which holds minor loot.

===A Path to the Soul Cairn===
You must now venture to [[Skyrim:Brittleshin Pass|Brittleshin Pass]], and enter either through its north or south entrance. Taking the southern approach will result in marginally fewer enemies to face. The enemies in question are [[Skyrim:Boneman|bonemen]], which appear in addition to the usual undead [[SR:Skeleton|skeleton]]s encountered in Brittleshin Pass.

You will need to make your way to the inner sanctum, where the boss level [[Skyrim:Necromancer|necromancer]] would usually be present. In his place, you will find Lushak gra-Ragdam and Ivara of Olenveld, two necromancers who will be hostile on sight. Beware Ivara, as she wields the Staff of Hasedoki. She can repeatedly use the staff to immobilize you. Once you've defeated them both, the remaining bonemen will disappear, leaving you free to loot and exit the cave. Lushak carries copies of ''[[Skyrim:Arkay the Enemy|Arkay the Enemy]]'' and ''[[Skyrim:The Black Arts On Trial|The Black Arts On Trial]]'', the latter being an [[Skyrim:Illusion|Illusion]] skill book. Ivara carries copies of ''[[Skyrim:The Light and the Dark|The Light and the Dark]]'', ''[[Skyrim:Ivara's Notes|Ivara's Notes]]'', and ''[[Skyrim:Souls, Black and White|Souls, Black and White]]'', as well as the Staff itself. Reading her notes will reveal that the two necromancers traveled all the way from the island of [[Lore:Olenveld|Olenveld]] to open a portal to the [[Skyrim:Soul Cairn|Soul Cairn]] and offer Hasedoki's soul to earn the favor of the [[Skyrim:Ideal Master Crystal|Ideal Masters]]. Loot his Staff from Ivara's corpse to end this plot and complete the quest.

The Staff creates a permanent 40-point [[Skyrim:Ward|ward]] protection while being held, and when cast it will ragdoll and forcefully knock targets backwards. (This includes you during your fight against Ivara.) If the target then dies within 60 seconds, they will be [[Skyrim:Soul Trap (effect)|soul trapped]]. 
{{NewLine}}

==Notes==
* Ivara, Lushak, and the three bonemen will spawn in Brittleshin Pass as soon as Modig Gilgar is killed or pickpocketed. Reading the ledger is optional. Brittleshin Pass is not reset by this. If you have not cleared it previously, Ivara will kill the necromancer boss, clearing the dungeon.
* Completing the quest will cause Modig Gilgar and his cart to immediately disappear.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
In order to start the quest, you need to read ''[[Skyrim:The Crimson Dirks, v4|The Crimson Dirks, v4]]'' in [[Skyrim:Candlehearth Hall|Candlehearth Hall]]. It recalls a tale where a young Bosmer named [[Skyrim:Fathrys|Fathrys]] had hoped to wed Zaharia. She dismissively rejected him by saying that she would only accept him if he were to give her a dragon scale. Hearing this, the drunken bandit mage Antonius regaled an old Nord legend where the warrior [[Skyrim:Ulfnir Bone-Skin|Ulfnir Bone-Skin]] slew the dragon Vithrelnaak, fashioning armor from his scales and ultimately burying it with him. Antonius claims that Ulfnir's corpse protects this armor through death in the barrow near [[Skyrim:Yorgrim Overlook|Yorgrim Overlook]].

With this, the quest directs you to Yorgrim Overlook to investigate. When you reach the overlook, you will find the lifeless skeleton of Fathrys holding his ''[[Skyrim:Poem for Zaharia|Poem for Zaharia]]''. You will be attacked by two generic skeletons and the skeleton of Ulfnir Bone-Skin himself. Defeat them and loot the [[Skyrim:Overlook Key|Overlook Key]]. With it, you can unlock the gate.

Claim the [[Skyrim:Studded Dragonscale Armor|Studded Dragonscale Armor]], [[Skyrim:Studded Dragonscale Boots|Studded Dragonscale Boots]], [[Skyrim:Studded Dragonscale Gauntlets|Studded Dragonscale Gauntlets]], and [[Skyrim:Studded Dragonscale Helmet|Studded Dragonscale Helmet]] from the chest. With this quest completed and the [[Skyrim:Smithing#Skill_Perks|Dragon Armor perk]], you will be able to craft more Studded Dragonscale items.
{{NewLine}}

==Notes==
*If Yorgrim Overlook is visited before you have read the book, the two skeletons will still attack you, but neither Fathrys' nor Ulfnir's skeletons will be there. Defeating the two skeletons will clear the location. The gate can still be unlocked and the chest looted, but there will be no Dragonscale armor. If the quest is attempted after doing this, Fathrys and Ulfnir will appear as normal and the armor will be added to the chest.
**By clearing Yorgrim Overlook and unlocking the gate before reading ''The Crimson Dirks, v4'', you will be able to easily retrieve the armor and complete the quest without defeating Ulfnir.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
This quest can be started after [[Skyrim:Spirits Away|Spirits Away]] has been completed by talking to [[Skyrim:Viriya|Viriya]]:
:'''Know of anyone in need of fishing work around Skyrim?'''
:''"You're headed to the capital. It's all in this note."''

She then hands you a [[Skyrim:Wanted: A Seafood Feast|note]] that requests [[Skyrim:Steamed Mudcrab Legs|Steamed Mudcrab Legs]], [[Skyrim:Cooked Arctic Char|Cooked Arctic Char]] and a bowl of [[Skyrim:Crab Stew|Crab Stew]]. This will likely involve [[SR:Cooking|cooking]].

You should have access to plenty of [[SR:Crab Meat|Crab Meat]] and [[SR:Mudcrab Legs|Mudcrab Legs]] after completing the [[Skyrim:Spirits Away|previous quest]], and the other ingredients needed for the stew are not hard to acquire. [[SR:Butter|Butter]] can be a little trickier to find, although you can simply make your own at a churn if you've [[SR:Construction|constructed]] a [[Skyrim:Kitchen|kitchen]]. If you don't wish to go fishing for an [[SR:Arctic Char|Arctic Char]], you can go diving at [[SR:Hela's Folly|Hela's Folly]] instead and catch one with your hands.

Once you have obtained all three dishes, head to [[Skyrim:The Winking Skeever|The Winking Skeever]] and set the upstairs table for [[Skyrim:Gisli|Gisli]]. She will sit down to eat, which will take her an hour. Once she's finished, she'll leave a [[Skyrim:Gisli's Note|note]] and a [[Skyrim:Coin Purse|coin purse]] on the plate.

==Quick Walkthrough== 
# To start this quest head to the Frozen Hearth inn within Winterhold. 
# Go inside and into one of the rooms to find [[Skyrim:Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v1|Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v1]].
# Head to the [[Skyrim:Frostroot Cave|Frostroot Cave]] and find the [[Skyrim:Nchuanthumz|Nchuanthumz]] entrance.
# Access Nchuanthumz's Manufactory
# Find the Argonian [[SR:Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts|Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts]]'s body near a control panel. Examine the corpse for clues.
# Read [[Skyrim:Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v2|Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v2]].
# Use one of the two buttons to activate the Dwarven Sphere Overseer.
# Collect 3 Dwemer Cogs, 3 Dwemer Actuators and a Dwemer Oil.
# Return to the Dwarven Sphere Overseer and bring the manufactory back online. 
# Collect a Centurion Dynamo Core and use it to construct a Dwarven Spider Renovator.
# Summon the Dwarven Spider Renovator to clean a section of the house.
# Wait 24 hours for the renovations to finish. A few rooms will be fully renovated and furnished. 
# Repeat this 2 more times to fully renovate the home.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
Go to [[SR:The Frozen Hearth|The Frozen Hearth]] in [[SR:Winterhold|Winterhold]], [[SR:Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v1|Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v1]] is on a table in the left room when facing to the innkeeper, read it to start the quest. Quest maker will direct to [[SR:Frostroot Cave|Frostroot Cave]]. Head to and enter the cave, fight three bandits and walk along a short way to Nchuanthumz.

Once you enter [[Skyrim:Nchuanthumz|Nchuanthumz]], head straight and deal with a few skeevers and three bandits until you reach the lift to Nchuanthumz's Manufactory. Use the lift and then continue straight forward until you reach the corpse of [[Skyrim:Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts|Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts]], examine the body to find a [[Skyrim:Dwemer Actuator|Dwemer Actuator]] and his [[Skyrim:Seeks-Ancient-Artifacts' Journal, v2|second journal]]. 

The journal lists the items required to repair the assembly lines, with the required items being one [[Skyrim:Dwarven Oil|Dwarven oil]], three [[Skyrim:Dwemer Cog|Dwemer cogs]], and three Dwemer Actuators. The room already contains everything you need. You should already have one Dwemer Actuator from Artifacts' own inventory; the other two are on the two tables on either side of the room, alongside the cogs and the oil. Collect all the required items and activate the Dwarven Sphere Overseer button. The quest markers will direct you to press either the right or left button to do so. 

The Dwarven Sphere Overseer will emerge from the scuttle on the right side of the room. Follow the Dwarven Sphere Overseer and give it the repair parts by interacting with it. You can then activate the manufactory; if you already have a [[Skyrim:Centurion Dynamo Core|Centurion Dynamo Core]] then you can head straight to the room on the left, however if you don't have one, go to the room on the west side of the manufactory to find a destroyed Dwarven Centurion Master, whose body has a core on it. 

Place the Centurion Dynamo Core into the Dynamo Actuator and then activate the button next to it. This will build a Dwarven Spider Renovator, head back to the lift and go back up to Nchuanthumz. There are three sections of the house to clear with the spider, each takes 24 hours once the spider is summoned using one of the levers. Once all three sections are complete, the quest will finish and you will have a fully furnished Dwarven house.

==Detailed Walkthrough==
[[File:SR-quest-The Unquiet Dead.jpg|Rin and the old well|right|thumb]]
You can start this quest by either asking an innkeeper for work until they give you [[SR:Bounty - Restless Spirits|Bounty - Restless Spirits]], or you can simply head straight to Goldenhills Plantation.

As you arrive at [[Skyrim:Goldenhills Plantation|Goldenhills Plantation]], a ghost will attack you, after dealing with it you can collect the [[Skyrim:Torn Page|torn page]] next to the corpse of [[Skyrim:Urval|Urval]]. Head inside and go to the top floor to find [[Skyrim:Urval's Journal|Urval's journal]] which shows that Urval accused his wife of being a witch before attacking her, after which she appears to have poisoned him. The next step is to find her secret laboratory to uncover the truth, head down to the basement and look to the right as you enter, there is a button on the wall by the door, press it and the cupboard will move to reveal the secret lab.

Enter the laboratory and the ghost of [[SR:Jonquil|Jonquil]] will appear and attack you, after dealing with her, read the [[Skyrim:Jonquil's Journal|journal]] on the apothecary table to discover the truth about what occurred at Goldenhills Plantation. After their son disappeared, Urval and Jonquil killed each other, Jonquil with extract of Deadly Nightshade, Urval with an axe each thinking that the other had murdered their son, Rin. To put their spirits to rest you need to discover what happened to Rin.

Head back upstairs to Rin's room, and look under his bed to find his [[Skyrim:Rin's Journal|journal]] which mentions that he was going to go to the old well to hunt a wolf. Leave the building and head southeast towards [[Skyrim:Gjukar's Monument|Gjukar's Monument]], as you are heading towards it, look to the left and you will see the old well surrounded by wolves. Once you have dispatched the wolves, take [[Skyrim:Rin's Toy Sword|Rin's toy sword]] from the child's skeleton. 

[[File:SR-quest-The Unquiet Dead 03.jpg|right|thumb|Urval, Jonquil and Rin]]

Take the toy sword into Rin's room and place it under the Imperial banner, the ghosts of Urval, Jonquil and Rin will appear behind you. Speak to Rin:
:'''Your family can rest in peace now.'''
:''"Thanks a lot! Here. Take this. For all your hard work."''

The [[Skyrim:Key to Goldenhills Plantation|key]] to the plantation will be placed in your inventory as a reward. The next quest, [[SR:A Farmer's Life For Me|A Farmer's Life For Me]] will then automatically start when you leave the house.

{{NewLine}}

==Notes==
*There's a [[SR:Unobtainable_Items#Nord_War_Horn|Nord War Horn]] in Rin's room, which is unobtainable otherwise, a unique Alembic in [[SR:Jonquil|Jonquil]]'s secret lab, a [[SR:Ores_and_Ingots#Broken_Iron_War_Axe_Head|Broken Iron War Axe Head]] and a [[SR:Ores_and_Ingots#Broken_Iron_War_Axe_Handle|Broken Iron War Axe Handle]] in the box on the second floor. They will disappear once the rooms are renovated.

== Detailed Walkthrough ==
===The Pit Dungeon===
[[File:SR-interior-The Pit Dungeon.jpg|left|thumb|The dungeon hallway]][[File:SR-interior-The Pit Dungeon 04.jpg|The set of iron armor|right|thumb]]
After you choose the power option during [[Skyrim:A Dying Wish|A Dying Wish]], you will pass out and awaken in a dungeon only wearing ragged robes and ragged boots. Exit the cell and you can explore the hallway and other cells. One cell has a dead hunter in it, and another a dead Thalmor soldier with a full set of Elven light armor. You can also pick up a set of iron armor and a health potion on the table in the main hallway. The optional objective "Search the dungeon for more information" refers to [[Skyrim:Prisoner's Note|Prisoner's Note]], in a bucket in one of the cells.
{{NewLine}}

===The Pit===
As you enter the arena, you will have to fight a [[Skyrim:Pit Fighter|Pit Fighter]] and a [[Skyrim:Wolf|wolf]]. Once they have been killed, the two [[Skyrim:Sabre Cat|sabre cats]] will be released from their cages and you will have to kill them. The pit champion, [[Skyrim:Neski Skull-Sabre|Neski Skull-Sabre]] will then enter the arena, kill her and you can then loot her body for the [[Skyrim:Bittercup_Items#Bittercup|Bittercup]], [[Skyrim:Grand Champion's Sword|Grand Champion's Sword]], and the [[Skyrim:Grand Champion's Helm|Grand Champion's Helm]]. She also carries the note [[Skyrim:On the Bittercup|On the Bittercup]].

There is a large number of dead bodies laying about the pit, these are; a [[SR:Breton (dead)|Breton]], [[SR:Hunter|hunter]], [[SR:Reaver|reaver]], [[SR:Master Vampire|master vampire]], [[SR:Khajiit (dead)|Khajiit]], [[SR:Wood Elf (dead)|Wood Elf]], and the [[SR:Corpse|corpse]] of an Imperial soldier. There are also two skeletons that can be looted as well.
{{NewLine}}
===Watchtower Barracks===
[[File:SR-quest-The Pit 02.jpg|left|thumb|The Pit Boss]][[File:SR-interior-Watchtower Barracks.jpg|right|thumb|Your belongings]]

You will then have to pull the lever next to the door in order to enter the [[Skyrim:Watchtower Barracks|Watchtower Barracks]]. Climb the stairs and you will have to enter the room on the left in order to kill the [[Skyrim:Pit Boss|Pit Boss]] and the two [[Skyrim:Pit Bandit|Pit Bandits]]. Loot the pit boss for the [[Skyrim:Pit Key|pit key]], which can be used to retrieve your belongings from the chest in the previous room with an iron door. There is also a [[Skyrim:Pit Fighter's Note|note]] next to the chest, with a flawless diamond, amethyst and an emerald on top of it.

You can then unlock the door to Skyrim, where you will be near the [[Skyrim:Falkreath Watchtower|Falkreath Watchtower]]. The quest will then be complete.
{{NewLine}}

==Notes==
*In the Pit, most attacks can be avoided by jumping on top of the hay stacks, especially while battling Neski.
*It is possible to use the [[Skyrim:The Ritual Stone|Ritual Stone]] to reanimate the dead bodies. At lower levels, this will make the fight significantly easier.
*All belongings that can't be dropped will stay in the inventory, which could prove useful.
*The upper gallery containing archers seems to be inaccessible. But after regaining your equipment you can wreak vengeance on them from below, for example with a bow or by conjuring an ally at the gallery level, or use destruction spell [[SR:Unbounded Storms|Unbounded Storms]].

Skyrim:The Pilgrim's Path.wikitext: {{Cleanup-srqrp |writtenBy= |checkedBy= |reward= |rewardChecked= }}{{CC Header|Divine Crusader}}{{Trail2|Divine Crusader|Quests|nocat=1}}{{Quest Header |notrail=1 |Icon=SR-qico-Miscellaneous.png |Giver= |Loc=See below |Reward=Removes the detrimental effects from equipping the Relics of the Crusader |Prev= |Next= |Image=SR-place-Four Skull Lookout.jpg |Imgdesc=Four Skull Lookout |description=Repent your sins by going on a pilgrimage. |ID=ccMTYSSE001_Quest |Mod=[[Skyrim:Divine Crusader|Divine Crusader]] }}[[Category:Skyrim-Quests]][[Category:Skyrim-Divine Crusader]][[Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Quests]] ==Quick Walkthrough== # Go to [[Skyrim:Four Skull Lookout|Four Skull Lookout]] and acquire the Crusader's armor. # Equip any piece of the armor. # If required, pray at each of the nine shrines. ==Detailed Walkthrough== Start the quest by equipping any piece of Crusader's armor, found at [[Skyrim:Four Skull Lookout|Four Skull Lookout]], between [[Skyrim:Karthwasten|Karthwasten]] and [[Skyrim:Karthspire|Karthspire]]. If your Infamy (see [[#Notes|notes]]) is higher than 0, and you are wearing a relic of the crusader, this quest will be started on an independent 12 hour cycle, or when any relic is updated (equipped/unequipped) with the following message: ''"Your crimes have made you unfit to wield the Crusader's Relics. Make the pilgrimage to repent your sins and once again seek the favor of the gods."'' Once the quest has started, you will be required to cleanse your soul by visiting the various shrines, similar to the Oblivion quest. All items may be equipped and unequipped freely, regardless of your Infamy. However, the active effect 'Relics of the Crusader' will impose Health and Stamina 300 regeneration penalties and Carry Weight is reduced by 100 while you are 'unfit'. {| class="wikitable" |+ colspan=3|Shrine Locations ! Index !! Shrine Of !! Location !! Cell Code !! Map |- | 1 || Akatosh || North of [[Skyrim:Rorikstead|Rorikstead]] || POITundra31 || {{Map Link|x=-84223|y=15342|zoom=17}} |- | 2 || Arkay || Southwest of [[Skyrim:Ironbind Barrow|Ironbind Barrow]] || WaywardPassExterior || {{Map Link|x=76286|y=63066|zoom=17}} |- | 3 || Dibella || South of [[Skyrim:Old Hroldan|Old Hroldan]] || POIReach16 || {{Map Link|x=-114063|y=-15486|zoom=17}} |- | 4 || Julianos || Southeast of [[Skyrim:Tumble Arch Pass|Tumble Arch Pass]] || POISnowy28 || {{Map Link|x=70163|y=26773|zoom=17}} |- | 5 || Kynareth || Northeast of [[Skyrim:Brood Cavern|Brood Cavern]] || POITundra17 || {{Map Link|x=-49995|y=48825|zoom=17}} |- | 6 || Mara || Northwest of [[Skyrim:Volunruud|Volunruud]] || POISnowy05 || {{Map Link|x=2173|y=34962|zoom=17}} |- | 7 || Stendarr || In the tower at [[Skyrim:Stendarr's Beacon|Stendarr's Beacon]] || StendarrsBeaconExterior01 || {{Map Link|x=197800|y=-116644|zoom=17}} |- | 8 || Talos || Mountains east of [[Skyrim:Lakeview Manor|Lakeview Manor]] || POIPineForest21 || {{Map Link|x=-2829|y=-68419|zoom=17}} |- | 9 || Zenithar || West of [[Skyrim:Four Skull Lookout|Four Skull Lookout]] || POIReach30 || {{Map Link|x=-137323|y=21616|zoom=17}} |} The shrines of Arkay and Stendarr are the easiest to find as they have a map marker for them. The shrine of Julianos is the hardest, as it just barely emerges from the snow and only a half-buried skeleton is there to mark it. ==Notes== *Infamy is the total of your: Murders + Assaults + Pockets Picked + Horses Stolen + Items Stolen + Trespasses + Jail Escapes. *Trespasses and Assaults are the main ways players can quickly become frustrated by the armor, due to being put into situations that are not usually considered morally wrong. Examples include: -Initiating combat, or using a negative spell effect against a target who has not been marked in red on the compass, even if they are actively committing a crime like attacking civilians, The entry sequence in Markarth is an example, as are dragon attacks. Some enemies who are always inherently hostile can be attacked without consequence, though there are exceptions most would not expect, like many bandits technically being "neutral" and only being "hostile" when you get too close -Your follower/summon/horse doing the above listed "crime" (it will count towards you.) -Using dragonrend on a target that has not been marked in red on the compass. (including Alduin the World-Eater) -Attacking a resting draugr (sometimes, inconsistent). -"Trespassing" in Hod's home when it's open, much like the Dragonsreach Jarl's Quarters. (it's not usually counted as trespassing once you gain affinity with the related owners) -Trespassing in the Thalmor embassy. -Killing Astrid when she abducts you. -Cannibalism/feeding as a vampire (this one actually makes sense but may not always be considered as most players would not think it would count as assault) *Some actions notably do '''not''' increase these infamy values like one might expect. These can be helpful for players that are committed to using this armor long term. Examples include: -Lockpicking or opening locks using the Tower Stone ability, or Fenrik's Welcome. -Melee Killcams will not count as assaults (but will count as murder if the target was innocent) -Killing Grelod the Kind is not murder or assault if killed with a melee killcam. -Transforming into a werewolf/vampire lord, because transformations add to a bounty directly rather than being counted as a crime in the statistics page (though feeding usually counts as assault.) -Other actions that add a bounty but change nothing else in the crime statistics page. (notably some quests will do this) *The armor will not always start the Pilgrims Path quest immediately when you reach your 1 infamy limit, though will almost always update once you equip/re-equip a new piece of armor. This can make the armor seem even more unfair and arbitrary. *If you get too close to a shrine, the regular effect may be triggered and your progress won't update. If this happens, step back from the shrine a little and try again. ==Bugs== {{Bug|The quest can restart while it is already in progress if your Infamy increases. This will cause all of your current shrine progress to reset, but those shrines will no longer be displayed as quest targets.}} ** {{Pc22}} In the [[Skyrim:Console|Console]], use the setstage X where X is the index of the location, as displayed in the table, above. {{Bug|The quest can clear the map while it is in progress. This will retain your current shrine progress, but other shrines will no longer be displayed as quest targets.}} {{Bug|The quest can restart while it is already in progress without an increase in infamy. This will cause all of your current shrine progress to reset.}} {{Bug|Worshipping at the Shrine of Mara may not register, requiring you to use the console to complete the quest.}} {{Bug|The Shrine of Dibella incorrectly gives the Blessing of Akatosh.|modnotes=POIReach16, ccMTYSSE001_ShrineActivator doesn't have the custom properties set on the TempleBlessingScript.|confirmed=1}} {{Bug|The quest will trigger if anything causes a criminal act to be registered, even other bugs. For example, attacking a sleeping Draugr will erroneously incur an assault bounty, triggering the quest when any relic is re-equipped.|confirmed=1}} *The quest will trigger even while doing a quest objective that requires a crime. *The quest can apparently restart even after completion, even if you have not gained any infamy since completing it, even if all you do is wield one of the weapons to try and put it on a weapon rack. ==Quest Stages== {{Journal Entries |10||I have committed acts that have made me unfit to wear the Crusader's Relics. You're finally awake."'']] [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 06.jpg|thumb|right|Fellow prisoners, Lokir and Ulfric Stormcloak]] You begin the game to find yourself bound at the wrists and under Imperial guard custody in a prisoner caravan. In the carriage with you is Ralof (a [[Lore:Stormcloaks|Stormcloak]] soldier), [[Skyrim:Lokir|Lokir]] (a horse thief), and [[Skyrim:Ulfric Stormcloak|Ulfric Stormcloak]] (leader of the Stormcloak rebellion and Jarl of [[Skyrim:Windhelm|Windhelm]]). Ralof sits across from you, with Lokir next to him and Ulfric to your right. [[Skyrim:Hadvar|Hadvar]], an Imperial Soldier, is riding a horse behind your cart, while [[Skyrim:General Tullius|General Tullius]], is riding a horse in front of the first cart. As revealed by [[Skyrim:Ralof|Ralof]], you are all prisoners of the [[Skyrim:Imperial Legion|Empire]], who had set an ambush for the Stormcloaks near [[Skyrim:Darkwater Crossing|Darkwater Crossing]]. You and Lokir were caught up in the same action, though at the time you had been crossing the border, and Lokir had stolen a horse. Despite this, you and Lokir were arrested as potential Stormcloak sympathizers and are now being sent to Helgen for execution. The carriage soon reaches [[Skyrim:Helgen|Helgen]], a town in [[Skyrim:Falkreath_Hold|Falkreath Hold]] not far from the southern border of Skyrim. At the time of your arrival, [[Skyrim:Siddgeir|Falkreath's Jarl]] is loyal to the Empire, and the hold is controlled by the [[Skyrim:Imperial Legion|Imperial Legion]], though the Stormcloaks have some presence in the area, hiding in a [[Skyrim:Falkreath Stormcloak Camp|camp]] within the Hold. As you enter Helgen, Ralof will make a comment about General Tullius, [[Lore:Skyrim|Skyrim]]'s military governer, on horseback by an [[Skyrim:Imperial Captain|Imperial captain]], facing First Emissary [[Skyrim:Elenwen|Elenwen]], also on horseback, and two [[Skyrim:Thalmor|Thalmor soldiers]] flanking her on foot. The carriage will ride through the village and draw to a stop in the central area of the town. The Imperial captain orders you and the other prisoners off the carts, then instructs you to proceed to the execution block as your name is called. Hadvar will first call Ulfric Stormcloak, and then Ralof. When Lokir is called, he will attempt to flee, but will always fail, since the Imperial captain will have him shot by an archer. After this, Hadvar will then demand you to step forward. ===Who Are You?=== [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 07.jpg|thumb|left|''"Who are you?"'']]When Hadvar asks for your identity, you'll need to take a moment to decide. {| class="hiddentable" | :: '''Game: ([[Skyrim:Character Creation|Create and name your character]].)''' |} Once you've created and named your character, Hadvar will make a comment based on your race. {{Showhide/Start|Possible Comments}} {| class="wikitable" !Race !!Dialogue |- |rowspan=2 |'''[[Skyrim:High Elf|Altmer]]''' ||You're not with the [[Skyrim:Thalmor Embassy|Thalmor Embassy]], are you high elf? At least you'll die here, in your homeland. |- |rowspan=2 |'''[[Skyrim:Orc|Orc]]'''||You from one of the [[Skyrim:Orc_Strongholds|strongholds]], Orc? How did you end up here? |- |I'm sorry. We'll make sure your remains are returned to [[Lore:Hammerfell|Hammerfell]]. |} {{Showhide/End}} {{NewLeft}} ===Keep Your Head=== The captain will order your death even though your name is not on the list. You will be forced to follow her to the executioner's block and after a brief confrontation between General Tullius and Ulfric Stormcloak a distant noise will echo across the sky. [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 10.jpg|thumb|Right|''"What was that?"'']] The general will dismiss it as nothing and order that the executions begin, and a [[Skyrim:Priestess of Arkay|priestess of Arkay]] will begin to administer the last rites to the condemned. A Stormcloak soldier will interrupt her and is promptly executed, and the captain will then order you to step up to the block. An ominous sound will again echo through the mountains, this time louder. Most of the assembly will be briefly distracted, but the captain will not be put off by this. You will be ordered to the block and forced into position, ready to be executed. From that perspective, you should have a view of the headsman and the tower behind him. As the headsman raises his axe, a [[Skyrim:Dragon|dragon]] known as [[Skyrim:Alduin|Alduin]] flies into the scene. {{NewLeft}} ===Return of the World-Eater=== The dragon will descend onto the nearby tower with a crash and proceed to use a special shout that turns the sky red and sends flaming meteors crashing down, which eventually damages the city beyond repair, knocking the headsman to the ground. [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 13.jpg|thumb|right|Alduin begins his attack on Helgen.]] The second shout he uses, [[Skyrim:Unrelenting Force|Unrelenting Force]], will stagger you. However, Ralof will urge you to your feet to escape, reasoning that the gods may not provide another chance. When you are able to stand, you'll be able to move about freely, and the quest will appear in your journal. ===Make Your Way to the Keep=== [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 16.jpg|thumb|left|''"In here! This way! Come on!"'']]If you are able to get your bearings soon enough, you can follow right behind Ralof. If it takes you a little time, Ralof will go into a tall tower to the south-southwest and call to you: ''"In here. This way! Come on!"'' Follow him into the tower as fireballs rain down from the sky and boulders fly off in all directions from the explosions. Despite the apparent danger, you will have no trouble getting into the tower unless you loiter in unsheltered areas for an extended time. Enter the building far enough so that the door can close behind you. Inside, you'll see two injured Stormcloaks and another tending to them. The same three that were on the first cart alongside the male Stormcloak executed before you. Stepping onto the carpet in the middle of the small room and turning back around toward the door will position you to observe a conversation between Ralof and Ulfric. At this point you cannot pick-up or interact with items with your hands, as they are bound. No one cuts your bonds. [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 18.jpg|thumb|left|Alduin's shout blasts through the stairway.]][[File:SR-quest-Unbound 17.jpg|thumb|right|Alduin attacks.]] Both Ralof and Ulfric will urge you to hurry up through the tower. Follow Ralof up the staircase. When a Stormcloak soldier up ahead tells you that some fallen masonry needs to be moved out of the way, the wall to your right (southeast) will be blown in by Alduin. He will then attack through the hole with a [[Skyrim:Fire Breath|Fire Breath]] shout. Though you cannot perceive it as such, Alduin will shout ''"Toor... Shul!"'' meaning ''"Inferno... Sun"'' in the [[Lore:Dragon Language|dragon language]]. This shout will knock Ralof off the stairs, but he will climb back up to you. The gods may indeed be providing you some extra protection, at least for now—you will not be hurt by the shout, even if you don't heed Ralof's warning to step back. Eventually, however, once you venture outside of Helgen, encounters with dragons will prove much more dangerous. After Alduin flies off, Ralof will urge you to jump out the hole just created and down into a partially destroyed inn below, telling you that they will follow as soon as they can and meet you on the other side. Your target landing spot will be indicated by your objective marker. Move to the ledge and jump while continuing to move forward. If you go downstairs in the tower before jumping, you'll find Ralof tending to the wounds of the two injured Stormcloaks. While the third Stormcloak that was doing that before is now crouching next to Ulfric. On landing, you may hear yourself grunt in pain, but you will only take minor damage. Travel eastward through the inn and drop down through the hole in the floor. Your objective marker will indicate the next waypoint. Follow Hadvar, the Imperial soldier you just saw near the execution block. He will be outside the door from the inn, and to your left (northeast), trying to help some citizens. Hadvar will be trying to coax a young boy, [[Skyrim:Haming|Haming]], away from an open area where his father, [[Skyrim:Torolf|Torolf]], lies injured in the road. As the boy returns toward Hadvar, Alduin will land to the northeast and send a Fire Breath shout toward Hadvar and the boy, killing Torolf. Hadvar will take Haming to safety back near the inn with another man, [[Skyrim:Gunnar Stone-Eye|Gunnar Stone-Eye]], and leave the boy in his care. When he sees you, Hadvar will address you as "prisoner" and tell you to follow him if you want to stay alive. [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 20.jpg|thumb|right|Ralof: ''"Jump and keep going! We'll meet you later!"'']] Follow Hadvar as he proceeds northeasterly across the area where Alduin just killed Torolf. Hadvar's purpose at this point is to ''"Find General Tullius and join the defense"'' of Helgen. Passing between a building and a stone wall, Hadvar will stop and advise you to stay near the wall. Alduin will then land on top of the wall and direct a Fire Breath shout at a Legionnaire ahead of you and to the right, around the corner. Once Alduin takes flight again, follow Hadvar up the steps and then to the left (northward) through the gap in the wall. Inside the ruined building, jog to the left, then turn right (eastward). You will exit into an open area where a number of [[Skyrim:Imperial_Mage|Imperial mages]], soldiers, and General Tullius will be counter-attacking Alduin with arrows and fireballs. {{Multiple Images |align=left |direction=horizontal |width=150 |image1=SR-quest-Unbound 26.jpg |caption1=Follow Hadvar to the northeast. |image2=SR-quest-Unbound 27.jpg |caption2=Turn to the left (northward). |image3=SR-quest-Unbound 28.jpg |caption3=Hadvar: ''"Stay close to the [left] wall."'' |image4=SR-quest-Unbound 29.jpg |caption4=Alduin lands and attacks again. }} {{Multiple Images |align=left |direction=horizontal |width=150 |image1=SR-quest-Unbound 30.jpg |caption1=Follow Hadvar up the steps... |image2=SR-quest-Unbound 31.jpg |caption2=...then to the left (north). |image3=SR-quest-Unbound 32.jpg |caption3=Jog around to the left, then turn right (eastward). |image4=SR-quest-Unbound 33.jpg |caption4=Soldiers and mages counter-attack the dragon. }} {{NewLeft}} [[File:SR-quest-Unbound 03.jpg|Choose your path|thumb|right]] When Hadvar approaches General Tullius, the general will order him into the Keep, announcing a retreat. Telling you to stay close to him, Hadvar will head north, then turn left towards the entrance to the Keep. ::Note: Hadvar should be taken seriously when he tells you to stay close to him. If you tag fairly close behind him at this point, Alduin will not harm you. If you choose to lag behind or explore the area, however, you will do so at your own considerable risk. Eventually, Alduin's shouts may hit you between this point and entering the Keep. He can use the Fire Breath shout and the less serious [[Skyrim:Unrelenting_Force|Unrelenting Force]] shout. If you are hit with the former, it may or may not kill you. The latter will violently shove you or may send you flying for a short distance. Once you reach the exterior of the Keep, if you remain outside for an extended period, Alduin may land and attack with a shout at close quarters or physically with his jaws, an attack that will be fatal. After running under an archway, Hadvar will encounter Ralof just outside the Keep. The two enemies will draw their weapons and prepare to fight before realizing that getting into the Keep and away from the dragon is a higher priority. As Hadvar and Ralof rush to two different but nearby entrances to the Keep, both calling to you to follow them, your journal will update to show the objective of making your way to the Keep as completed, and the next objective will appear, presenting you with a choice. ===Unsafe Haven=== :''Note: After entering the Keep, depending on whether you chose to enter with Hadvar or Ralof, the part of the interior map which you emerge in and the initial events that occur will differ slightly.'' {| cellpadding=10 |{{C|2}} If you choose to go with Ralof, you will discover the body of a dead Stormcloak, [[Skyrim:Gunjar|Gunjar]], in a circular room immediately after entering the keep. After freeing you from your bindings, Ralof will instruct you to recover the gear on Gunjar's body for your own use. While you equip yourself, Ralof will examine the doors. He will discover one door is locked, and the other can't be opened from the side you're on. Luckily, the captain and an Imperial soldier will come through and open the door secured from the other side. Once they open the door, you will be forced to kill them to recover the key to the other gate from their bodies. Don't forget to loot the barracks they came from. |{{AL|T}} {{C|2}} If you choose to go with Hadvar, you will enter the keep to find yourself in the barracks room where Hadvar will cut your bonds and instruct you to loot the room for some equipment. Once you have acquired some gear from the marked chest, he will open a gate and you will follow him down a path to the circular room containing Gunjar's body. Here you will face two hostile Stormcloaks. Once they are defeated, follow Hadvar onward through the opposite door. |} :''From here onward, the physical path taken by both Hadvar and Ralof is identical. Only the type of enemies and the accompanying dialogue is different: for Hadvar's path you face Stormcloaks, while for Ralof's path you face Imperial soldiers.'' Going through the door onto the now opened-up path, the dragon's activities above will cause the ceiling to fall, forcing you to divert through a door on your left, where you will discover a storeroom with two Imperial soldiers/Stormcloaks gathering supplies. After defeating the enemies, Hadvar or Ralof will advise you to go through the barrels for any valuables they may contain. Continuing down, you will arrive at an interrogation room, where a battle between an Imperial [[Skyrim:Torturer|torturer]], his [[Skyrim:Torturer's Assistant|assistant]], and some Stormcloak soldiers is taking place, prompting you to fight with whichever enemies your escort is not aligned with. If you are with Hadvar, he has a conversation with the torturer, trying to convince him to come; his attempts prove futile, however, as only the assistant torturer follows. If you're with Ralof, he has a quick conversation with the surviving Stormcloaks, who will both choose to join your party. Hadvar/Ralof will then point to a cage with a dead [[Skyrim:Mage|mage]] and several valuables inside it (including mage [[Skyrim:Novice Robes|robes]], and [[Skyrim:Novice Hood|hood]] and a [[Skyrim:Sparks|Sparks]] spell tome), offering you several lockpicks, and suggesting you [[Skyrim:Lockpicking|pick the lock]] to get to the items. If you are not near Hadvar/Ralof when he offers you the picks, you will not get them, but there are a couple of picks in the room in the corner that also contains an iron shield and iron mace, as well as four picks inside a [[Skyrim:Knapsack|knapsack]] laying on a small table near the cells. The table also holds a copy of ''[[Skyrim:The Book of the Dragonborn|The Book of the Dragonborn]]''. There are two empty, locked cells on either side of the dead mage, and two other locked cells down the hall (this is a safe chance to practice the lockpicking skill, as well as learning the game mechanic). Continue down the corridor past some prison cells which can be unlocked for some minor loot, and through another prison room, and you will eventually enter a natural cave, filled with either Imperial soldiers guarding it for General Tullius, or some lost Stormcloaks. There is an [[Skyrim:Oil Slick|oil spill]] that can be set alight to damage the enemies on the upper level using the [[Skyrim:Flames|Flames]] spell. After the enemies are killed, the allied Stormcloak soldiers or torturer's assistant will stay in the room if they survived the assault, leaving you and Ralof/Hadvar to continue alone. You will find a raised drawbridge obstructing your path. A nearby lever can be used to lower the bridge, which will subsequently be destroyed by falling rubble shortly after you cross it. Continuing on, you will come to a skeleton near the passage leading towards another large cavern inhabited by several [[Skyrim:Frostbite Spider|frostbite spiders]]. Near the skeleton is an iron dagger, a potion of minor healing, and a coin purse. Once you defeat the spiders, head through a passage leading deeper into the caverns. In the next chamber, near an underground stream, you will encounter a resting [[Skyrim:Bear|bear]]. Ralof/Hadvar will advise you to [[Skyrim:Sneak|sneak]] past it, but he will give you a bow and some arrows in case you choose to ambush it. Fighting the bear is not too difficult with Hadvar/Ralof helping you. Afterwards, follow Hadvar/Ralof and exit the cave through a crevice in the rock. Leaving the dungeon, you'll see Alduin flying off into the distance, towards the north, completing the quest. ===Achievements=== One [[Skyrim:Achievements|achievement]] is unlocked when you complete this quest: * {{achievement|Unbound (achievement)|descr=no}} ==Notes== *For all intents and purposes, choosing to side with Hadvar or Ralof doesn't matter, as you aren't locked out of any quest chain. The only difference between the two paths is the type of loot and enemies inside the keep, and the rewards given for helping them escape (given during the next quest). At the end, you will still have the option of choosing to side with the Empire or the Stormcloaks. *Both Hadvar and Ralof are essential NPCs at this point, so they cannot die, and will never turn hostile (unless you're an Altmer and cast Fury on them) until the quest is finished. This can be exploited to level up your attack skills ([[Skyrim:Destruction|Destruction]], [[Skyrim:One-handed|One-handed]], [[Skyrim:Two-handed|Two-handed]], and [[Skyrim:Archery|Archery]]) and [[Skyrim:Sneak|Sneak]] skill early in the game. You won't be able to pickpocket them, though. *The game always starts with a [[Lore:Calendar#Skyrim_Calendar|calendar]] date of the 17th of Last Seed, making this quest the only one in the game with a fixed date. The day of the week can vary, though: **If you had a game loaded immediately before starting your new game, the day of the week will be whatever it was before you exited back to the main menu. **If you did ''not'' have a game loaded, the day of the week will be Sundas. *You will always know the spells [[Skyrim:Flames|Flames]] and [[Skyrim:Healing|Healing]] by the time you start the quest, regardless of your race, and depending on your race, other spells will also be known: **[[Skyrim:High Elf|Altmer]] will also know [[Skyrim:Fury|Fury]]. **[[Skyrim:Breton|Bretons]] will also know [[skyrim:Conjure Familiar|Conjure Familiar]]. **[[Skyrim:Dark Elf|Dunmer]] will also know [[Skyrim:Sparks|Sparks]]. *You may wish to see the main page for [[Skyrim:Skyrim|Skyrim]] for information such as using [[Skyrim:Controls|controls]] and our [[Skyrim:First_Time_Players|guide for first-time players]]. *If you take too long to make your way up the stairs in the tower, Ralof and Ulfric will tell you to hurry up. **Likewise, if you take too long to make your way to the keep, Hadvar and General Tullius will do the same. *If you wait around in any one area for too long, Alduin will begin specifically targeting you. *It is possible to exit Helgen very early in the quest. Follow Ralof and Ulfric into the tower, then bring up the map in your journal and fast travel to Helgen. You'll appear outside the gates and free to roam around, but there are some conditions: **Your hands will remain bound at all times. **The camera will be stuck in first-person view. **The sky will have an orange dragon-like tint during the day. **Your inventory, spells, and character menu will be unavailable. **You can discover locations, but you won't be able to clear any dungeons. **You can sprint, but you'll have to wait until your stamina replenishes naturally. **The ability to sleep, sit, wait, cast spells, and use racial powers will be absent. **The 2 alternating music tracks that play when making your way to the keep will play non-stop. **If you enter Helgen Keep through the exit this way, the bridge will already be destroyed. **You'll neither be able to finish the quest nor earn the achievement. ***This feature won't be available if [[Skyrim:Survival Mode|Survival Mode]] is active, as fast travel will be disabled. *If you clip through the walls in the barracks in the Keep, you may fall and end up in the storage room. No one else will be present in the storage room, and you can freely search it. There is also a chance that the torturer, torturer's assistant, and the 2 Stormcloak soldiers in the torture room won't be hostile to you or each other, and you can freely talk to them. The 5 frostbite spiders and the bear in the cave aren't affected by this, though, and will still attack on sight. **Be warned, however, that once Hadvar or Ralof are freed from the key-locked gate, the 2 enemies in the storage room will come back, and the hostilities between the torturer, torturer's assistant, and the 2 Stormcloak soldiers in the torture room will return. Also, if you make your way to the cave and go back the other way, the bridge may still collapse in front of you. *It is possible to save [[Skyrim:Torolf|Torolf]] and the Legionnaire. When the dragon lands in front of Torolf and you are quick enough you can run past Alduin and he will fly off, not harming him. With the Legionnaire you have to be quick enough as well. If you get to him before Alduin lands on the wall, you can sprint into him, knock him into the building and Alduin's fire breath shout will miss. Be careful to stay in front of him though, as there is a chance he will run back to his spot, running into the fire shout. **You can also save [[Skyrim:Vilod|Vilod]] in the same manner if you run past Hadvar quickly enough. *After escaping from Helgen, it can be re-entered immediately. If you re-enter the Keep and any Imperial and/or Stormcloak soldiers you didn't kill were left behind, they will still be inside, but they won't be hostile. *When making your way to the keep, the locations to nearby [[Skyrim:Bonechill Passage|Bonechill Passage]], [[Skyrim:Greywater Grotto|Greywater Grotto]], [[Skyrim:Fort Neugrad|Fort Neugrad]], [[Skyrim:Orphan Rock|Orphan Rock]], and [[Skyrim:South Skybound Watch|South Skybound Watch]] will appear on your compass, but you won't be able to discover them yet. *By default you'll start with a carry weight limit of 300. If [[Skyrim:Survival Mode|Survival Mode]] is active, your carry weight limit will be cut in half to 150. *You can kill the Imperial Torturer and his assistant with no consequence, even if you are following Hadvar. *This is the only quest in the game where an [[Skyrim:Imperial Mage|Imperial Mage]] can be seen; [[Skyrim:Cut Content|originally]] they were meant to also appear in the [[Skyrim:Civil War|Civil War]] as troops, but didn't make it to the final version. *Even if you kill the bear with a sneak attack, Hadvar will say "Not the sneaking type, eh?" or Ralof will say "Sneaking is highly overrated, eh?" *If you enter the Keep with Hadvar, the on-screen tutorial message will say "Press activate to open containers." If you enter with Ralof, it will say "Press activate to loot bodies" instead. *Once you make your way out of Helgen, many [[Skyrim:Creation Club Quests|quests]] involving [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creation Club]] content may start immediately, overloading your journal in the process. **The Anniversary update changes this so that the quests start more naturally through gameplay. ==Bugs== {{cleanup|lots of very unlikely bugs here; needs removal of the most ridiculous ones, testing of the believable ones}} {{Bug|You might encounter bugs in the quest script where the game will stop progressing.
